meta.title: Atlas of Fundamental Concepts
meta.description: A source-backed visual atlas connecting the mathematics of physical theories to foundational laws, spacetime, quantum mechanics, QFT, Standard Model fields and interactions, controlled reductions and effective theories, composite hadrons and nuclei, and precision atomic structure.
meta.direction: Fields are stacked vertically. Within a field, smaller level values are more structurally primitive or less composite; larger values generally indicate specialization, composition, effective description, collective organization, or emergence. The order is ontological and structural, not pedagogical difficulty.
meta.scope: Mathematics and a deeply sourced physics atlas from classical and relativistic foundations through quantum mechanics, QFT consistency and symmetry structure, complete Standard Model field and particle content, electroweak and low-energy EFT matching, QCD chiral and nuclear effective layers, and atomic composition, states, spectra, interactions, and precision corrections through atoms and ions.
meta.sourceFormat: Canonical JSON; the build embeds it in the browser bundle and publishes a readable JSON copy.

add-data.label: Add data
add-data.description: Equip an existing carrier or structured object with additional chosen data, when such compatible data exists. Use a construction junction when several independently meaningful inputs must coexist on the same carrier or interact compatibly.

impose-axiom.label: Impose axiom
impose-axiom.description: Keep the existing data and select the subclass satisfying an additional law, existence condition, finiteness condition, or other property.

induced-forgotten.label: Induced / forgotten
induced-forgotten.description: Pass canonically from a stronger object to structure it determines, or forget part of the data while retaining a valid weaker structure. The carrier may change under a canonical induced construction.

canonical-construction.label: Canonical construction
canonical-construction.description: Apply a standard functorial or canonical construction whose output is not merely a reduct of the input and is not generally an equivalent presentation of the same object.

quotient-construction.label: Quotient construction
quotient-construction.description: Identify elements by a stated equivalence relation and equip the quotient with the induced structure. The edge detail must state the representatives and equivalence relation.

canonical-embedding.label: Canonical embedding
canonical-embedding.description: Map one structure injectively into another by the standard structure-preserving inclusion or representation. This records a canonical copy, not necessarily literal set containment.

combine-compatible.label: Combine compatible structures
combine-compatible.description: Feed several structures into a construction junction and impose compatibility between them.

representation-equivalence.label: Representation / equivalence
representation-equivalence.description: Reinterpret an object, pass to an equivalent presentation, or relate canonically corresponding structures; the carrier may change.

theorem-implication.label: Theorem implication
theorem-implication.description: Record a genuine theorem implication that is not part of the target definition; these edges may point toward a weaker structure.

mathematical-formulation.label: Mathematical formulation
mathematical-formulation.description: A mathematical structure supplies part of the formal language or state space used by a physical theory or model. This does not claim that the physical content follows from mathematics alone.

framework-specialization.label: Framework specialization
framework-specialization.description: A more specific theory, model, entity class, or regime is obtained by restricting or extending the scope of a broader framework.

quantization.label: Quantization
quantization.description: A classical system or field theory is used to construct a quantum theory through a stated quantization procedure. Quantization need not be unique and is not guaranteed to preserve every classical structure.

theory-component.label: Theory component
theory-component.description: The source supplies a substantive formal ingredient, dynamical sector, law, field content, or mechanism of the target theoretical framework.

describes-governs.label: Describes / governs
describes-governs.description: A theory, law, or interaction describes the behavior of the target within a stated regime. The edge detail must state important limits or qualifications.

composition.label: Physical constitution / realization
composition.description: The source is a material constituent, structural component, or underlying quantum field whose excitation realizes the target physical system or particle. The edge label and detail must distinguish composition from field excitation; neither implies a simple classical sum of parts.

classification.label: Classification
classification.description: The target is a member or subtype of the broader source class.

state-description.label: State / property description
state-description.description: The target represents a state, property, observable, or state-dependent description associated with the source system or theory.

transformation-process.label: Transformation / process
transformation-process.description: A physical process transforms the source into, or produces, the target under the conditions stated in the edge detail.

mathematical-limit.label: Limit / controlled approximation
mathematical-limit.description: The target is recovered from the source either in a stated mathematical or asymptotic limit, or through a quantitatively controlled approximation with identified small parameters or omitted terms. The edge label and detail must state which case applies and its regime of validity.

effective-theory.label: Effective theory / model
effective-theory.description: The target retains the degrees of freedom and interactions relevant below a stated scale or within a stated regime, while higher-energy or unresolved degrees of freedom from the source are integrated out, coarse-grained, or encoded in effective couplings.

emergence.label: Emergent / collective behavior
emergence.description: The target is a collective, organizational, or scale-dependent phenomenon of the source constituents and interactions; it is not a mere list or classical sum of constituents.

couples-interacts.label: Physical interaction / binding
couples-interacts.description: The source field, particle, charge, current, or interaction couples to, acts on, binds, forms, or stabilizes the target in the stated regime. The edge label and detail must identify the exact coupling, interaction, or binding claim and its qualifications.

model-realization.label: Model / approximation method
model-realization.description: The target is a model, idealization, restricted ansatz, approximation scheme, phenomenological fit, or historical representation used for the source system or theory. It need not have a universal small error parameter and is not thereby a controlled limit or effective theory. The edge label and detail must identify the precise status.

historically-motivated.label: Historically motivated
historically-motivated.description: The source experiment, observation, anomaly, or problem materially motivated the development, revision, or acceptance of the target concept. Historical influence is not logical derivation; the edge detail states the documented role and avoids retrospective origin myths.

experimentally-verified-by.label: Experimentally tested / supported by
experimentally-verified-by.description: The source theory, law, entity, prediction, or structural claim is directly tested, supported, constrained, or established by the target experiment or observation. Experimental support is not final logical proof; the edge detail states exactly what was measured.

nodes.label: Finite set
nodes.summary: A set in bijection with $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ for some natural number $n \in \mathbb{N}$, including $n=0$.

nodes.label: Countable set
nodes.summary: A finite or countably infinite set.
nodes.notes: Convention: “countable” means finite or countably infinite (at most countable). Some authors reserve “countable” for countably infinite sets.

nodes.label: Indexed family
nodes.summary: A collection of objects labelled by elements of an index set.
carriers: ambient class or set of values

nodes.label: Transitive set
nodes.summary: A set whose elements are all subsets of it.

nodes.label: Well-founded relation
nodes.summary: An endorelation for which every nonempty subset has an $R$-minimal element.
axioms: every nonempty subset has an $R$-minimal element
nodes.notes: The formulation by absence of infinite descending sequences is equivalent only under suitable choice/dependent-choice assumptions and convention choices.

nodes.label: Ordinal
nodes.summary: A transitive set well-ordered by membership.
nodes.notes: Equivalently, an ordinal is a transitive set all of whose elements are transitive; the present formulation follows the standard von Neumann definition.

nodes.label: Cardinal
nodes.summary: An initial ordinal used to represent the size of a set.
axioms: not equipotent with any smaller ordinal
nodes.notes: A cardinal is an initial ordinal. In ZF this represents the size of any well-orderable set; assigning a cardinal to every set is equivalent to the well-ordering principle and hence to the axiom of choice.

nodes.label: Empty set
nodes.summary: The unique set $\varnothing$ having no elements.
nodes.notes: The empty set is used as the von Neumann realization of zero, but that identification is a chosen encoding rather than an intrinsic meaning of zero.

nodes.label: Power set
nodes.summary: For a set $X$, the set $\mathcal P(X)$ of all subsets of $X$.
induces: strictly larger cardinality by Cantor’s theorem
nodes.notes: In ZF, the power-set axiom guarantees that $\mathcal P(X)$ is a set.

nodes.label: Cantor’s theorem
nodes.summary: For every set $X$, no function $X\to\mathcal P(X)$ is surjective; hence $|X|<|\mathcal P(X)|$.
axioms: ordinary classical or intuitionistic set theory suffices
induces: an unending hierarchy of larger cardinalities
nodes.notes: The theorem rules out a greatest cardinal and does not depend on the continuum hypothesis.

nodes.label: Finite ordinal
nodes.summary: A von Neumann ordinal $n$ obtained from $0=\varnothing$ by finitely many successor steps, so $n=\{0,1,\ldots,n-1\}$.  For example, $0=\varnothing$, $1=\{0\}$, $2=\{0,1\}$, $3=\{0,1,2\}$, and so on, or in terms of empty sets: $0=\varnothing$, $1=\{\varnothing\}$, $2=\{\varnothing,\{\varnothing\}\}$, $3=\{\varnothing,\{\varnothing\},\{\varnothing,\{\varnothing\}\}\}$, and so on.
nodes.notes: Finite ordinals are canonical representatives of finite order types and finite cardinalities.

nodes.label: Successor ordinal
nodes.summary: An ordinal of the form $\alpha+1=\alpha\cup\{\alpha\}$.

nodes.label: Limit ordinal
nodes.summary: A nonzero ordinal that is not a successor ordinal; equivalently, an ordinal equal to the union of all smaller ordinals.
nodes.notes: $\omega$ is the first limit ordinal.

nodes.label: First infinite ordinal $\omega$
nodes.summary: The least infinite ordinal and the set of all finite von Neumann ordinals.
induces: standard carrier of the natural numbers
first infinite cardinal when viewed by cardinality
nodes.notes: $\omega$ is an ordinal; $\aleph_0$ denotes its role as the least infinite cardinal. In the von Neumann convention they have the same underlying set but different structural roles.

nodes.label: Finite cardinal
nodes.summary: A cardinal represented by a finite ordinal $n$.

nodes.label: Infinite cardinal
nodes.summary: A cardinal that is not finite.
nodes.notes: There is no greatest infinite cardinal, by Cantor’s theorem.

nodes.label: Countable ordinal
nodes.summary: An ordinal whose underlying set is finite or countably infinite.
nodes.notes: The collection of all countable ordinals is itself uncountable and forms $\omega_1$.

nodes.label: Countable infinity $\aleph_0$
nodes.summary: The least infinite cardinal, represented by the initial ordinal $\omega$.
induces: cardinality of $\mathbb N$, $\mathbb Z$, and $\mathbb Q$

nodes.label: Ordinal arithmetic
nodes.summary: Addition, multiplication, and exponentiation of ordinals, defined recursively in the right argument.
nodes.notes: Ordinal addition and multiplication are associative but generally not commutative.

nodes.label: Transfinite recursion
nodes.summary: A method for defining a function on all ordinals by specifying its value from the values at earlier ordinals.

nodes.label: First uncountable ordinal $\omega_1$
nodes.summary: The least uncountable ordinal, equivalently the set of all countable ordinals.
nodes.notes: Its underlying cardinal is $\aleph_1$; the continuum hypothesis asks whether $|\mathbb R|=\aleph_1$.

nodes.label: Successor cardinal
nodes.summary: For a cardinal $\kappa$, the least cardinal $\kappa^+$ strictly greater than $\kappa$.
axioms: $\kappa<\kappa^+$ and no cardinal lies strictly between them
nodes.notes: Cantor’s theorem gives $\kappa^+\le 2^\kappa$, but equality is not provable in ZFC in general.

nodes.label: Limit cardinal
nodes.summary: An infinite cardinal that is not the successor of any cardinal.

nodes.label: Epsilon-zero ordinal $\varepsilon_0$
nodes.summary: The least nonzero fixed point of ordinal exponentiation $\alpha\mapsto\omega^\alpha$.
nodes.notes: $\varepsilon_0$ is countable despite lying far beyond every finite tower formed from $\omega$ by ordinal exponentiation.

nodes.label: Aleph hierarchy
nodes.summary: The transfinite enumeration $\aleph_\alpha$ of the infinite initial ordinals.
nodes.notes: In ZF, alephs enumerate the well-orderable infinite cardinalities; Choice says every set is well-orderable and hence has an aleph cardinality.

nodes.label: Beth hierarchy
nodes.summary: In ZFC, the cardinal hierarchy generated from $\beth_0=\aleph_0$ by repeated power sets and suprema at limit stages.
nodes.notes: Without Choice, a power set of a well-orderable set need not be well-orderable; the displayed initial-ordinal beth hierarchy therefore uses the ZFC setting selected later in the story.

nodes.label: Class of all ordinals $\mathrm{Ord}$
nodes.summary: The collection of every ordinal, ordered by membership.
nodes.notes: If $\mathrm{Ord}$ were a set, it would itself determine an ordinal larger than every ordinal, giving the Burali–Forti contradiction.

nodes.label: Cardinality of the continuum $\mathfrak c$
nodes.summary: The size of the real line, denoted $\mathfrak c$; in ZFC it is the cardinal $|\mathbb R|=2^{\aleph_0}$.
carriers: equipotence type of $\mathbb R$; an initial ordinal under Choice
induces: size of $\mathcal P(\mathbb N)$ and of the real line
nodes.notes: In bare ZF, $\mathbb R$ need not be well-orderable, so its size need not have an initial-ordinal representative. The equality with $|\mathcal P(\mathbb N)|$ is equipotence, not literal identity.

nodes.label: Continuum hypothesis
nodes.summary: The assertion $2^{\aleph_0}=\aleph_1$, equivalently that no cardinal lies strictly between $\aleph_0$ and $\mathfrak c$.
nodes.notes: Gödel and Cohen showed that CH can neither be disproved nor proved from ZFC, assuming ZFC is consistent.

nodes.label: Generalized continuum hypothesis
nodes.summary: The assertion $2^\kappa=\kappa^+$ for every infinite cardinal $\kappa$.
nodes.notes: GCH implies CH and is independent of ZFC, relative to the consistency of ZFC.

nodes.label: Large cardinal
nodes.summary: A cardinal satisfying one of several strong closure, compactness, measure, or elementary-embedding properties used to calibrate set-theoretic strength.
nodes.notes: ZFC does not prove that inaccessible, measurable, or supercompact cardinals exist, assuming the usual consistency hypotheses; their existence is adopted through additional axioms.

nodes.label: Strongly inaccessible cardinal
nodes.summary: An uncountable regular strong-limit cardinal.
induces: a transitive set $V_\kappa$ modeling a substantial fragment of ZFC
nodes.notes: The existence of an inaccessible cardinal is not provable in ZFC if ZFC is consistent.

nodes.label: Measurable cardinal
nodes.summary: An uncountable cardinal $\kappa$ carrying a nonprincipal $\kappa$-complete ultrafilter.
induces: elementary embedding of the universe into an inner model
nodes.notes: Every measurable cardinal is strongly inaccessible in ZFC.

nodes.label: Supercompact cardinal
nodes.summary: A cardinal $\kappa$ whose elementary-embedding or fine-measure properties witness compactness at every scale $\lambda\ge\kappa$.
data: fine normal $\kappa$-complete measures on $\mathcal P_\kappa(\lambda)$ for all $\lambda\ge\kappa$
induces: very strong compactness and reflection principles
nodes.notes: Every supercompact cardinal is measurable. Measurability alone does not imply supercompactness.

nodes.label: Binary relation
nodes.summary: A relation from one set to another, represented by a subset of their Cartesian product.
nodes.notes: Order, equivalence, accessibility, and well-foundedness use the endorelation specialization $X=Y$.

nodes.label: Equivalence relation
nodes.summary: A relation that partitions a set into equivalence classes.

nodes.label: Preorder
nodes.summary: A reflexive and transitive binary relation.

nodes.label: Partial order / poset
nodes.summary: A preorder in which mutual comparability forces equality.

nodes.label: Bounded poset
nodes.summary: A poset with a least element and a greatest element.
nodes.notes: Least and greatest elements, when they exist, are unique; boundedness is an existence property.

nodes.label: Directed set
nodes.summary: A nonempty preorder in which every pair has a common upper bound.
axioms: for any x,y there is z with $x\le z$ and $y\le z$

nodes.label: Join-semilattice
nodes.summary: A poset in which every pair has a least upper bound.
data: partial order; equivalently, a binary join operation

nodes.label: Meet-semilattice
nodes.summary: A poset in which every pair has a greatest lower bound.
data: partial order; equivalently, a binary meet operation

nodes.label: Total order
nodes.summary: A partial order in which every pair is comparable.

nodes.label: group + total order
nodes.summary: Put a compatible total order on a group.
nodes.notes: Construction junction: it is a visual device, not a separate standard mathematical structure.

combination.compatibility: The order is invariant under translation by group elements.

nodes.label: meet + join
nodes.summary: Combine compatible meet- and join-semilattice structure on one order.
nodes.notes: Construction junction: it is a visual device, not a separate standard mathematical structure.

combination.compatibility: The meet and join are computed with respect to the same partial order.

nodes.label: Well-order
nodes.summary: A total order in which every nonempty subset has a least element.

nodes.label: Directed-complete partial order
nodes.summary: A poset in which every directed subset has a supremum.
axioms: every directed subset has a least upper bound

nodes.label: Lattice
nodes.summary: A poset in which every pair has both a meet and a join.
data: partial order; binary meet and join
axioms: meet and join are the greatest lower and least upper bounds

nodes.label: Totally ordered group
nodes.summary: A group equipped with a translation-invariant total order.
axioms: $a\le b$ implies $xay\le xby$ for all x,y (equivalently, left and right translations preserve order)
nodes.notes: “Ordered group” can mean a partially ordered group in some literature. This node specifically means a totally ordered group.

nodes.label: Bounded lattice
nodes.summary: A lattice with a least and a greatest element.

nodes.label: Distributive lattice
nodes.summary: A lattice whose meet and join distribute over one another.

nodes.label: group + lattice order
nodes.summary: Compatibility construction producing Lattice-ordered group.
nodes.notes: All incoming branches are jointly required.

combination.compatibility: Require left and right translations to preserve the lattice order.

nodes.label: lattice + monoid with residuals
nodes.summary: Compatibility construction producing Residuated lattice.
nodes.notes: All incoming branches are jointly required.

combination.compatibility: Require monoid multiplication to be monotone and admit left and right residuals with respect to the order.

nodes.label: Pointed CPO
nodes.summary: A directed-complete partial order with a least element.
nodes.notes: Terminology varies: some authors use CPO for a dcpo without requiring a least element; this atlas uses “pointed CPO”. The least element is unique if it exists.

nodes.label: bounded + distributive
nodes.summary: Combine bounds with distributive lattice laws.
nodes.notes: Construction junction: it is a visual device, not a separate standard mathematical structure.

combination.compatibility: The bounds, meet, and join belong to the same lattice structure.

nodes.label: Complete lattice
nodes.summary: A poset in which every subset has both a supremum and an infimum.

nodes.label: Lattice-ordered group
nodes.summary: A group with a lattice order invariant under translations.
nodes.notes: Every totally ordered group is lattice-ordered, but not conversely.

nodes.label: Residuated lattice
nodes.summary: A lattice-ordered monoid whose multiplication has residuals.

nodes.label: ring + total order
nodes.summary: Put a compatible total order on a ring.
nodes.notes: Construction junction: it is a visual device, not a separate standard mathematical structure.

combination.compatibility: Addition preserves order and products of nonnegative elements are nonnegative.

nodes.label: Bounded distributive lattice
nodes.summary: A distributive lattice equipped with bottom and top.

nodes.label: Frame / complete Heyting algebra
nodes.summary: A complete lattice in which finite meets distribute over arbitrary joins.

nodes.label: Ordered ring
nodes.summary: A ring whose total order is compatible with addition and multiplication.

nodes.label: Boolean algebra
nodes.summary: A bounded distributive lattice in which every element has a complement.

nodes.label: Heyting algebra
nodes.summary: A bounded lattice with an implication operation right-adjoint to meet.

nodes.label: Complete Boolean algebra
nodes.summary: A Boolean algebra that is complete as a lattice.

nodes.label: field + total order
nodes.summary: Put a compatible total order on a field.
nodes.notes: Construction junction: it is a visual device, not a separate standard mathematical structure.

combination.compatibility: The field operations preserve the ordered-ring laws.

nodes.label: Ordered field
nodes.summary: A field equipped with an order making it an ordered ring.

nodes.label: First-order signature
nodes.summary: A vocabulary of function, relation, and constant symbols together with their arities.

nodes.label: First-order theory
nodes.summary: A set of first-order sentences in a fixed signature.
nodes.notes: A theory need not be deductively closed unless that convention is stated explicitly.

nodes.label: Modal Kripke model
nodes.summary: A binary-relation frame together with a valuation of propositional variables at worlds.
nodes.notes: The recursive forcing clauses define the semantics; they are not an additional frame axiom. Frame conditions such as reflexivity or transitivity correspond to particular modal logics.

nodes.label: signature + carrier
nodes.summary: Interpret a first-order signature on a nonempty carrier set.
nodes.notes: Construction junction: it is a visual device, not a separate standard mathematical structure.

combination.compatibility: Each symbol is assigned an operation, relation, or distinguished element of the specified arity on the carrier.

nodes.label: First-order structure
nodes.summary: A nonempty carrier together with interpretations of every symbol in a first-order signature.
data: interpretations of constants, functions, and relations
nodes.notes: The signature and carrier are separate inputs; interpretations are additional data on that pair.

nodes.label: Propositional intuitionistic Kripke model
nodes.summary: A preorder of information states with a persistent valuation of propositional atoms.
axioms: truth persists upward along the preorder
nodes.notes: The displayed data define the propositional semantics. First-order intuitionistic Kripke models additionally require domains and interpretations varying monotonically with worlds.

nodes.label: theory + structure satisfying it
nodes.summary: Combine a first-order theory with a structure in the same signature and impose satisfaction.
nodes.notes: All incoming branches are jointly required.

combination.compatibility: The theory and structure use the same signature L, and the structure satisfies every sentence in T.

nodes.label: Model of a theory
nodes.summary: A first-order structure satisfying every sentence of a specified theory.
carriers: first-order theory T in signature L
axioms: M satisfies every sentence of T
nodes.notes: The theory and structure are independent inputs that must use the same signature.

nodes.label: Normal modal algebra
nodes.summary: A Boolean algebra with a normal modal necessity operator.
nodes.notes: Equivalently, the dual possibility operator preserves 0 and finite joins. Additional modal logics impose further equations.

nodes.label: Category
nodes.summary: A collection of objects and morphisms with identities and associative composition; size is controlled by an ambient set-theoretic convention.
nodes.notes: “Category” does not by itself mean small. A separate Small category node records the set-sized case.

nodes.label: Cartesian category
nodes.summary: A category with chosen finite products.

nodes.label: Finitely complete category
nodes.summary: A category admitting all finite limits.
axioms: every finite diagram has a limit

nodes.label: Groupoid
nodes.summary: A category in which every morphism is invertible.

nodes.label: Monoidal category
nodes.summary: A category with a tensor product, unit object, and coherent associativity and unit isomorphisms.

nodes.label: Preadditive category
nodes.summary: A category whose hom-sets are abelian groups and whose composition is bilinear.

nodes.label: Small category
nodes.summary: A category whose objects and morphisms form sets.
nodes.notes: Smallness is relative to the ambient universe or foundational convention.

nodes.label: Thin category
nodes.summary: A category with at most one morphism between any ordered pair of objects.
axioms: each hom-set has at most one element

nodes.label: Additive category
nodes.summary: A preadditive category with finite biproducts.

nodes.label: Braided monoidal category
nodes.summary: A monoidal category with a coherent braiding exchanging tensor factors.

nodes.label: Cartesian closed category
nodes.summary: A cartesian category in which product with each object has a right adjoint.

nodes.label: category + cosimplicial diagram data
nodes.summary: Combine an ambient category with a degree-indexed family and compatible coface/codegeneracy morphisms.
nodes.notes: All incoming branches are jointly required.

combination.compatibility: Every $X^{n}$ is an object of the same category C; add coface and codegeneracy morphisms in C satisfying the cosimplicial identities.

nodes.label: category + simplicial diagram data
nodes.summary: Combine an ambient category with a degree-indexed family and compatible face/degeneracy morphisms.
nodes.notes: All incoming branches are jointly required.

combination.compatibility: Every $X_{n}$ is an object of the same category C; add face and degeneracy morphisms in C satisfying the simplicial identities.

nodes.label: Dagger category
nodes.summary: A category with an identity-on-objects involutive contravariant endofunctor.

nodes.label: objects + monoidal base
nodes.summary: Supply an object collection and a monoidal category in which hom-objects, composition, and units will live.
nodes.notes: Construction junction: an enriched category is not generally an ordinary category with extra data.

combination.compatibility: Choose a hom-object in the monoidal base for each ordered object pair, together with enriched composition and units satisfying enriched associativity and unit laws.

nodes.label: Presheaf
nodes.summary: A Set-valued contravariant functor on a small category.
nodes.notes: This atlas uses the standard Set-valued meaning so that the sheaf and sheaf-of-algebraic-objects branches are type-correct. Functors $C^{\mathrm{op}}\to D$ for general D are D-valued presheaves.

nodes.label: Site
nodes.summary: A category equipped with a Grothendieck topology or a pretopology of covering families.
nodes.notes: This atlas uses sites small relative to the ambient universe. Large-site conventions require explicit universe management.

nodes.label: Abelian category
nodes.summary: An additive category with kernels and cokernels in which monomorphisms and epimorphisms are normal.

nodes.label: Closed monoidal category
nodes.summary: A monoidal category in which tensoring has internal-hom right adjoints.

nodes.label: Cosimplicial object
nodes.summary: A covariant functor from the simplex category Δ to a category.
nodes.notes: Equivalently, a functor $\Delta\to C$. The ambient category is part of the specification.

nodes.label: Enriched category
nodes.summary: A collection of objects whose homs are objects of a monoidal category, with enriched composition and units.
nodes.notes: An underlying ordinary category exists only when the enriching base supplies an appropriate way to extract hom-sets.

nodes.label: finite limits + exponentials
nodes.summary: Combine finite-limit and cartesian-closed structure, then add a subobject classifier.
nodes.notes: Construction junction: it is a visual device, not a separate standard mathematical structure.

combination.compatibility: The finite products used by the closed structure agree with those from finite limits; a subobject classifier is also supplied.

nodes.label: Simplicial object
nodes.summary: A contravariant functor from the simplex category Δ to a category.
nodes.notes: Equivalently, a functor $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to C$. The ambient category is part of the specification.

nodes.label: Symmetric monoidal category
nodes.summary: A braided monoidal category whose braiding is its own inverse.

nodes.label: Elementary topos
nodes.summary: A finitely complete cartesian closed category with a subobject classifier.

nodes.label: Compact closed category
nodes.summary: A symmetric monoidal category in which every object is equipped with a dual and evaluation/coevaluation satisfying the snake identities.
nodes.notes: Compact closure canonically determines duals and internal homs; for example, $[A,B]=A^*\otimes B$.

nodes.label: Grothendieck topos
nodes.summary: A category equivalent to the category of sheaves on a site.
axioms: E is equivalent to Sh(C,J) for some small site (C,J)
nodes.notes: A site presents a Grothendieck topos, but is not itself the carrier of the topos; different sites can present equivalent topoi.

nodes.label: Quiver / directed multigraph
nodes.summary: A vertex set and an arrow set equipped with source and target maps; loops and parallel arrows are allowed.
nodes.notes: This is a quiver (also called a directed multigraph), not the simple-digraph convention in which an edge is merely an ordered pair of vertices.

nodes.label: Undirected multigraph
nodes.summary: An undirected incidence graph with a vertex set and an edge set; loops and parallel edges are allowed.
data: endpoint map assigning to each edge a one- or two-element multiset of vertices
nodes.notes: This atlas uses a broad incidence/multigraph convention. A simple graph is the loopless, no-parallel-edge specialization.

nodes.label: Directed acyclic graph
nodes.summary: A directed graph with no directed cycle.

nodes.label: Hypergraph
nodes.summary: A vertex set together with a family of arbitrary vertex subsets called hyperedges.

nodes.label: Simple graph
nodes.summary: An undirected graph with no loops or parallel edges.

nodes.label: Abstract simplicial complex
nodes.summary: A family of finite vertex subsets closed under taking subsets.

nodes.label: Bipartite graph
nodes.summary: An undirected graph whose vertex set admits a partition into two parts such that every edge joins different parts.
axioms: there exists a bipartition $V=A\sqcup B$ with every edge crossing between A and B
nodes.notes: The bipartition is treated as an existence property, not as chosen coloring data.

nodes.label: Forest
nodes.summary: An undirected graph with no cycles.

nodes.label: Matroid
nodes.summary: A ground set with a family of independent subsets satisfying the matroid independence axioms.
axioms: for infinite matroids, the maximal-extension axiom (IM)
nodes.notes: For finite ground sets the usual hereditary and augmentation axioms suffice; infinite matroids require an additional maximality condition.

nodes.label: Planar graph
nodes.summary: A graph admitting an embedding in the plane without edge crossings.

nodes.label: Tournament
nodes.summary: An orientation of a complete simple graph.
data: for each distinct pair, exactly one directed edge
nodes.notes: Finite tournaments are most common in elementary graph theory, but the definition extends to infinite vertex sets.

nodes.label: Weighted graph
nodes.summary: A graph equipped with numerical or algebraic weights on edges or vertices.

nodes.label: Oriented matroid
nodes.summary: A matroid enriched with orientation data abstracting signs of vector configurations.
nodes.notes: The standard finite oriented-matroid theory is intended here; infinite oriented matroids require additional axiomatic care.

nodes.label: Tree
nodes.summary: A connected acyclic undirected graph.

nodes.label: Algebraic signature
nodes.summary: A signature containing operation symbols with specified arities and no relation symbols.

nodes.label: Quasigroup
nodes.summary: A magma in which left and right division equations have unique solutions.
axioms: left and right translations are bijections

nodes.label: signature + carrier operations
nodes.summary: Interpret an algebraic signature by operations on one carrier set.
nodes.notes: Construction junction: the signature and carrier are jointly required.

combination.compatibility: Use a nonempty carrier A and, for each n-ary operation symbol, choose an operation $A^{n}\to A$.

nodes.label: Algebra for a finitary signature (Ω-algebra)
nodes.summary: A nonempty set interpreting each operation symbol of a fixed finitary algebraic signature.
data: an operation $A^{n}\to A$ for each n-ary symbol
nodes.notes: “Universal algebra” is the subject; an individual object is an algebra for a signature, often called an $\Omega$-algebra. This atlas adopts the common nonempty-carrier convention.

nodes.label: Loop
nodes.summary: A quasigroup with a two-sided identity element.
nodes.notes: A two-sided identity in a quasigroup, if it exists, is unique.

nodes.label: Rack
nodes.summary: A set with a self-distributive operation whose right translations are bijective.

nodes.label: Quandle
nodes.summary: An idempotent rack, important in knot invariants.

nodes.label: Magma
nodes.summary: A set with a closed binary operation.

nodes.label: Semigroup
nodes.summary: An associative magma.

nodes.label: Monoid
nodes.summary: A semigroup with an identity element.
nodes.notes: The identity, if it exists in a semigroup, is unique; monoidhood is therefore an existence property rather than freely chosen additional data.

nodes.label: Commutative monoid
nodes.summary: A monoid whose operation is commutative.

nodes.label: Group
nodes.summary: A monoid in which every element has an inverse.

nodes.label: Abelian group
nodes.summary: A group with commutative multiplication, usually written additively.

nodes.label: two compatible monoids
nodes.summary: Use one commutative monoid as addition and another monoid as multiplication on the same carrier.
nodes.notes: Construction junction: it is a visual device, not a separate standard mathematical structure.

combination.compatibility: The two operations share a carrier; multiplication distributes over addition, and zero is absorbing.

nodes.label: Semiring
nodes.summary: A ring-like structure without requiring additive inverses.
nodes.notes: Convention: semirings here are unital and have an absorbing zero. Some literature drops one or both requirements.

nodes.label: Ring
nodes.summary: A unital semiring whose additive commutative monoid is an abelian group.
nodes.notes: This atlas uses the convention that rings have a multiplicative identity and ring homomorphisms preserve it.

nodes.label: Commutative ring
nodes.summary: A ring with commutative multiplication.

nodes.label: Division ring
nodes.summary: A nonzero ring in which every nonzero element is multiplicatively invertible.
axioms: each nonzero element has a multiplicative inverse

nodes.label: ring action on an abelian group
nodes.summary: Combine a scalar ring with an additive abelian group.
nodes.notes: Construction junction: it is a visual device, not a separate standard mathematical structure.

combination.compatibility: Add scalar multiplication $R \times M \to M$ satisfying distributivity, associativity of scalar action, and the unit law.

nodes.label: Module over a ring
nodes.summary: An abelian group acted on linearly by a ring.
nodes.notes: Convention: modules are left modules unless explicitly stated otherwise. Right modules reverse the scalar-action convention.

nodes.label: Field
nodes.summary: A commutative ring in which every nonzero element has a multiplicative inverse.
axioms: every nonzero element has a multiplicative inverse
nodes.notes: The inverse of each nonzero element is unique. The convention excludes the zero ring.

nodes.label: Affine space
nodes.summary: A set with a free transitive action of a vector space, retaining displacement vectors without a preferred origin.
axioms: for every $a,b\in A$ there is a unique $v\in V$ with $a+v=b$
nodes.notes: No origin is distinguished; choosing one identifies $A$ noncanonically with $V$.

nodes.label: Algebraically closed field
nodes.summary: A field in which every nonconstant polynomial has a root.

nodes.label: field action on an abelian group
nodes.summary: Specialize scalar multiplication to scalars from a field.
nodes.notes: Construction junction: it is a visual device, not a separate standard mathematical structure.

combination.compatibility: Add $F \times V \to V$ satisfying the vector-space axioms.

nodes.label: Perfect field
nodes.summary: A field whose algebraic extensions are separable.

nodes.label: Vector space
nodes.summary: An abelian group with scalar multiplication by a field.

nodes.label: Complex vector space
nodes.summary: A vector space whose scalar field is $\mathbb C$.

nodes.label: Dual vector space
nodes.summary: The vector space of linear functionals from a vector space to its scalar field.
nodes.notes: For infinite-dimensional topological vector spaces, the continuous dual depends on the topology and can differ from the algebraic dual.

nodes.label: Lie algebra
nodes.summary: A vector space with an alternating bilinear bracket satisfying the Jacobi identity.
nodes.notes: The alternating axiom implies antisymmetry over every field. The converse needs characteristic different from 2, so antisymmetry is not used as an unrestricted substitute.

nodes.label: Symplectic vector space
nodes.summary: A vector space with a nondegenerate alternating bilinear form.
nodes.notes: Finite-dimensional symplectic vector spaces have even dimension.

nodes.label: Algebra over a field
nodes.summary: A vector space equipped with a bilinear multiplication, not necessarily associative or unital.
nodes.notes: Associativity, a multiplicative identity, commutativity, Lie identities, and similar laws define more specialized kinds of algebra.

nodes.label: Associative algebra
nodes.summary: An algebra over a commutative base ring or field whose multiplication is associative.

nodes.label: Tensor-product vector space
nodes.summary: A vector space $V\otimes W$ representing bilinear maps out of $V\times W$ by linear maps.
nodes.notes: The construction is canonical up to unique isomorphism, not equality of a particular concrete realization.

nodes.label: Coalgebra
nodes.summary: Over a fixed commutative base ring k, a k-module with coassociative comultiplication and counit.

nodes.label: Exterior algebra
nodes.summary: The graded algebra $\Lambda V$ generated by a vector space $V$ subject to the alternating relations $v\wedge v=0$.
axioms: universal property for alternating algebra maps
nodes.notes: In characteristic not equal to 2, the alternating relation implies graded anticommutativity for degree-one generators; the alternating formulation is characteristic-independent.

nodes.label: Unital associative algebra
nodes.summary: An associative algebra with a multiplicative identity compatible with the base scalar action.
nodes.notes: A multiplicative identity, if it exists, is unique; unitality is an existence condition on the associative multiplication.

nodes.label: *-algebra
nodes.summary: A complex associative algebra equipped with a conjugate-linear involutive anti-automorphism.
nodes.notes: The scalar involution here is complex conjugation.

nodes.label: algebra + coalgebra compatibility
nodes.summary: Compatibility construction producing Bialgebra.
nodes.notes: All incoming branches are jointly required.

combination.compatibility: Use the same module or vector space and require comultiplication and counit to be algebra homomorphisms (equivalently multiplication and unit are coalgebra homomorphisms).

nodes.label: Clifford algebra
nodes.summary: An associative algebra generated by a quadratic space with $v^2=Q(v)1$.
nodes.notes: Sign conventions for $Q$ and the Clifford relation vary across mathematics and physics.

nodes.label: Commutative unital algebra over a field
nodes.summary: A unital associative algebra over a fixed field whose multiplication is commutative.
nodes.notes: “Commutative algebra” also names the subject. This node denotes an individual commutative unital algebra over the scalar field inherited from the algebra branch.

nodes.label: Grassmann algebra
nodes.summary: The exterior algebra of a vector space, especially when its generators are interpreted as anticommuting Grassmann variables.
data: exterior algebra $\Lambda V$ viewed with Grassmann generators
nodes.notes: This is the exterior algebra under terminology common in physics; it is not a second distinct algebraic construction.

nodes.label: Bialgebra
nodes.summary: Over a fixed commutative base ring, a compatible unital associative algebra and counital coassociative coalgebra.
axioms: comultiplication and counit are algebra maps
nodes.notes: Compatibility may equivalently be stated by requiring multiplication and unit to be coalgebra maps, or comultiplication and counit to be algebra maps.

nodes.label: Gamma matrices
nodes.summary: Matrices or endomorphisms satisfying the Clifford relation $\{\gamma^\mu,\gamma^\nu\}=2g^{\mu\nu}I$, used to realize spinor representations.
induces: representation of the relevant Clifford algebra
Dirac operator after coupling to derivatives
nodes.notes: Matrix size, reality conditions, and sign conventions depend on dimension, signature, and representation.

nodes.label: Hopf algebra
nodes.summary: A bialgebra equipped with an antipode.
nodes.notes: For a fixed bialgebra structure, an antipode is unique if it exists; Hopf algebra status is therefore an existence property, not a free choice of extra map.

nodes.label: Slater determinant
nodes.summary: The determinant or exterior product of one-particle spin-orbitals representing a single antisymmetric fermion configuration.
axioms: changes sign under odd particle permutations
induces: one-body density matrix for the determinant
nodes.notes: A single Slater determinant captures antisymmetry and exchange but not general many-body correlation.

nodes.label: group + carrier action
nodes.summary: Compatibility construction producing Group action.
nodes.notes: All incoming branches are jointly required.

combination.compatibility: Use the group multiplication to act associatively on the set and let the group identity act trivially.

nodes.label: Group action
nodes.summary: An action of a group on an object, here initially a set, respecting multiplication and identity.

nodes.label: G-set
nodes.summary: A set equipped with an action of a specified group G.

nodes.label: Circle group $U(1)$
nodes.summary: The one-dimensional compact Lie group of complex numbers of unit modulus.
nodes.notes: Isomorphic to $\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$ and to $SO(2)$.

nodes.label: Lorentz group
nodes.summary: The group preserving a nondegenerate quadratic form of Lorentzian signature.
carriers: real vector space with Lorentzian quadratic form
induces: proper, orthochronous, and other connected components
nodes.notes: “Lorentz group” may denote the full group $O(1,3)$ or a specified subgroup such as $SO^+(1,3)$.

nodes.label: Poincaré group
nodes.summary: The semidirect product of spacetime translations with the Lorentz group.
induces: energy–momentum and spin classification of stable particles via unitary irreducible representations
nodes.notes: The connected, universal-cover, and full disconnected versions must be distinguished in representation theory.

nodes.label: Special unitary group
nodes.summary: The compact Lie group $SU(n)$ of unitary matrices with determinant one.

nodes.label: Spin group
nodes.summary: The group constructed in a Clifford algebra that double-covers $SO(n)$ in Euclidean signature; in indefinite signature it covers the appropriate identity component according to convention.
data: specified subgroup of invertible even Clifford elements
induces: covering homomorphism to an orthogonal group or its identity component
nodes.notes: The precise target and notation depend on signature and convention; in Euclidean signature $\mathrm{Spin}(n)$ double-covers $SO(n)$.

nodes.label: group + vector space action
nodes.summary: Compatibility construction producing Linear representation of a group.
nodes.notes: All incoming branches are jointly required.

combination.compatibility: Require the group action maps to be invertible linear transformations.

nodes.label: Lie algebra + vector space action
nodes.summary: Compatibility construction producing Representation of a Lie algebra.
nodes.notes: All incoming branches are jointly required.

combination.compatibility: The Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ and vector space V are over the same field k, and the k-linear action sends [x,y] to the commutator of the corresponding endomorphisms.

nodes.label: Linear representation of a group
nodes.summary: A group action on a vector space by invertible linear maps.

nodes.label: Irreducible representation
nodes.summary: A nonzero representation with no proper nonzero invariant subspace.
axioms: no invariant subspaces other than $0$ and $V$
nodes.notes: Irreducibility depends on the base field and the category of representations being used.

nodes.label: Representation of a Lie algebra
nodes.summary: A Lie algebra homomorphism into the endomorphism Lie algebra of a vector space.
carriers: Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ over a field k

nodes.label: Spinor representation
nodes.summary: A representation of a spin group that does not generally descend to the corresponding orthogonal group.
axioms: Clifford/spin relations appropriate to dimension and signature
induces: spinor fields after forming associated bundles
nodes.notes: Real, complex, Weyl, Majorana, and Dirac spinors exist under different dimensional and signature conditions.

nodes.label: Unitary representation
nodes.summary: A group representation by unitary operators on a Hilbert space.
axioms: usually an explicit continuity condition for topological groups
induces: self-adjoint generators for strongly continuous one-parameter subgroups
nodes.notes: For topological groups, continuity is part of the standard analytic notion.

nodes.label: Clebsch–Gordan coefficient
nodes.summary: A coefficient transforming between uncoupled and coupled bases in a tensor product of angular-momentum representations.
nodes.notes: The coefficients depend on basis and phase conventions; the decomposition multiplicities do not.

nodes.label: Set
nodes.summary: A collection regarded as a single mathematical object.

nodes.label: Pointed set
nodes.summary: A set with one distinguished element.

nodes.label: Function
nodes.summary: A total single-valued relation from a domain set to a codomain set.
axioms: for every $x\in X$ there exists exactly one $y\in Y$ with $x \mathrel{f} y$

nodes.label: Successor structure
nodes.summary: A set equipped with a distinguished zero and a unary successor operation.
nodes.notes: The second-order Peano axioms are categorical under full second-order semantics. First-order Peano arithmetic is not categorical by the compactness and Löwenheim–Skolem theorems.

nodes.label: Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory (ZF)
nodes.summary: The standard first-order set theory with extensionality, foundation, pairing, union, power set, infinity, and the separation and replacement schemas, but without the axiom of choice.
data: axioms and axiom schemas of ZF
induces: formal universe in which the set-theoretic constructions are carried out
nodes.notes: Equivalent presentations may trade some axioms for theorems; the defining editorial distinction here is that ZF omits Choice.

nodes.label: Axiom of choice (AC)
nodes.summary: The assertion that every set-indexed family of nonempty sets has a choice function.
data: choice function selecting one element from each member of a family
induces: well-ordering theorem and Zorn’s lemma over ZF
nodes.notes: AC is independent of ZF, assuming ZF is consistent. Its standard equivalents are equivalent over ZF, not in arbitrary weak background theories.

nodes.label: Well-ordering theorem
nodes.summary: Every set can be well-ordered.
induces: a cardinal representative for every set
nodes.notes: Over ZF, the well-ordering theorem is equivalent to the axiom of choice.

nodes.label: Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory with Choice (ZFC)
nodes.summary: ZF augmented by the axiom of choice.
data: all axioms and schemas of ZF
induces: the conventional classical foundational setting for much of mathematics
nodes.notes: CH, GCH, and the existence of inaccessible, measurable, or supercompact cardinals are not theorems of ZFC, under the corresponding consistency assumptions.

nodes.label: Von Neumann zero $0$
nodes.summary: The chosen realization $0:=\varnothing$.
induces: first finite ordinal and finite cardinal
nodes.notes: This is the standard von Neumann encoding; abstract zero is not intrinsically identical with the empty set.

nodes.label: Von Neumann successor
nodes.summary: The operation $S(x)=x\cup\{x\}$; on ordinals it produces the least larger ordinal.

nodes.label: Von Neumann one $1$
nodes.summary: The set $1:=S(0)=\{0\}=\{\varnothing\}$.

nodes.label: Peano system
nodes.summary: A set with zero and successor satisfying the second-order Peano axioms.

nodes.label: Natural numbers $\mathbb N$
nodes.summary: The standard Peano system, realized here on the carrier $\omega$ with zero, successor, addition, multiplication, and order.
nodes.notes: The atlas distinguishes the abstract Peano structure from its selected von Neumann carrier $\omega$.

nodes.label: Difference pairs of natural numbers
nodes.summary: Pairs $(a,b)\in\mathbb N^2$ representing formal differences $a-b$.
nodes.notes: This is the Grothendieck group completion of the additive commutative monoid $\mathbb N$.

nodes.label: Integers $\mathbb Z$
nodes.summary: The ordered commutative ring obtained from formal differences of natural numbers.
nodes.notes: The map $n\mapsto[(n,0)]$ canonically embeds $\mathbb N$ into $\mathbb Z$; it need not be literal subset inclusion in the quotient realization.

nodes.label: Integer fraction pairs
nodes.summary: Pairs $(a,b)\in\mathbb Z\times(\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\})$ representing fractions $a/b$.

nodes.label: Rational numbers $\mathbb Q$
nodes.summary: The ordered field of fractions of $\mathbb Z$.
induces: countable dense linear order without endpoints
nodes.notes: The map $z\mapsto[(z,1)]$ canonically embeds $\mathbb Z$ into $\mathbb Q$.

nodes.label: Integral domain
nodes.summary: A nonzero commutative ring with no zero divisors.

nodes.label: Dedekind domain
nodes.summary: A Noetherian, integrally closed integral domain of Krull dimension one.
nodes.notes: This atlas uses the dimension-one convention, excluding fields; some references allow dimension at most one and hence include fields.

nodes.label: GCD domain
nodes.summary: An integral domain in which any two nonzero elements have a greatest common divisor.
axioms: greatest common divisors exist up to units

nodes.label: Valuation ring
nodes.summary: An integral domain whose ideals are totally ordered by inclusion, equivalently a valuation subring of its fraction field.
axioms: for every fraction x, x or $x^{-1}$ lies in V

nodes.label: Finite field
nodes.summary: A field with finitely many elements.

nodes.label: Number field
nodes.summary: A finite field extension of the rational numbers.
axioms: K is finite-dimensional as a vector space over $\mathbb{Q}$

nodes.label: Unique factorization domain
nodes.summary: An integral domain in which nonzero nonunits factor uniquely into irreducibles up to units and order.
axioms: existence and uniqueness of irreducible factorization

nodes.label: Valued field
nodes.summary: A field equipped with a Krull valuation or an absolute value.
data: valuation into an ordered value group or absolute value
axioms: multiplicativity and ultrametric/triangle inequality in the chosen formulation
nodes.notes: A general Krull valuation takes values in an ordered abelian group and canonically induces a topology/uniformity. A real-valued metric is available for absolute values and rank-one valuations, not for every value group without additional choices.

nodes.label: Global field
nodes.summary: A finite extension of $\mathbb Q$, or a finite extension of the one-variable rational function field $\mathbb F_q(t)$.
axioms: number field or global function field

nodes.label: Principal ideal domain
nodes.summary: An integral domain in which every ideal is generated by one element.

nodes.label: Real closed field
nodes.summary: An ordered field with no proper algebraic ordered extension, equivalently whose algebraic closure is obtained by adjoining $\sqrt{-1}$.
nodes.notes: A real-closed field has a unique compatible ordering: its positive elements are exactly the nonzero squares.

nodes.label: Ring of integers
nodes.summary: The integral closure of $\mathbb{Z}$ inside a number field.
carriers: subset $O_K$ of a number field K
axioms: elements satisfy a monic polynomial over $\mathbb{Z}$
nodes.notes: For a number field K, $O_K$ is the integral closure of $\mathbb{Z}$ in K and is a Dedekind domain.

nodes.label: Complete valued field
nodes.summary: A field complete for the uniformity induced by its valuation; in the absolute-value/rank-one case, complete for the associated metric.
axioms: Cauchy completeness for the valuation uniformity
nodes.notes: The metric wording is restricted to absolute values or rank-one valuations. General valued fields are naturally uniform spaces.

nodes.label: Discrete valuation ring
nodes.summary: A nonfield local principal ideal domain, equivalently a Noetherian local domain of Krull dimension one whose maximal ideal is principal.
axioms: unique nonzero prime ideal (the maximal ideal)
induces: a normalized discrete valuation on its fraction field
nodes.notes: The explicit nonfield condition avoids collapsing the notion to a field under conventions that allow fields as PIDs.

nodes.label: Euclidean domain
nodes.summary: An integral domain that admits a Euclidean function supporting division with strictly smaller remainder.
axioms: there exists a Euclidean function on nonzero elements satisfying the division-with-remainder condition
nodes.notes: The Euclidean function is treated as an existence property, not as chosen structure; not every principal ideal domain is Euclidean.

nodes.label: Local field
nodes.summary: A nondiscrete locally compact Hausdorff topological field.
nodes.notes: Under this broad definition, $\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathbb{C}$ are archimedean local fields. “Non-archimedean local field” excludes them and is often the intended arithmetic convention.

nodes.label: p-adic field
nodes.summary: A finite extension of the p-adic numbers $Q_{p}$.

nodes.label: presheaf + site
nodes.summary: Combine a presheaf with a covering structure on its domain and impose descent/gluing.
nodes.notes: The presheaf and site must use the same domain category.

combination.compatibility: The presheaf is defined on the site’s underlying category and satisfies the sheaf equalizer/gluing condition for every cover.

nodes.label: Sheaf
nodes.summary: A presheaf on a site satisfying the local identity and unique gluing condition for every cover.
axioms: matching local sections glue uniquely for every cover
nodes.notes: This node means a sheaf of sets on a site. Sheaves valued in groups, rings, modules, or other categories are modeled by the corresponding algebraic-object nodes.

nodes.label: Sheaf of groups
nodes.summary: A sheaf whose sections form groups and whose restriction maps are homomorphisms.

nodes.label: Sheaf of rings
nodes.summary: A sheaf whose sections form rings and whose restrictions are ring homomorphisms.

nodes.label: Ringed space
nodes.summary: A topological space equipped with a sheaf of rings.

nodes.label: space + sheaf of rings
nodes.summary: Compatibility construction producing Ringed space.
nodes.notes: All incoming branches are jointly required.

combination.compatibility: Use the same topological space as the base of the sheaf of rings.

nodes.label: Local ring
nodes.summary: A commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal.

nodes.label: Locally ringed space
nodes.summary: A ringed space whose stalks are local rings.
axioms: every stalk $O_{X,x}$ is a local ring

nodes.label: Noetherian ring
nodes.summary: A commutative ring satisfying the ascending chain condition on ideals.

nodes.label: Artinian ring
nodes.summary: A commutative ring satisfying the descending chain condition on ideals.

nodes.label: Noetherian + local regularity
nodes.summary: Compatibility construction producing Regular local ring.
nodes.notes: All incoming branches are jointly required.

combination.compatibility: Use the same ring and require the embedding dimension to equal the Krull dimension.

nodes.label: Scheme
nodes.summary: A locally ringed space locally isomorphic to affine schemes.
axioms: affine open neighborhood at every point

nodes.label: Affine scheme
nodes.summary: A locally ringed space isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec} R$ for a commutative ring R.
axioms: $X\cong \operatorname{Spec} R$ for some commutative ring R

nodes.label: Regular local ring
nodes.summary: A Noetherian local ring whose maximal ideal has the minimal number of generators allowed by its Krull dimension.

nodes.label: Algebraic space
nodes.summary: A sheaf of sets on the big fppf site over S with representable diagonal and an étale surjective cover by a scheme.
axioms: F is a sheaf for the fppf topology
the diagonal $F\to F\times F$ is representable by schemes
there exists a scheme U and a surjective étale morphism $h_U\to F$
nodes.notes: The existence of an étale cover is a property; no atlas is selected as part of the algebraic-space structure. Equivalent étale-site formulations are standard.

nodes.label: Complete local ring
nodes.summary: A local ring complete and separated for its maximal-ideal-adic topology.

nodes.label: Noetherian scheme
nodes.summary: A quasi-compact locally Noetherian scheme.
axioms: affine neighborhoods have Noetherian coordinate rings

nodes.label: Reduced scheme
nodes.summary: A scheme whose local rings contain no nonzero nilpotents.

nodes.label: scheme over a field
nodes.summary: Compatibility construction producing Algebraic variety.
nodes.notes: All incoming branches are jointly required.

combination.compatibility: Equip X with a finite-type structure morphism $X\to \operatorname{Spec}(k)$ and require X to be integral and the morphism separated.

nodes.label: Separated scheme
nodes.summary: A scheme whose structure morphism $X\to \operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb{Z})$ is separated.
axioms: relative diagonal $\Delta_{X/\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb{Z})}\colon X\to X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb{Z})}X$ is a closed immersion
nodes.notes: For an S-scheme $X\to S$, relative separatedness uses $\Delta_{X/S}\colon X\to X\times_S X$.

nodes.label: Algebraic variety
nodes.summary: Under the adopted Stacks Project convention, an integral separated scheme of finite type over a field.
nodes.notes: Terminology varies across authors; this atlas fixes the Stacks Project convention rather than mixing reduced, irreducible, or nonseparated variants.

nodes.label: Integral scheme
nodes.summary: A nonempty scheme that is reduced and irreducible.

nodes.label: Regular scheme
nodes.summary: A locally Noetherian scheme whose local rings are regular local rings.
nodes.notes: Regularity is local Noetherianity plus regularity of every local ring. It does not imply quasi-compactness, so a regular scheme need not be a Noetherian scheme.

nodes.label: Scheme over a base
nodes.summary: A scheme X equipped with a specified morphism to a base scheme S.
nodes.notes: This is the object-level notion of an S-scheme.

nodes.label: Projective scheme
nodes.summary: A scheme X over a base S whose structure morphism $X\to S$ is projective.
axioms: X admits an S-closed immersion into some projective space $P^{n}_S$
nodes.notes: The closed immersion is an existence witness, not chosen data of the projective scheme.

nodes.label: Topological space
nodes.summary: A set with a specified family of open subsets.

nodes.label: Compact space
nodes.summary: A topological space in which every open cover has a finite subcover.

nodes.label: Locally Euclidean space
nodes.summary: A topological space locally homeomorphic to Euclidean space.
axioms: each point has a neighborhood homeomorphic to an open subset of $R^{n}$
nodes.notes: No atlas is chosen at this node; local Euclidean charts are witnesses to a property of the topology. Dimension is normally fixed on each connected component.

nodes.label: Pseudometric space
nodes.summary: A set with a distance-like function that may assign zero distance to distinct points.

nodes.label: Second-countable space
nodes.summary: A topological space with a countable base.

nodes.label: T₀ space
nodes.summary: A topological space whose distinct points are topologically distinguishable.

nodes.label: Uniform space
nodes.summary: A set with structure that compares neighborhoods of pairs of points uniformly.
induces: notions of uniform continuity and Cauchy filters

nodes.label: Connected space
nodes.summary: A topological space not expressible as the union of two disjoint nonempty open sets.

nodes.label: First-countable space
nodes.summary: A space whose every point has a countable neighborhood basis.
axioms: countable local base at each point

nodes.label: Locally compact space
nodes.summary: A topological space locally modeled by compact neighborhoods; conventions vary outside Hausdorff spaces.
nodes.notes: The exact definition has convention-sensitive variants. The combined “locally compact Hausdorff” node avoids most ambiguity.

nodes.label: Metric space
nodes.summary: A pseudometric space in which zero distance implies equality.

nodes.label: T₁ space
nodes.summary: A topological space in which singletons are closed.

nodes.label: Complete metric space
nodes.summary: A metric space in which every Cauchy sequence converges.

nodes.label: Hausdorff space
nodes.summary: A topological space whose distinct points have disjoint neighborhoods.

nodes.label: Locally connected space
nodes.summary: A space with a basis of connected open sets.
axioms: connected neighborhoods form a local base

nodes.label: semigroup + topology
nodes.summary: Compatibility construction producing Topological semigroup.
nodes.notes: All incoming branches are jointly required.

combination.compatibility: Require the semigroup multiplication $S\times S\to S$ to be continuous.

nodes.label: Separable metric space
nodes.summary: A metric space with a countable dense subset.

nodes.label: Totally disconnected space
nodes.summary: A space whose connected components are singletons.
axioms: only connected subsets with more than one point are absent

nodes.label: compact + Hausdorff
nodes.summary: Combine compactness and Hausdorff separation on one topology.
nodes.notes: Construction junction: it is a visual device, not a separate standard mathematical structure.

combination.compatibility: Both properties concern the same topological space and topology.

nodes.label: compact + metric
nodes.summary: Combine a metric topology with compactness.
nodes.notes: Construction junction: it is a visual device, not a separate standard mathematical structure.

combination.compatibility: The compact topology is the topology induced by the metric.

nodes.label: group + topology
nodes.summary: Put group and topological structure on the same carrier.
nodes.notes: Construction junction: it is a visual device, not a separate standard mathematical structure.

combination.compatibility: Multiplication $G\times G\to G$ and inversion $G\to G$ are continuous.

nodes.label: local compactness + Hausdorff
nodes.summary: Combine local compactness with Hausdorff separation.
nodes.notes: Construction junction: it is a visual device, not a separate standard mathematical structure.

combination.compatibility: Both properties concern the same topology.

nodes.label: manifold compatibility
nodes.summary: Combine local Euclidean structure, Hausdorff separation, and a countable base.
nodes.notes: Construction junction: it is a visual device, not a separate standard mathematical structure.

combination.compatibility: All three conditions refer to one topology; local Euclidean dimension is usually fixed on each connected component.

nodes.label: monoid + topology
nodes.summary: Compatibility construction producing Topological monoid.
nodes.notes: All incoming branches are jointly required.

combination.compatibility: Require multiplication to be continuous; the identity is already part of the monoid.

nodes.label: Regular T₁ space
nodes.summary: $A T_{1}$ space in which points and closed sets can be separated by neighborhoods.

nodes.label: Topological semigroup
nodes.summary: A semigroup whose multiplication is continuous.

nodes.label: topological spaces + covering map
nodes.summary: Combine topologies on total and base spaces with a projection satisfying the covering condition.
nodes.notes: The topological-space input is instantiated for both E and B.

combination.compatibility: Give E and B topologies, take $p:E\to B,$ require continuity and that every $b\in B$ has an evenly covered neighborhood.

nodes.label: Zero-dimensional space
nodes.summary: A topological space with a basis of clopen sets.
nodes.notes: Convention: “zero-dimensional” means having a basis of clopen sets. Other dimension theories and separation assumptions can produce different formulations.

nodes.label: Compact Hausdorff space
nodes.summary: A topological space that is both compact and Hausdorff.

nodes.label: Compact metric space
nodes.summary: A metric space that is compact in its metric topology.

nodes.label: Locally compact Hausdorff space
nodes.summary: A Hausdorff space in which every point has a compact neighborhood.

nodes.label: Normal T₁ space
nodes.summary: $A T_{1}$ space in which disjoint closed sets have disjoint neighborhoods.

nodes.label: Polish space
nodes.summary: A separable topological space admitting a compatible complete metric.
nodes.notes: A Polish space is a topological space; a particular compatible complete metric is generally not part of the specified data.

nodes.label: Topological group
nodes.summary: A group whose operations are continuous.

nodes.label: Topological manifold
nodes.summary: A Hausdorff, second-countable, locally Euclidean space.
nodes.notes: The manifold condition asserts existence of local Euclidean charts; a particular topological atlas is not additional structure. This atlas adopts the Hausdorff, second-countable convention.

nodes.label: Topological monoid
nodes.summary: A monoid whose multiplication is continuous.

nodes.label: topological spaces + locally trivial projection
nodes.summary: Combine total/base topologies with a projection, a typical fiber, and local product trivializations.
nodes.notes: The topological-space input is instantiated for total space, base, and typical fiber as needed.

combination.compatibility: Give E and B topologies, take $p\colon E\to B$, require continuity and that every $b\in B$ has an evenly covered neighborhood.

nodes.label: Tychonoff space
nodes.summary: A completely regular Hausdorff space.
axioms: points and closed sets separated by continuous real functions

nodes.label: Fiber bundle
nodes.summary: A locally trivial projection $E\to B$ with typical fiber F.
nodes.notes: A bundle specifies total space, base space, projection, typical fiber, and local trivializations; it is not structure on a single topological space alone.

nodes.label: ring + topology
nodes.summary: Put ring and topological structure on the same carrier.
nodes.notes: Construction junction: it is a visual device, not a separate standard mathematical structure.

combination.compatibility: Addition and multiplication are continuous; additive inversion is then also required/automatic from the topological-group structure.

nodes.label: Topological ring
nodes.summary: A ring with a topology for which addition, multiplication, and additive inversion are continuous.

nodes.label: Locale
nodes.summary: A point-free space represented contravariantly by a frame of opens.

nodes.label: field + topology
nodes.summary: Put field and topological structure on the same carrier.
nodes.notes: Construction junction: it is a visual device, not a separate standard mathematical structure.

combination.compatibility: Addition, multiplication, additive inversion, and inversion on $F\setminus\{0\}$ are continuous.

nodes.label: Topological field
nodes.summary: A field with a topology making its additive group, multiplication, and nonzero inversion continuous.
axioms: addition, multiplication, and additive inverse are continuous

nodes.label: topology + basepoint
nodes.summary: Compatibility construction producing Pointed topological space.
nodes.notes: All incoming branches are jointly required.

combination.compatibility: Use the same carrier set, topology, and distinguished point.

nodes.label: Pointed topological space
nodes.summary: A topological space with a distinguished basepoint.

nodes.label: Topological pair
nodes.summary: A topological space X with a specified subspace $A\subseteq X$.

nodes.label: Path-connected space
nodes.summary: A space in which every two points can be joined by a continuous path.
axioms: a path exists between every pair of points

nodes.label: Compactly generated space
nodes.summary: A space whose topology is detected by maps from compact Hausdorff spaces.
nodes.notes: Convention-sensitive: some authors mean k-space; others reserve “compactly generated” for compactly generated weak Hausdorff spaces. This node uses the k-space condition only.

nodes.label: Contractible space
nodes.summary: A space homotopy equivalent to a point.
axioms: the identity map is homotopic to a constant map
nodes.notes: Contractibility is an existence property. A chosen contraction would be additional pointed homotopy data, not part of the ordinary notion.

nodes.label: H-space
nodes.summary: A pointed space with multiplication and unit laws holding up to homotopy.
axioms: left and right unit up to homotopy

nodes.label: Simply connected space
nodes.summary: A path-connected space with trivial fundamental group.

nodes.label: Covering space
nodes.summary: A space E over a base B locally isomorphic to a disjoint union of copies of B.
nodes.notes: A covering is a map $p:E\to B$ together with topologies on both E and B satisfying the evenly-covered-neighborhood condition; it is not structure on one topological space alone.

nodes.label: CW complex
nodes.summary: A space constructed inductively by attaching cells along their boundaries.

nodes.label: Simplicial set
nodes.summary: A contravariant functor from the simplex category Δ to sets.
nodes.notes: Precisely a simplicial object in Set.

nodes.label: groupoid + smooth structure
nodes.summary: Compatibility construction producing Lie groupoid.
nodes.notes: All incoming branches are jointly required.

combination.compatibility: Equip both the object set and arrow set with smooth manifold structures; require all groupoid structure maps smooth and source and target submersions.

nodes.label: Smooth manifold
nodes.summary: A topological manifold equipped with a compatible smooth atlas.

nodes.label: bundle + group action
nodes.summary: Compatibility construction producing Principal bundle.
nodes.notes: All incoming branches are jointly required.

combination.compatibility: Add a continuous right G-action on the total space that is free and transitive on each fiber and locally equivariantly trivial.

nodes.label: Complex manifold
nodes.summary: A manifold locally modeled on complex Euclidean space with holomorphic transition maps.

nodes.label: group + smooth manifold
nodes.summary: Put compatible group and smooth-manifold structure on one carrier.
nodes.notes: Construction junction: it is a visual device, not a separate standard mathematical structure.

combination.compatibility: Use the same carrier and require multiplication and inversion to be smooth.

nodes.label: Lie groupoid
nodes.summary: A groupoid whose object and arrow spaces are smooth manifolds and whose structure maps are smooth, with source and target submersions.

nodes.label: Manifold with affine connection
nodes.summary: A smooth manifold equipped with a covariant derivative on vector fields.

nodes.label: Poisson manifold
nodes.summary: A smooth manifold whose smooth functions carry a compatible Poisson bracket.
data: Poisson bivector or bracket on smooth functions

nodes.label: Pseudo-Riemannian manifold
nodes.summary: A smooth manifold with a smoothly varying nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form of fixed signature.

nodes.label: Real-analytic manifold
nodes.summary: A manifold whose chart transitions are real-analytic.
nodes.notes: A real-analytic atlas refines the smooth structure. The analytic structure is extra data; the underlying smooth structure is canonically obtained by forgetting analyticity.

nodes.label: Riemannian manifold
nodes.summary: A smooth manifold with a smoothly varying positive-definite inner product on tangent spaces.

nodes.label: Smooth manifold with boundary
nodes.summary: A Hausdorff, second-countable space locally modeled on the closed half-space, equipped with a compatible smooth atlas.
nodes.notes: This node includes a smooth half-space atlas; it is not merely a topological manifold with boundary.

nodes.label: Symplectic manifold
nodes.summary: A smooth manifold with a closed nondegenerate differential 2-form.

nodes.label: Vector bundle
nodes.summary: A fiber bundle whose fibers are vector spaces and transition functions are linear.

nodes.label: Cotangent bundle
nodes.summary: The dual vector bundle $T^*M$ of covectors on a smooth manifold.
induces: canonical one-form and canonical symplectic form

nodes.label: Tangent bundle
nodes.summary: The vector bundle $TM$ whose fiber at each point is the tangent space of a smooth manifold.

nodes.label: complex manifold + metric
nodes.summary: Compatibility construction producing Hermitian manifold.
nodes.notes: All incoming branches are jointly required.

combination.compatibility: Use the same underlying real manifold and require $g(JX,JY)=g(X,Y)$; equivalently, the metric is the real part of a positive-definite Hermitian form.

nodes.label: Contact manifold
nodes.summary: An odd-dimensional manifold with a maximally nonintegrable hyperplane distribution.
nodes.notes: A globally defined contact form is extra coorientation/trivialization data. The contact distribution is the intrinsic object.

nodes.label: Differential form
nodes.summary: A smooth section of an exterior-power cotangent bundle; differential forms can be integrated and differentiated by $d$.
nodes.notes: A differential $k$-form is alternating and covariant; orientation is not required merely to define forms.

nodes.label: Foliated manifold
nodes.summary: A manifold partitioned locally into parallel submanifolds called leaves.
data: integrable subbundle of TM or foliation atlas

nodes.label: Lie group
nodes.summary: A smooth manifold whose group operations are smooth.
induces: A Lie algebra at the identity

nodes.label: Lorentzian manifold
nodes.summary: A pseudo-Riemannian manifold with Lorentzian signature.

nodes.label: Oriented smooth manifold
nodes.summary: A smooth manifold with a consistent choice of orientation.
data: orientation of tangent spaces or oriented atlas

nodes.label: Principal bundle
nodes.summary: A fiber bundle with a free and transitive right action of a structure group on each fiber.
axioms: the G-action is free and transitive on each fiber
nodes.notes: This node denotes a topological principal bundle. Smooth principal bundles require a Lie group and smooth total/base spaces.

nodes.label: Tensor bundle
nodes.summary: A vector bundle assembled from tensor powers of tangent and cotangent bundles.
data: bundle built from tensor powers of $TM$ and $T^*M$
axioms: smooth transition functions induced from those of $TM$

nodes.label: vector bundle over smooth base
nodes.summary: Compatibility construction producing Smooth vector bundle.
nodes.notes: All incoming branches are jointly required.

combination.compatibility: Use the smooth manifold as base and require smooth fiberwise-linear transition functions.

nodes.label: Compact Lie group
nodes.summary: A Lie group whose underlying topological space is compact.

nodes.label: Connection on a vector bundle
nodes.summary: A covariant derivative that differentiates sections of a vector bundle along tangent directions.
nodes.notes: A connection is additional data; a generic vector bundle has no preferred connection.

nodes.label: de Rham complex
nodes.summary: The cochain complex of differential forms with exterior derivative $d$, satisfying $d^2=0$.
nodes.notes: The de Rham theorem identifies this cohomology with singular cohomology over $\mathbb R$ under standard hypotheses.

nodes.label: Hermitian manifold
nodes.summary: A complex manifold with a smoothly varying Hermitian inner product on tangent spaces.

nodes.label: Principal connection
nodes.summary: A connection on a principal bundle, equivalently a suitable Lie-algebra-valued one-form.
axioms: reproduction of fundamental vertical vector fields

nodes.label: Smooth vector bundle
nodes.summary: A vector bundle over a smooth manifold with smooth total space and smooth linear transition functions.

nodes.label: Tensor field
nodes.summary: A smooth section of a tensor bundle.
data: smooth section of a tensor bundle
induces: coordinate components with tensorial transformation law
