nodes.label: Curvature form
nodes.summary: The Lie-algebra-valued (or endomorphism-valued) two-form measuring the non-flatness of a connection.
axioms: defined by $F=dA+A\wedge A$ locally, with convention-dependent signs
nodes.notes: Curvature is tensorial even though a local connection potential is gauge-dependent.

nodes.label: Kähler manifold
nodes.summary: A Hermitian manifold whose fundamental 2-form is closed.

nodes.label: Hodge star operator
nodes.summary: The metric- and orientation-dependent isomorphism between complementary-degree differential forms.
nodes.notes: The square of $*$ depends on degree, dimension, and metric signature.

nodes.label: Levi–Civita connection
nodes.summary: The unique torsion-free connection compatible with a pseudo-Riemannian metric.
nodes.notes: Existence and uniqueness are consequences of the metric.

nodes.label: Geodesic
nodes.summary: A curve whose tangent is parallel transported along itself with respect to a connection.
induces: locally extremal-length behavior in Riemannian geometry
nodes.notes: For pseudo-Riemannian metrics, geodesics need not minimize length; null geodesics have zero proper length.

nodes.label: Riemann curvature tensor
nodes.summary: The tensor measuring failure of covariant derivatives to commute and of parallel transport to be path independent.
axioms: multilinearity and curvature symmetries appropriate to the connection
nodes.notes: Sign conventions for $R$ vary.

nodes.label: Spin structure
nodes.summary: A lift of an oriented orthonormal frame bundle to a spin-group principal bundle, enabling globally defined spinor fields.
data: twofold bundle map to the frame bundle
nodes.notes: Existence is obstructed by the second Stiefel–Whitney class; when structures exist they need not be unique.

nodes.label: Ricci curvature tensor
nodes.summary: The contraction of the Riemann curvature tensor entering the Einstein field equation.
data: contraction of the Riemann curvature tensor
induces: scalar curvature after contraction with the inverse metric
nodes.notes: Index and sign conventions depend on the convention for the Riemann tensor.

nodes.label: Scalar curvature
nodes.summary: The trace of the Ricci tensor with the inverse metric.
induces: Einstein–Hilbert action density with the volume form

nodes.label: Einstein tensor
nodes.summary:
The tensor $G_{\mu
u}=R_{\mu
u}-	frac12 Rg_{\mu
u}$, whose covariant divergence vanishes.
induces: left-hand side of Einstein field equations

nodes.label: Bigraded object
nodes.summary: A family of objects indexed by two degrees, usually pairs of integers.
induces: graded objects by total degree when suitable sums exist
nodes.notes: A bigraded object is not merely a singly graded object with extra maps; the second grading is part of its indexing data.

nodes.label: Graded object
nodes.summary: A family of objects indexed by degrees, usually integers or natural numbers.

nodes.label: Chain complex
nodes.summary: A graded object with degree $-1$ differential squaring to zero.
carriers: graded family $C_{n}$ in a preadditive category
induces: homology objects when the ambient category has the required kernels and images (for example, in an abelian category)
nodes.notes: The zero composite $d^{2}=0$ requires zero morphisms; preadditive categories suffice. Homology objects require additional kernel/image or abelian hypotheses.

nodes.label: Cochain complex
nodes.summary: A graded object with degree +1 differential squaring to zero.
carriers: graded family $C^{n}$ in a preadditive category
induces: cohomology objects when the ambient category has the required kernels and images (for example, in an abelian category)
nodes.notes: The zero composite $d^{2}=0$ requires zero morphisms; preadditive categories suffice. Cohomology objects require additional kernel/image or abelian hypotheses.

nodes.label: Exact category
nodes.summary: An additive category with a chosen class of kernel–cokernel pairs behaving like short exact sequences.

nodes.label: Double complex
nodes.summary: A bigraded object with horizontal and vertical differentials satisfying square-zero and anticommutation laws.
carriers: bigraded family $C^{p,q}$ in an additive category
induces: total complex when the required direct sums or products exist
nodes.notes: The usual total-complex construction additionally needs the relevant direct sums or products.

nodes.label: Grothendieck abelian category
nodes.summary: An abelian category with all small colimits, exact filtered colimits (AB5), and a generator.

nodes.label: Model category
nodes.summary: A category with weak equivalences, fibrations, and cofibrations satisfying Quillen axioms.

nodes.label: Triangulated category
nodes.summary: An additive category with a shift autoequivalence and distinguished triangles satisfying triangulation axioms.

nodes.label: Derived category
nodes.summary: For an abelian category A, the localization of its homotopy category $K(A)$ of complexes at quasi-isomorphisms.
nodes.notes: A derived category is constructed from a category of complexes, not from one individual chain complex.

nodes.label: DG-category
nodes.summary: A category enriched over chain complexes.
axioms: associativity and units compatible with differentials
nodes.notes: A DG-category is a category enriched over chain complexes for a specified commutative base ring and grading/sign convention.

nodes.label: Differential graded algebra
nodes.summary: A graded associative algebra with a square-zero differential satisfying the graded Leibniz rule.
carriers: graded object A in a symmetric monoidal additive setting
nodes.notes: This node uses the cochain convention. An ordinary associative algebra can be formed from the total direct sum only when that direct sum exists in the ambient setting.

nodes.label: Dedekind-cut real line
nodes.summary: The ordered field whose elements are proper downward-closed subsets of $\mathbb Q$ with no greatest element.
carriers: set of Dedekind cuts in $\mathbb Q$
nodes.notes: This realization emphasizes order completeness and is canonically isomorphic to the Cauchy-sequence realization.

nodes.label: Cauchy sequences of rationals
nodes.summary: Rational Cauchy sequences, with two sequences identified when their difference converges to zero.
carriers: set of Cauchy sequences in $\mathbb Q$
nodes.notes: The definition of convergence here uses the rational absolute-value metric, not a prior construction of the real numbers.

nodes.label: Real numbers $\mathbb R$
nodes.summary: The complete Archimedean ordered field, unique up to unique order-preserving field isomorphism.
nodes.notes: Dedekind cuts and Cauchy sequences give different set-theoretic realizations of the same abstract ordered field.

nodes.label: Ordered-pair complex field
nodes.summary: The field on $\mathbb R^2$ with $(a,b)(c,d)=(ac-bd,ad+bc)$.

nodes.label: Polynomial-quotient complex field
nodes.summary: The quotient field $\mathbb R[x]/(x^2+1)$.
nodes.notes: Because $x^2+1$ is irreducible over $\mathbb R$, the quotient is a field.

nodes.label: Complex numbers $\mathbb C$
nodes.summary: The algebraically closed topological field obtained from $\mathbb R$ by adjoining a square root $i$ of $-1$.
nodes.notes: $\mathbb C$ cannot be ordered as an ordered field. The pair and polynomial-quotient constructions are equivalent presentations, not simultaneous literal definitions.

nodes.label: linear + topological compatibility
nodes.summary: Combine vector-space, topological-space, and topological-field structures.
nodes.notes: Construction junction: it is a visual device, not a separate standard mathematical structure.

combination.compatibility: Vector addition $V\times V\to V$ and scalar multiplication $F\times V\to V$ are continuous, using the same scalar field.

nodes.label: Linear operator
nodes.summary: A linear map from a vector space to itself, or more generally between vector spaces.
carriers: vector space $V$ (or specified domain and codomain)
nodes.notes: In analysis, “operator” often carries additional domain, topology, or boundedness data.

nodes.label: Seminormed vector space
nodes.summary: A vector space equipped with a seminorm.
carriers: vector space V over a field K with a specified real-valued absolute value $|\cdot |$
nodes.notes: More general value-group-valued norms require a different codomain and axioms; this node records the real-valued analytic notion.

nodes.label: Topological vector space
nodes.summary: A vector space with a compatible topology.
nodes.notes: This atlas adopts the common Hausdorff convention.

nodes.label: Normed vector space
nodes.summary: A seminormed vector space whose seminorm separates points.
carriers: seminormed vector space V over a field with a specified real-valued absolute value
nodes.notes: Its norm canonically induces a metric, uniformity, topology, and topological-vector-space structure.

nodes.label: Inner-product space
nodes.summary: A vector space with a positive-definite inner product.
carriers: real or complex vector space V
nodes.notes: The inner product canonically induces a norm. The complex convention is Hermitian sesquilinear.

nodes.label: Locally convex space
nodes.summary: A real or complex topological vector space whose origin has a base of convex neighborhoods.
carriers: topological vector space V over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$
data: existing vector topology; equivalently often a family of seminorms

nodes.label: Partial differential equation
nodes.summary: An equation involving a multivariable function and its partial derivatives.
carriers: domain in a space with several independent variables
induces: solution spaces after boundary or initial conditions
nodes.notes: A PDE may be linear or nonlinear; regularity and boundary data are separate essential issues.

nodes.label: Bounded linear operator
nodes.summary: A linear operator between normed spaces whose operator norm is finite.
induces: Banach algebra structure when $X=Y$ is Banach

nodes.label: Differential operator
nodes.summary: A linear or nonlinear operator built locally from derivatives and multiplication by coefficient functions.
data: local rule built from derivatives and coefficient functions
axioms: finite order in the ordinary differential-operator sense
nodes.notes: Differential operators may be linear or nonlinear.

nodes.label: Fréchet space
nodes.summary: A complete metrizable locally convex topological vector space.
carriers: real or complex locally convex space V
nodes.notes: A Fréchet space is defined by its locally convex topology; no particular compatible complete metric is selected. It need not be normable. Every real or complex Banach space is Fréchet via its norm topology.

nodes.label: Banach space
nodes.summary: A complete normed vector space.

nodes.label: Calculus of variations
nodes.summary: The study of extrema and stationary points of functionals under variations of functions, curves, or fields.
carriers: space of admissible functions, curves, or fields
axioms: regularity and boundary conditions sufficient for variations
nodes.notes: Stationary points need not be minima.

nodes.label: Densely defined operator
nodes.summary: A linear operator defined on a dense linear subspace of a topological vector space, commonly a Hilbert space.
induces: adjoint when the setting is Hilbertian
nodes.notes: An unbounded operator cannot be defined and bounded on all of a Banach space; its domain is part of the operator.

nodes.label: Fourier transform
nodes.summary: A transformation between position or time variables and conjugate frequency or momentum variables.
carriers: specified function or distribution space on an Abelian group or Euclidean space
data: integral or duality transform to frequency variables
nodes.notes: Normalization conventions vary; not every arbitrary function has a classical Fourier integral.

nodes.label: Laplace operator
nodes.summary: The divergence of the gradient, or its geometric Laplace–Beltrami generalization.
induces: spectral decomposition under suitable boundary conditions
nodes.notes: The overall sign convention varies.

nodes.label: Adjoint operator
nodes.summary: For a densely defined operator between Hilbert spaces, the operator determined on its natural domain by $\langle Ax,y\rangle=\langle x,A^*y\rangle$.
nodes.notes: For unbounded operators, equality of domains is essential and the adjoint is always closed.

nodes.label: complete normed algebra
nodes.summary: Combine an associative algebra with a Banach-space norm on the same carrier.
nodes.notes: Construction junction: it is a visual device, not a separate standard mathematical structure.

combination.compatibility: Both structures use the same normed field K, carrier, addition, and scalar action, and the norm satisfies $\lVert ab \rVert \le \lVert a \rVert \lVert b \rVert$.

nodes.label: Functional derivative
nodes.summary: A derivative of a functional with respect to a function or field, defined through its first variation.
data: distribution or function representing the first variation when it exists
axioms: $\delta F=\int (\delta F/\delta\phi)\,\delta\phi$ in the chosen pairing
nodes.notes: Existence and representation depend on the function space, topology, measure, and boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Schwartz space
nodes.summary: The Fréchet space of smooth functions whose derivatives decay faster than every inverse polynomial.

nodes.label: Banach algebra
nodes.summary: An associative algebra over a normed field that is complete under a submultiplicative norm.
carriers: associative algebra A over a normed field K
Banach-space structure on the same K-vector space

nodes.label: Banach algebra + involution
nodes.summary: Compatibility construction producing C*-algebra.
nodes.notes: All incoming branches are jointly required.

combination.compatibility: Use the same complex algebra structure and norm; star is conjugate-linear and antimultiplicative, and $\lVert a^*a\rVert=\lVert a\rVert^2$.

nodes.label: Green function
nodes.summary: A kernel representing an inverse or fundamental solution of a linear differential operator under specified boundary conditions.
nodes.notes: Green functions are not guaranteed to exist and are not unique until boundary, causal, or other conditions are fixed.

nodes.label: Hilbert space
nodes.summary: A complete inner-product space.
carriers: real or complex vector space H
nodes.notes: A Hilbert space is an inner-product space complete in the induced norm. The Banach-space structure is then canonical and is not an independent input.

nodes.label: Projection operator
nodes.summary: An idempotent linear operator; an orthogonal projection is also self-adjoint.
nodes.notes: An orthogonal projection additionally satisfies $P=P^*$; a general projection need not.

nodes.label: Self-adjoint operator
nodes.summary: A densely defined operator equal to its adjoint, including equality of domains.
nodes.notes: Symmetric is weaker than self-adjoint for unbounded operators.

nodes.label: Sobolev space
nodes.summary: A Banach or Hilbert space controlling weak derivatives in $L^p$.
carriers: functions or distributions with weak derivatives
data: norm controlling derivatives through order $k$ in $L^p$
axioms: weak derivatives belong to the specified $L^p$ spaces
nodes.notes: Boundary conditions define important closed subspaces such as $W_0^{k,p}$.

nodes.label: Space of distributions
nodes.summary: The continuous dual of a test-function space, generalizing ordinary functions and measures.
data: continuous linear functionals on the test space
nodes.notes: The term “distribution” depends on the test-function space; tempered distributions are dual to Schwartz space.

nodes.label: Spherical harmonic
nodes.summary: A simultaneous eigenfunction of the spherical Laplace–Beltrami operator (equivalently $\mathbf L^2$) and a chosen component $L_z$; the $Y_{\ell m}$ form an orthonormal basis of $L^2(S^2)$.
axioms: $L_zY_{\ell m}=m\hbar Y_{\ell m}$ under the physics normalization
nodes.notes: Normalization and phase conventions vary.

nodes.label: Unitary operator
nodes.summary: A surjective inner-product-preserving linear operator with $U^*U=UU^*=I$.

nodes.label: C*-algebra
nodes.summary: A complex associative Banach *-algebra satisfying the C*-identity.
nodes.notes: Some authors build the unit into “C*-algebra”; others allow nonunital C*-algebras. This atlas does not require a unit at this node.

nodes.label: Operator spectrum
nodes.summary: For a bounded operator on a complex Banach space, or a closed densely defined operator, the scalars $\lambda$ for which $A-\lambda I$ has no everywhere-defined bounded inverse.
carriers: complex Banach space and bounded operator, or closed densely defined operator
axioms: $\lambda\in\sigma(A)$ iff $A-\lambda I$ lacks an everywhere-defined bounded inverse
induces: point, continuous, and residual spectral parts under appropriate definitions
nodes.notes: For unbounded operators the domain and closedness are essential.

nodes.label: Positive operator
nodes.summary: A self-adjoint operator $A$ satisfying $\langle\psi,A\psi\rangle\ge0$ on its domain.
data: bounded or suitably defined self-adjoint operator $A$
axioms: $\langle x,Ax\rangle\ge0$ for all vectors in the domain
nodes.notes: For unbounded positive operators, domain and self-adjointness conditions must be stated.

nodes.label: Projective Hilbert space
nodes.summary: The space of one-dimensional rays in a Hilbert space, identifying nonzero vectors that differ by a nonzero scalar.
data: set of one-dimensional complex subspaces or rays
axioms: nonzero vectors identified under multiplication by nonzero complex scalars
induces: transition probabilities from ray inner products
nodes.notes: Physical pure states are rays; normalized vectors retain an unobservable overall phase.

nodes.label: Fock space
nodes.summary: The direct sum of zero-, one-, and many-particle tensor powers of a one-particle Hilbert space.
data: Hilbert direct sum $\bigoplus_{n\ge0}H^{\otimes n}$ or its symmetric/antisymmetric version
axioms: Hilbert-space completion and chosen exchange symmetry
nodes.notes: Full tensor Fock space, bosonic Fock space, and fermionic Fock space are distinct constructions.

nodes.label: Rigged Hilbert space
nodes.summary: A dense test-function space $\Phi$ embedded in a Hilbert space $H$, embedded in the continuous dual $\Phi^*$.
axioms: compatibility of embeddings and dual pairing
nodes.notes: Often called a Gelfand triple; nuclearity is common but not part of every definition.

nodes.label: Spectral measure
nodes.summary: A normalized, countably additive projection-valued measure $E$ on a measurable space, with $E(\Omega)=I$ and mutually orthogonal projections on disjoint sets.
nodes.notes: A spectral measure is a projection-valued measure, hence a special POVM.

nodes.label: Tensor-product Hilbert space
nodes.summary: The completed tensor product representing composite quantum systems and independent degrees of freedom.
data: completion of the algebraic tensor product under the canonical inner product

nodes.label: Trace-class operator
nodes.summary: A compact operator whose singular values are summable, permitting a basis-independent finite trace.
axioms: sum of singular values is finite
nodes.notes: Trace class is stronger than Hilbert–Schmidt class.

nodes.label: Bosonic Fock space
nodes.summary: Fock space formed from symmetric tensor powers, appropriate to bosonic exchange symmetry.
data: Hilbert direct sum of symmetric tensor powers $\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathrm{Sym}^nH$

nodes.label: Fermionic Fock space
nodes.summary: Fock space formed from antisymmetric tensor powers, appropriate to fermionic exchange symmetry.
data: Hilbert direct sum of exterior powers $\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\Lambda^nH$

nodes.label: Partial trace
nodes.summary: For a trace-class operator on $H_A\otimes H_B$, the unique trace-class operator on $H_A$ satisfying $\operatorname{Tr}[(X\otimes I)T]=\operatorname{Tr}[X\,\operatorname{Tr}_B T]$ for bounded $X$.
axioms: trace-pairing characterization with bounded operators on $H_A$
nodes.notes: The partial trace is not defined on every bounded operator in infinite dimensions.

nodes.label: Spectral theorem for self-adjoint operators
nodes.summary: A self-adjoint operator admits a projection-valued spectral resolution and functional calculus.
carriers: normal or self-adjoint operator in a specified Hilbert-space setting
data: projection-valued spectral measure or multiplication-operator representation
axioms: hypotheses depend on bounded versus unbounded case
nodes.notes: There are distinct finite-dimensional, bounded-normal, compact, and unbounded-self-adjoint versions.

nodes.label: Stone theorem
nodes.summary: Strongly continuous one-parameter unitary groups correspond to self-adjoint generators.
carriers: strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group $U(t)$ on a Hilbert space
induces: unique infinitesimal generator and converse unitary group
nodes.notes: An isolated unitary operator does not satisfy the hypotheses; the theorem concerns a continuous one-parameter group.

nodes.label: ordered family + ambient measurable space
nodes.summary: Combine an ordered indexed family with one ambient measurable space to form nested sub-σ-algebras.
nodes.notes: The index order and common ambient σ-algebra are essential parts of the definition.

combination.compatibility: Index by a preorder (usually time), make every family member a sub-σ-algebra of the same ambient σ-algebra, and require $F_s\subseteq F_t$ whenever $s\le t$.

nodes.label: probability domain + measurable map
nodes.summary: Combine a probability space with a measurable map having that space as domain.
nodes.notes: All incoming branches are jointly required.

combination.compatibility: The measurable-function domain is the measurable space underlying the probability space; its codomain is the value space.

nodes.label: Filtration
nodes.summary: An increasing indexed family of σ-algebras representing information over time.
nodes.notes: A filtration is a monotone family of sub-σ-algebras of one ambient measurable space, indexed by an ordered set.

nodes.label: Random variable
nodes.summary: A measurable function from a probability space to a measurable value space.
nodes.notes: The probability space and value-space σ-algebra are part of the data. Traditionally the codomain is $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{R}^{n}$; for a general measurable codomain, “random element” is also common.

nodes.label: Filtered probability space
nodes.summary: A probability space equipped with a filtration of sub-σ-algebras.

nodes.label: probability + filtration
nodes.summary: Compatibility construction producing Filtered probability space.
nodes.notes: All incoming branches are jointly required.

combination.compatibility: Use a filtration of sub-σ-algebras of the probability space.

nodes.label: Standard probability space
nodes.summary: A probability space isomorphic modulo null sets to a standard Borel probability space.
nodes.notes: Convention-sensitive: common formulations classify completed probability spaces modulo null sets as a standard nonatomic part plus at most countably many atoms. A standard Borel probability space before completion is a related but distinct notion.

nodes.label: probability + indexed random variables
nodes.summary: Combine an index set/family with random variables sharing one probability space.
nodes.notes: All incoming branches are jointly required.

combination.compatibility: All random variables have the same probability-space domain and a common state space (or a specified family of state spaces), and the indexed family enumerates them.

nodes.label: Stochastic process
nodes.summary: An indexed family of random variables defined on a common probability space.
nodes.notes: All component random variables share a probability-space domain; state spaces may be common or indexed depending on convention.

nodes.label: Markov chain
nodes.summary: A discrete-time stochastic process with the Markov conditional-independence property.
axioms: future conditional law depends on the present state, not the full past

nodes.label: Measurable space
nodes.summary: A set equipped with a σ-algebra of measurable subsets.

nodes.label: Measure space
nodes.summary: A measurable space equipped with a countably additive measure.

nodes.label: function + measurable domain/codomain
nodes.summary: Combine a function with measurable structures on its domain and codomain, then impose measurability.
nodes.notes: The measurable-space input is instantiated for both domain and codomain.

combination.compatibility: The function domain and codomain carry the supplied σ-algebras, and inverse images of codomain-measurable sets are domain-measurable.

nodes.label: Borel measurable space
nodes.summary: A topological space equipped with the σ-algebra generated by its open sets.
nodes.notes: The Borel σ-algebra is canonically determined by the topology.

nodes.label: Measurable function
nodes.summary: A function whose inverse images of measurable sets are measurable.
nodes.notes: Both domain and codomain measurable structures are part of the specification; measurability is not a property of a bare function alone.

nodes.label: Probability space
nodes.summary: A measure space of total mass one.

nodes.label: σ-finite measure space
nodes.summary: A measure space covered by countably many sets of finite measure.

nodes.label: regular measure on LCH space
nodes.summary: Combine a locally compact Hausdorff topology with a measure.
nodes.notes: Construction junction: it is a visual device, not a separate standard mathematical structure.

combination.compatibility: Use the Borel σ-algebra (or a specified completion containing it) on the locally compact Hausdorff space and require local finiteness plus inner/outer regularity under the stated convention.

nodes.label: Radon measure space
nodes.summary: A topological measure space with a regular, locally finite Borel measure under standard conventions.
nodes.notes: Definitions vary slightly across texts and levels of generality.

nodes.label: Haar measure
nodes.summary: A nonzero left-invariant regular Borel measure on a locally compact Hausdorff group, unique up to positive scale; right Haar measure is analogous, and a left Haar measure is also right-invariant precisely for unimodular groups.
nodes.notes: Left Haar measure is unique up to positive scale. Right Haar measure is analogous; a left Haar measure is also right-invariant precisely when the group is unimodular.

nodes.label: Positive-operator-valued measure
nodes.summary: A weakly countably additive map $E$ from a measurable outcome space to positive operators on a Hilbert space, normalized by $E(\Omega)=I$.
nodes.notes: A PVM is the special case in which every effect is an orthogonal projection.

nodes.label: Physical system
nodes.summary: A delimited portion or idealized part of the physical world selected for description by a physical theory or model.

sections.title: Scope
sections.body: The boundary and degrees of freedom are chosen for the problem; the same physical situation can support several valid system decompositions.

nodes.label: Physical theory
nodes.summary: A mathematically expressed, empirically constrained framework that represents classes of physical systems and predicts relations among measurable quantities.

sections.title: Epistemic status
sections.body: Theories supply models and predictions within tested regimes; they are not logical consequences of their mathematical formalism alone.

nodes.label: Physical law
nodes.summary: A compact relation or rule describing a stable regularity of physical systems within a stated domain of validity.

nodes.label: Physical quantity
nodes.summary: A measurable or theoretically defined property represented by a value, unit, tensor, operator, field, or distribution.

nodes.label: Degree of freedom
nodes.summary: An independent variable or mode needed to specify a state within a chosen description.

nodes.label: Observable
nodes.summary: A quantity represented by a theory and connected to a possible measurement outcome or statistical distribution.

sections.title: Caution
sections.body: The mathematical representation of an observable depends on the theory: functions on phase space in classical mechanics and self-adjoint operators or POVMs in quantum theory.

nodes.label: Physical scale
nodes.summary: A characteristic length, time, energy, momentum, or mass used to separate relevant from unresolved degrees of freedom.

nodes.label: Physical state
nodes.summary: A specification, relative to a theory, sufficient to determine probabilities or allowed future behavior for the observables represented by that theory.

sections.title: Theory dependence
sections.body: Classical states are commonly points in phase space; quantum states are rays or density operators on a Hilbert space.

nodes.label: Physical symmetry
nodes.summary: A transformation that leaves specified physical structure, laws, or observables invariant; exact, approximate, local, global, continuous, or discrete symmetries must be distinguished.

nodes.label: Fundamental interaction
nodes.summary: An interaction currently treated as irreducible within established theory. The conventional list is gravitational, electromagnetic, strong, and weak; the Standard Model describes the latter three, with electromagnetic and weak interactions unified electroweakly and QCD forming a separate gauge factor.

sections.title: Current classification
sections.body: Electromagnetic, weak, strong, and gravitational interactions are conventionally treated as fundamental. The Standard Model contains the electroweak and strong gauge sectors but not gravitation.

nodes.label: Physical model
nodes.summary: A representation of a selected physical system that specifies retained degrees of freedom, laws, parameters, and idealizations; a model can instantiate a theory without being either exact or a controlled approximation.

nodes.label: Conservation law
nodes.summary: A statement that a physical quantity is constant under evolution or obeys a local continuity equation, often but not always associated with a symmetry.

nodes.label: Coupling constant
nodes.summary: A parameter controlling the strength of an interaction term; in QFT its renormalized value may depend on scale.

nodes.label: Equation of motion
nodes.summary: An equation determining allowed histories or evolution from the dynamical variables and initial or boundary data.

nodes.label: Effective description
nodes.summary: A description valid in a limited regime that suppresses, averages, or integrates out inaccessible degrees of freedom and encodes their effects in parameters or operators.

nodes.label: Classical field theory
nodes.summary: A theory in which continuously distributed fields obey classical equations of motion. A classical field theory may be formulated independently or arise as an effective, mean-field, or semiclassical description in an appropriate regime.

sections.title: Examples
items: The metric field in general relativity.

sections.title: Relation to QFT
sections.body: Quantizing an appropriate classical field theory is a principal route to a quantum field theory, while classical field equations can reappear as semiclassical or low-fluctuation limits.

nodes.label: Action functional
nodes.summary: A functional $S$ of a history or field configuration whose stationary points satisfy equations of motion.

nodes.label: Classical mechanics
nodes.summary: The classical theory family for motion and fields when quantum coherence, particle creation, relativistic effects, and strong-gravity effects are negligible at the required precision.

sections.title: Regime
sections.body: Accurate when relativistic and quantum corrections are negligible at the required precision.

nodes.label: Configuration space
nodes.summary: The space of possible instantaneous configurations of a system before momenta are added.

nodes.label: Hamiltonian
nodes.summary: A function on phase space that generates Hamiltonian time evolution; in quantum theory the Hamiltonian is normally a self-adjoint operator.

nodes.label: Lagrangian
nodes.summary: A function $L(q,\dot q,t)$ whose Euler–Lagrange equations determine classical trajectories.

nodes.label: Lagrangian density
nodes.summary: A local density whose spacetime integral gives the action for a classical or quantum field theory.

nodes.label: Canonical momentum
nodes.summary: The momentum $p_i=\partial L/\partial\dot q_i$ conjugate to a generalized coordinate.

nodes.label: Hamiltonian mechanics
nodes.summary: A phase-space formulation of classical mechanics in which observables evolve under a Hamiltonian through Poisson brackets.

sections.title: Core structure
sections.body: States are points of phase space, commonly a symplectic manifold, and the Hamiltonian generates time evolution.

nodes.label: Lagrangian mechanics
nodes.summary: A formulation of classical mechanics based on an action functional and the Euler–Lagrange equations.

sections.title: Core structure
sections.body: A Lagrangian encodes dynamics; stationary action yields the equations of motion. The formalism extends naturally to fields.

nodes.label: Phase space
nodes.summary: A state space carrying positions and conjugate momenta, ordinarily a symplectic manifold in Hamiltonian mechanics.

nodes.label: Poisson bracket
nodes.summary: The antisymmetric bracket on classical observables that generates Hamiltonian evolution and satisfies the Jacobi and Leibniz identities.

nodes.label: Stationary-action principle
nodes.summary: The physical history is a stationary point of the action under allowed variations; “stationary” need not mean globally least.

nodes.label: Euler–Lagrange equation
nodes.summary: The differential equation obtained by setting the first variation of an action to zero under fixed-boundary variations.

nodes.label: Newtonian mechanics
nodes.summary: The nonrelativistic classical mechanics of particles and forces in Euclidean space with absolute time.

nodes.label: Classical point particle
nodes.summary: An idealized object with finitely many degrees of freedom and no resolved internal spatial structure.

nodes.label: Spacetime
nodes.summary: The four-dimensional collection of physical events in which temporal and spatial relations are represented together.

sections.title: Relativity
sections.body: Special relativity uses flat spacetime; general relativity permits curved Lorentzian spacetime whose geometry is dynamical.

nodes.label: Special relativity
nodes.summary: The relativistic framework for nongravitational physics in inertial frames, with invariant light speed and Lorentz symmetry.

sections.title: Scope
sections.body: It neglects dynamical gravitation but constrains every relativistic local field theory, including the Standard Model.

nodes.label: General relativity
nodes.summary: Einstein’s classical theory of gravitation, in which gravity is represented by dynamical Lorentzian spacetime geometry.

sections.title: Core content
sections.body: Matter and non-gravitational fields source curvature; freely falling bodies follow the geometry rather than experiencing gravity as an ordinary force.

sections.title: Limits
sections.body: It is classical and is not a complete quantum theory of gravity.

nodes.label: Minkowski spacetime
nodes.summary: Flat four-dimensional spacetime equipped with the Lorentzian metric used by special relativity.

sections.title: Structure
sections.body: Its invariant interval and light-cone causal structure are preserved by Poincaré transformations.

nodes.label: Equivalence principle
nodes.summary: The local universality of free fall and local equivalence between gravitation and acceleration, in formulations appropriate to general relativity.

nodes.label: Gravitation
nodes.summary: The interaction described classically by general relativity as spacetime curvature.

sections.title: Standard Model boundary
sections.body: Gravitation is not included in the Standard Model of particle physics.

nodes.label: Lorentz symmetry
nodes.summary: Invariance or covariance under Lorentz transformations preserving the Minkowski metric.

nodes.label: Spacetime metric
nodes.summary: The Lorentzian metric that determines intervals, causal structure, geodesics, and in general relativity the gravitational geometry.

nodes.label: Four-vector
nodes.summary: A vector transforming in the defining representation of the Lorentz group.

nodes.label: Inertial frame
nodes.summary: A frame in which free particles move uniformly and the nongravitational laws take their special-relativistic form.

nodes.label: Poincaré symmetry
nodes.summary: The spacetime symmetry combining Lorentz transformations with translations in Minkowski spacetime.

nodes.label: Proper time
nodes.summary: The Lorentz-invariant time measured along a timelike worldline.

nodes.label: Stress–energy tensor
nodes.summary: The tensor encoding local energy density, momentum density, stresses, and fluxes that sources spacetime curvature.

nodes.label: Einstein field equation
nodes.summary: The field equation relating spacetime curvature to the stress–energy content of matter and non-gravitational fields.

sections.title: Schematic form
sections.body: The geometric tensor $G_{\mu\nu}$, optionally with a cosmological term, is proportional to the stress–energy tensor $T_{\mu\nu}$.

nodes.label: Energy–momentum four-vector
nodes.summary: The four-vector $p^\mu=(E/c,\mathbf p)$ satisfying the mass-shell relation for a free particle.

nodes.label: Geodesic motion
nodes.summary: Ideal freely falling test bodies follow timelike geodesics, while light rays follow null geodesics in the geometric-optics limit, when nongravitational forces, finite-wavelength effects, and self-force are neglected.

nodes.label: Relativistic particle mechanics
nodes.summary: Classical particle mechanics constrained by Minkowski spacetime and Lorentz invariance.

nodes.label: Weak-field gravity
nodes.summary: The expansion of general relativity about nearly flat spacetime when metric perturbations are small.

nodes.label: Newtonian gravitation
nodes.summary: The inverse-square gravitational theory recovered from general relativity in the weak-field, slow-motion regime.

nodes.label: Fine-structure constant
nodes.summary: The dimensionless electromagnetic coupling $\alpha=e^2/(4\pi\varepsilon_0\hbar c)$ in SI conventions, whose renormalized value runs with energy.

nodes.label: Classical electromagnetism
nodes.summary: The classical theory of electric and magnetic fields, charges, currents, radiation, and their Maxwell–Lorentz dynamics.

nodes.label: Electric four-current
nodes.summary: The four-vector $J^\mu=(c\rho,\mathbf J)$ combining charge density and electric current and sourcing Maxwell equations.

nodes.label: Electromagnetic field
nodes.summary: The antisymmetric field-strength tensor $F_{\mu\nu}$, or equivalently electric and magnetic fields relative to an observer.

nodes.label: Electromagnetic four-potential
nodes.summary: A spacetime one-form $A_\mu$ whose exterior derivative or curl is the electromagnetic field strength; gauge-related potentials represent the same local field strength.

nodes.label: Electric field
nodes.summary: The force-per-unit-charge field and time–space part of the electromagnetic field relative to an observer.

nodes.label: Magnetic field
nodes.summary: The spatial rotational part of the electromagnetic field relative to an observer, coupling to moving charges and magnetic moments.

nodes.label: Maxwell equations
nodes.summary: The differential equations relating electric and magnetic fields to charge and current and governing electromagnetic induction and radiation.

nodes.label: Electrostatics
nodes.summary: The approximately time-independent regime of classical electromagnetism for stationary charges.

nodes.label: Lorentz force law
nodes.summary: The classical force $q(\mathbf E+\mathbf v\times\mathbf B)$ on a point charge, or its covariant four-force form.

nodes.label: Coulomb law
nodes.summary: The inverse-square electrostatic force or potential between ideal point charges in vacuum.

nodes.label: Coulomb potential
nodes.summary: The electrostatic potential $V(r)=q_1q_2/(4\pi\varepsilon_0 r)$ used in nonrelativistic charged-particle Hamiltonians.

nodes.label: Quantum mechanics
nodes.summary: The framework governing physical systems whose states exhibit superposition, probabilistic measurement outcomes, and noncommuting observables.

sections.title: Mathematical core
sections.body: States are represented in a complex Hilbert space, observables by operators, and isolated-system evolution by unitary dynamics.

sections.title: Scope
sections.body: Nonrelativistic quantum mechanics is an effective framework; relativistic particle creation and annihilation require quantum field theory.

nodes.label: Quantum system
nodes.summary: A system described by quantum states, observables, probabilities, and quantum dynamics.

nodes.label: Quantum state
nodes.summary: In standard Hilbert-space quantum mechanics, a complete specification of a system’s statistical predictions: a ray (or vector representative) for a pure state, and more generally a positive trace-one density operator for a mixed state.

sections.title: Pure and mixed
sections.body: Pure states are represented by rays in Hilbert space; mixed states require density operators.

nodes.label: Mixed quantum state
nodes.summary: A non-extremal statistical quantum state represented by a positive trace-one density operator.

nodes.label: Pure quantum state
nodes.summary: An extremal quantum state represented by a ray in Hilbert space or a rank-one density operator.

nodes.label: Density operator
nodes.summary: A positive trace-one operator representing pure or mixed quantum states and reduced states of subsystems.

nodes.label: Quantum observable
nodes.summary: An observable represented in standard quantum mechanics by a self-adjoint operator, or more generally by a positive-operator-valued measure for a measurement.

sections.title: Noncommutativity
sections.body: Incompatible observables need not have simultaneously sharp values because their operators do not commute.

nodes.label: Wavefunction
nodes.summary: A coordinate representation of a quantum state, commonly a complex-valued amplitude over position or another configuration basis.

sections.title: Interpretation
sections.body: The wavefunction itself depends on basis and phase convention; the Born rule extracts probabilities from amplitudes.

nodes.label: Born rule
nodes.summary: The rule assigning probabilities from a quantum state and measurement operators, including $|\langle a|\psi\rangle|^2$ in the projective case.

nodes.label: Canonical commutation relations
nodes.summary: Relations such as $[Q_i,P_j]=i\hbar\delta_{ij}$ encoding canonical quantum kinematics in suitable representations.

nodes.label: Quantum measurement
nodes.summary: An interaction and outcome-description represented by projective measurements or, more generally, positive-operator-valued measures and quantum instruments.

nodes.label: Relativistic wave equations
nodes.summary: Single-particle relativistic wave equations such as Klein–Gordon and Dirac equations; a full interacting relativistic theory generally requires QFT.

nodes.label: Unitary time evolution
nodes.summary: Closed-system quantum evolution generated by a self-adjoint Hamiltonian through a unitary one-parameter group.

nodes.label: Dirac equation
nodes.summary: The first-order Lorentz-covariant equation for spinor fields, predicting spin-$1/2$ structure and antiparticle solutions.

nodes.label: Klein–Gordon equation
nodes.summary: The relativistic second-order wave equation for a scalar field, serving as a classical field equation and free scalar-QFT equation.

nodes.label: Quantum angular momentum
nodes.summary: The generators of spatial rotations satisfying the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ commutation relations.

nodes.label: Second-quantized formalism
nodes.summary: A Fock-space formalism using field, creation, and annihilation operators to represent variable occupation numbers; it is a reformulation for fixed particle species, not literally a second act of quantization in all uses.

nodes.label: Spin
nodes.summary: Intrinsic quantum angular momentum classified by representations of the rotation or Poincaré symmetry groups.

nodes.label: Uncertainty principle
nodes.summary: Bounds such as $\Delta A\Delta B\ge |\langle[A,B]\rangle|/2$, distinct from mere measurement disturbance.

nodes.label: Annihilation operator
nodes.summary: An operator lowering the occupation number of a mode, subject to bosonic commutation or fermionic anticommutation relations.

nodes.label: Creation operator
nodes.summary: An operator raising the occupation number of a mode, subject to bosonic commutation or fermionic anticommutation relations.

nodes.label: Identical quantum particles
nodes.summary: Particles of the same species are represented without individually observable labels, with states constrained by exchange statistics.

nodes.label: Nonrelativistic quantum mechanics
nodes.summary: Quantum mechanics for degrees of freedom with velocities small compared with $c$ and energies far below pair-production thresholds.

nodes.label: Orbital angular momentum
nodes.summary: The position–momentum angular momentum $\mathbf L=\mathbf r\times\mathbf p$ in nonrelativistic quantum mechanics.

nodes.label: Quantum number
nodes.summary: An eigenvalue or representation label used to classify quantum states under commuting observables and symmetries.

nodes.label: Spin one-half
nodes.summary: The two-dimensional irreducible representation of $SU(2)\cong\mathrm{Spin}(3)$, corresponding to a projective representation of $SO(3)$ and spin projections $\pm\hbar/2$ along a chosen axis.

nodes.label: Bose–Einstein statistics
nodes.summary: The symmetric exchange sector for identical bosons, yielding Bose–Einstein occupation statistics in applicable ensembles.

nodes.label: Fermi–Dirac statistics
nodes.summary: The antisymmetric exchange sector for identical fermions, yielding Fermi–Dirac occupation statistics in applicable ensembles and the Pauli exclusion consequence.

nodes.label: Occupation-number state
nodes.summary: A Fock-basis state labeled by the occupation number of each one-particle mode.

nodes.label: Pauli equation
nodes.summary: The nonrelativistic spin-$1/2$ equation coupling a two-component spinor to electromagnetic fields, obtained from the Dirac theory at low velocity.

nodes.label: Quantum bound state
nodes.summary: A normalizable state spatially confined by an interaction, typically associated with discrete spectrum below a continuum threshold.

nodes.label: Quantum harmonic oscillator
nodes.summary: The quantum system with a quadratic Hamiltonian. The standard one-dimensional oscillator has equally spaced energy levels and creation–annihilation operator structure.

nodes.label: Quantum scattering theory
nodes.summary: The analysis of asymptotic in/out states, cross sections, phase shifts, and transition amplitudes.

nodes.label: Scattering state
nodes.summary: An asymptotic or generalized state associated with continuum spectrum and unbound motion.

nodes.label: Schrödinger equation
nodes.summary: The Schrödinger-picture evolution equation $i\hbar\,\partial_t|\psi(t)\rangle=H|\psi(t)\rangle$; its concrete Hamiltonian may describe a nonrelativistic system or an effective quantum theory.

nodes.label: Many-body quantum mechanics
nodes.summary: Quantum mechanics of several or many interacting identical or distinguishable degrees of freedom.

nodes.label: Pauli exclusion principle
nodes.summary: No two identical fermions can occupy the same one-particle state, as a consequence of antisymmetry of the many-fermion state.

nodes.label: Quantum perturbation theory
nodes.summary: An expansion around a solvable Hamiltonian in powers of a small interaction or parameter.

nodes.label: Quantum variational method
nodes.summary: An approximation based on optimizing trial states, with the Rayleigh–Ritz bound for the ground-state energy.

nodes.label: Quantum field theory
nodes.summary: A framework in which fields are quantum degrees of freedom, supporting many-body and variable-particle-number descriptions. Relativistic QFT additionally imposes relativistic symmetry and causal locality and naturally accommodates antiparticles and scattering.

sections.title: Core ingredients
items: Quantum fields or local observables and a quantum state space.
Dynamics encoded by a Hamiltonian, action, or algebraic evolution law.
In relativistic formulations, Lorentz or spacetime symmetry and causal locality.
Correlation functions, response functions, or scattering observables, with renormalization where required.

sections.title: Scope
sections.body: Relativistic QFT underlies the Standard Model; nonrelativistic quantum field theories also provide effective descriptions of many-body and condensed-matter systems.

nodes.label: Gauge field theory
nodes.summary: A field theory with local gauge redundancy, whose gauge structure constrains interactions and introduces gauge fields.

sections.title: Mathematical structure
sections.body: Gauge theories are formulated using Lie groups and Lie algebras; globally, connections on principal bundles provide the geometric language.

nodes.label: Gauge redundancy
nodes.summary: A local redundancy in field variables: gauge-related configurations represent the same physical state, while global and boundary gauge transformations may carry physical charges.

nodes.label: Global physical symmetry
nodes.summary: A symmetry whose transformation parameters are not arbitrary functions of spacetime. Internal global symmetries act on fields at fixed spacetime points; spacetime symmetries are also global but act on spacetime itself.

nodes.label: Locality principle
nodes.summary: The requirement that physical influence and observables respect spacetime locality or causal separation in the theory’s precise formulation.

nodes.label: Quantum field
nodes.summary: A field degree of freedom in a quantum field theory; in common formulations fields are operator-valued distributions, while particle states arise from the theory’s excitations and asymptotic sectors.

sections.title: Particle relation
sections.body: In regimes with a useful particle interpretation, particle states are excitations of quantum fields; that interpretation can be observer- and background-dependent.

nodes.label: Abelian gauge theory
nodes.summary: A gauge theory with Abelian gauge group, lacking the pure-gauge self-couplings characteristic of non-Abelian Yang–Mills fields.

nodes.label: Canonical field quantization
nodes.summary: A procedure promoting canonical field variables and momenta to operators with commutation or anticommutation relations.

nodes.label: Gauge field
nodes.summary: A connection on a principal bundle or its local gauge potential, whose curvature is the field strength.

nodes.label: Local gauge invariance
nodes.summary: Invariance of the description under spacetime-dependent gauge transformations, implemented by gauge connections and constraints.

nodes.label: Matter field
nodes.summary: A quantum field carrying matter quantum numbers rather than serving as the gauge connection itself; its gauge representation may be fundamental, adjoint, or another representation depending on the theory.

nodes.label: Microcausality
nodes.summary: Local observables commute, or graded-commute for fields, at spacelike separation.

nodes.label: Noether theorem
nodes.summary: A continuous global symmetry of the action yields a conserved current on equations of motion, subject to boundary and gauge qualifications.

nodes.label: Non-Abelian gauge theory
nodes.summary: A gauge theory with noncommutative gauge group and self-interacting gauge fields.

nodes.label: Path-integral formulation
nodes.summary: A formulation of amplitudes and correlation functions as functional integrals, often defined perturbatively or through regulated Euclidean constructions.

nodes.label: Quantum field operator
nodes.summary: A spacetime-indexed operator-valued object; rigorously, fields are generally distributions that must be smeared with test functions.

nodes.label: Scalar field
nodes.summary: A field transforming as a Lorentz scalar; in QFT its quanta have spin zero.

nodes.label: Spinor field
nodes.summary: A field transforming in a spinor representation of the Lorentz spin group, used for fermionic matter.

nodes.label: Standard Model gauge group
nodes.summary: The local gauge group $SU(3)_C\times SU(2)_L\times U(1)_Y$, modulo possible finite central identifications, underlying the Standard Model interactions.

nodes.label: Vector field in physics
nodes.summary: A field transforming as a spacetime vector; gauge potentials are important examples but not every vector field is a gauge field.

nodes.label: Yang–Mills theory
nodes.summary: A non-Abelian gauge theory with curvature field strength and self-interacting gauge bosons.

nodes.label: Bosonic quantum field
nodes.summary: A physical quantum field whose particle excitations obey bosonic statistics under the spin–statistics assumptions; auxiliary ghost fields require separate treatment.

nodes.label: Effective field theory
nodes.summary: A QFT organized as all local operators allowed by chosen degrees of freedom and symmetries, ordered by powers of a high-energy scale.

nodes.label: Electroweak theory
nodes.summary: The unified gauge theory of weak and electromagnetic interactions before and through spontaneous electroweak symmetry breaking.

sections.title: Gauge structure
sections.body: The theory is based on $SU(2)_L \times U(1)_Y$ and yields the photon and massive $W^\pm$ and $Z$ bosons after symmetry breaking.

nodes.label: Fermionic quantum field
nodes.summary: A physical quantum field whose particle excitations obey fermionic statistics and whose canonical operators anticommute under the spin–statistics assumptions.

nodes.label: Free quantum field
nodes.summary: A quantum field theory with quadratic action and no interaction vertices, decomposable into independent oscillator modes.

nodes.label: Gauge fixing
nodes.summary: A choice that removes redundant gauge descriptions sufficiently to define propagators or quantization, while preserving physical gauge independence.

nodes.label: Gauge interaction
nodes.summary: Interactions fixed by replacing ordinary derivatives with gauge-covariant derivatives and by the gauge-field curvature terms.

nodes.label: Noether current
nodes.summary: The local current associated with a continuous global symmetry by Noether’s theorem, modulo improvement and gauge ambiguities.

nodes.label: Operator-valued distribution
nodes.summary: A distribution whose values act as operators on a state space, providing the mathematically appropriate local-field notion in many QFT frameworks.

nodes.label: Quantum chromodynamics
nodes.summary: The non-Abelian gauge theory of quarks and gluons and the fundamental strong interaction.

sections.title: Characteristic behavior
items: Color confinement prevents isolated quarks and gluons at ordinary energies.
Asymptotic freedom makes the interaction weaker at sufficiently high momentum transfer.

nodes.label: Scalar self-interaction
nodes.summary: A nonlinear scalar potential term, such as the quartic Higgs interaction, controlling scalar-field vacuum structure and self-coupling.

nodes.label: Spontaneous symmetry breaking
nodes.summary: A situation in which the dynamics has a symmetry but the chosen vacuum state does not, producing order parameters and, for global continuous symmetries, Goldstone modes.

nodes.label: Standard Model Lagrangian
nodes.summary: The gauge-invariant renormalizable Lagrangian containing gauge kinetic terms, chiral fermion kinetic terms, one Higgs doublet, Yukawa couplings, and the Higgs potential.

nodes.label: Vacuum state
nodes.summary: A lowest-energy or invariant state relative to a chosen Hamiltonian and spacetime structure; a unique particle vacuum need not exist in general curved spacetime.

nodes.label: Yukawa interaction
nodes.summary: A coupling between scalar and fermion fields; in the Standard Model, Yukawa matrices generate charged-fermion masses after electroweak symmetry breaking.

nodes.label: BRST symmetry
nodes.summary: A nilpotent graded symmetry encoding gauge invariance after gauge fixing and organizing physical states by cohomology.

nodes.label: Conserved charge
nodes.summary: A charge obtained by integrating the time component of a conserved current under suitable boundary conditions.

nodes.label: Faddeev–Popov ghost field
nodes.summary: An anticommuting auxiliary field introduced in covariant quantization of non-Abelian gauge theories; it does not represent an asymptotic physical particle.

nodes.label: Gluon gauge field
nodes.summary: The eight gauge-field components of $SU(3)_C$, transforming in the adjoint representation and self-interacting.

nodes.label: Higgs doublet field
nodes.summary: The complex scalar field transforming as an $SU(2)_L$ doublet with weak hypercharge $Y=1/2$ in the Standard Model. Its nonzero vacuum expectation value breaks electroweak symmetry.

nodes.label: Interacting quantum field
nodes.summary: A quantum field theory with nonquadratic couplings, requiring perturbative, lattice, bootstrap, algebraic, or other nonperturbative methods.

nodes.label: Perturbative quantum field theory
nodes.summary: A formal expansion in coupling constants or loops around a free or solvable theory, with domain controlled when couplings and kinematics permit.

nodes.label: Regularization
nodes.summary: A modification introducing a cutoff, dimension shift, lattice, or other regulator so divergent expressions become well-defined before renormalization.

nodes.label: Renormalization group
nodes.summary: The flow of couplings and operators with resolution scale, expressing how descriptions change under coarse-graining or scale transformations.

nodes.label: Standard Model chiral fermion multiplet
nodes.summary: A left- or right-chiral fermion field transforming in a specified representation of $SU(3)_C\times SU(2)_L\times U(1)_Y$.

nodes.label: Standard Model fermion field
nodes.summary: A quark or lepton field transforming chirally under the electroweak group and in a color representation for quarks.

nodes.label: Weak-hypercharge gauge field
nodes.summary: The $U(1)_Y$ gauge field coupling to weak hypercharge before electroweak symmetry breaking.

nodes.label: Weak-isospin gauge fields
nodes.summary: The three $SU(2)_L$ gauge fields coupling to left-handed weak-isospin doublets.

nodes.label: Asymptotic freedom
nodes.summary: The decrease of the QCD coupling at high momentum transfer, enabling perturbative calculations at short distances.

nodes.label: Brout–Englert–Higgs mechanism
nodes.summary: In a gauge theory with a symmetry-breaking scalar vacuum, gauge fields associated with broken generators acquire longitudinal modes and masses, while gauge fields of the unbroken subgroup remain massless.

sections.title: Qualification
sections.body: Most of the mass of ordinary matter is not directly supplied by the Higgs mechanism; proton and neutron masses arise predominantly from QCD dynamics.

nodes.label: Correlation function
nodes.summary: An expectation value of products of fields or observables, encoding propagation, response, and scattering information.

nodes.label: Electroweak symmetry breaking
nodes.summary: The Higgs vacuum reduces $SU(2)_L\times U(1)_Y$ to electromagnetic $U(1)_{\rm em}$, producing massive $W^\pm$ and $Z$ fields and a massless photon.

nodes.label: Gluon self-interaction
nodes.summary: Three-gluon and four-gluon interactions generated by the non-Abelian $SU(3)_C$ field-strength term.

nodes.label: Higgs vacuum expectation value
nodes.summary: The nonzero vacuum expectation value of the neutral Higgs component, setting the electroweak scale.

nodes.label: Left-handed lepton doublet field
nodes.summary: For each generation, a color-singlet $SU(2)_L$ doublet $L_L=(\nu_L,e_L)$ with weak hypercharge $-1/2$.

nodes.label: Left-handed quark doublet field
nodes.summary: For each generation, a color-triplet $SU(2)_L$ doublet $Q_L=(u_L,d_L)$ with weak hypercharge $1/6$.

nodes.label: Lepton field
nodes.summary: A color-singlet spinor field carrying electroweak quantum numbers and lepton flavor.

nodes.label: One-particle state
nodes.summary: A state in a one-particle representation or asymptotic sector associated with a stable particle species.

nodes.label: Quark field
nodes.summary: A color-triplet spinor field carrying flavor, electric charge, weak quantum numbers, and baryon number.

nodes.label: Quark–gluon interaction
nodes.summary: The QCD coupling of color-triplet quark fields to the gluon connection through the covariant derivative.

nodes.label: Renormalization
nodes.summary: The systematic relation between regulated parameters and finite observables, including counterterms and renormalization conditions.

nodes.label: Right-handed charged-lepton field
nodes.summary: For each generation, a color-singlet $SU(2)_L$ singlet $e_R$ with weak hypercharge $-1$. The minimal Standard Model has no right-handed neutrino field.

nodes.label: Right-handed down-type quark field
nodes.summary: For each generation, a color-triplet $SU(2)_L$ singlet $d_R$ with weak hypercharge $-1/3$.

nodes.label: Right-handed up-type quark field
nodes.summary: For each generation, a color-triplet $SU(2)_L$ singlet $u_R$ with weak hypercharge $2/3$.

nodes.label: Running coupling
nodes.summary: A renormalized interaction strength whose value depends on energy or length scale according to a beta function.

nodes.label: $Z$ field
nodes.summary: The massive neutral electroweak gauge field obtained by mixing the neutral weak-isospin and hypercharge fields.

nodes.label: Charged $W$ fields
nodes.summary: The charged combinations of weak-isospin gauge fields that mediate charged-current weak interactions.

nodes.label: Electroweak gauge-field mixing
nodes.summary: After electroweak symmetry breaking, the neutral $W^3_\mu$ and hypercharge $B_\mu$ fields mix into the photon and $Z$ fields.

nodes.label: Higgs field
nodes.summary: The physical scalar degree of freedom remaining from the Standard Model Higgs doublet after electroweak symmetry breaking; its quantum excitation is the Higgs boson.

nodes.label: Lattice QCD
nodes.conceptType: Regulated nonperturbative formulation and computational method
nodes.summary: A Euclidean spacetime lattice regularization of QCD enabling numerical path-integral calculations and continuum extrapolation.

nodes.label: Multiparticle state
nodes.summary: A Fock or scattering state containing several particle excitations, with exchange statistics and interactions treated appropriately.

nodes.label: Photon field
nodes.summary: The massless electromagnetic gauge field obtained from electroweak neutral-field mixing.

nodes.label: Propagator
nodes.summary: A two-point Green function or inverse kinetic operator with specified boundary prescription, not a literal particle trajectory.

nodes.label: Charge conjugation
nodes.summary: A transformation exchanging particle and antiparticle fields and conjugating internal charges; it need not be a symmetry of the full theory.

nodes.label: Feynman diagram
nodes.summary: A graph organizing terms in a perturbative expansion of correlation functions or amplitudes; internal lines are not directly observed particles.

nodes.label: Quantum electrodynamics
nodes.summary: The relativistic quantum field theory of the electromagnetic interaction between electrically charged fields and the photon field.

sections.title: Status
sections.body: QED is the electromagnetic sector of the broken electroweak theory and is extraordinarily well tested.

nodes.label: S-matrix
nodes.summary: The operator mapping asymptotic in-states to out-states when such asymptotic particle states exist.

nodes.label: Scattering amplitude
nodes.summary: A complex quantity whose squared magnitude and phase-space factors determine scattering probabilities and cross sections.

nodes.label: Wilsonian effective action
nodes.summary: An action for low-momentum modes obtained by integrating out higher-momentum degrees of freedom down to a cutoff scale.

nodes.label: Left-handed fermion field
nodes.summary: A field in a left-handed Weyl representation; Standard Model left-handed quarks and leptons form $SU(2)_L$ doublets.

nodes.label: Photon–fermion interaction
nodes.summary: The QED coupling $eQ\,\bar\psi\gamma^\mu\psi A_\mu$ between the photon field and an electrically charged fermion current.

nodes.label: Right-handed fermion field
nodes.summary: A right-handed Weyl field; charged right-handed Standard Model fermions are $SU(2)_L$ singlets.

nodes.label: Standard Model effective field theory
nodes.summary: An extension of the Standard Model Lagrangian by higher-dimension operators built from Standard Model fields and preserving its gauge symmetry, organized in inverse powers of a heavy new-physics scale. It is not obtained by integrating the Standard Model out of itself.

nodes.label: Fermi theory of weak interactions
nodes.summary: A local four-fermion theory approximating charged-current weak processes at momentum transfers far below the $W$-boson mass.

nodes.label: Low-energy QCD
nodes.summary: The strongly coupled regime of QCD where quarks and gluons are confined and hadrons are the useful degrees of freedom.

nodes.label: Four-fermion interaction
nodes.summary: A local operator involving four fermion fields, generated at low energy by integrating out a heavy mediator in cases such as Fermi theory.

nodes.label: Chiral perturbation theory
nodes.summary: The systematic low-energy expansion of QCD in momenta and light-quark masses using pions and, when included, nucleons as effective degrees of freedom.

nodes.label: Strong interaction
nodes.summary: The color interaction described by QCD; at hadronic and nuclear scales it also produces residual forces between color-neutral hadrons.

nodes.label: Weak mixing angle
nodes.summary: The electroweak mixing parameter $\theta_W$ relating gauge couplings and the neutral gauge-field combinations; its renormalized numerical value depends on scheme and scale.

nodes.label: Baryon number
nodes.summary: A perturbatively conserved Standard Model global number assigning $1/3$ to quarks and $1$ to baryons; nonperturbative electroweak effects violate $B+L$.

nodes.label: Chirality
nodes.summary: The left- or right-handed Weyl representation of the proper Lorentz group; for massive particles chirality is not identical to helicity.

nodes.label: CKM matrix
nodes.summary: The unitary matrix relating down-type quark weak-interaction eigenstates to mass eigenstates in charged-current interactions.

nodes.label: Color charge
nodes.summary: The $SU(3)_C$ quantum number carried by quarks and gluons; observable isolated states are color singlets.

nodes.label: Electric charge
nodes.summary: The charge generating electromagnetic $U(1)_{\rm em}$ and determining coupling to the photon.

nodes.label: Electromagnetic interaction
nodes.summary: The interaction of electrically charged matter and the electromagnetic field, described quantum mechanically by QED.

nodes.label: Lepton number
nodes.summary: A global quantum number assigned to leptons. Individual flavor numbers are violated by neutrino mixing; total lepton number is an accidental perturbative symmetry of the renormalizable Standard Model but participates in the nonperturbative $B+L$ anomaly and may be violated by Majorana masses or beyond-Standard-Model interactions.

nodes.label: Particle mass
nodes.summary: For a stable one-particle state, the invariant mass labels a Poincaré representation. Unstable resonances are characterized instead by a complex pole or a mass-and-width convention; composite masses include constituent, field, kinetic, and binding contributions.

nodes.label: PMNS matrix
nodes.summary: The lepton mixing matrix relating neutrino flavor states to neutrino mass eigenstates.

nodes.label: Standard Model of particle physics
nodes.summary: The renormalizable gauge quantum field theory with gauge group $SU(3)_C\times SU(2)_L\times U(1)_Y$, three observed fermion generations, one Higgs doublet, and the strong and electroweak interactions; gravity is not included.

sections.title: Field content
sections.body: Gauge fields for $SU(3)_C\times SU(2)_L\times U(1)_Y$, three generations of chiral quark and lepton multiplets, and one complex Higgs doublet.

sections.title: Interaction terms
items: Charged-current, neutral-current, and electroweak gauge-boson self-interactions.
Higgs self-coupling, Higgs–gauge couplings, and Yukawa couplings to fermions.

sections.title: Minimal-model qualification
sections.body: The minimal renormalizable Standard Model has no neutrino-mass term. Observed neutrino oscillations therefore require an extension, such as additional fields or higher-dimension operators.

sections.title: Known limitations
items: No established particle explanation of dark matter or dark energy.
Does not explain the number of generations, flavor parameters, baryon asymmetry, or the origin and nature of neutrino masses.

nodes.label: Weak hypercharge
nodes.summary: The $U(1)_Y$ charge related after symmetry breaking by $Q=T_3+Y$.

nodes.label: Weak interaction
nodes.summary: The interaction responsible for charged-current and neutral-current processes such as beta decay and neutrino scattering, described perturbatively in the Standard Model by couplings to the $W^\pm$ and $Z$ gauge fields.

nodes.label: Weak isospin
nodes.summary: The $SU(2)_L$ representation quantum number. Left-handed fermions and the Higgs field occur in nontrivial multiplets (doublets in the minimal Standard Model), while right-handed charged-fermion fields are singlets.

nodes.label: Antiparticle
nodes.summary: A particle state in the conjugate internal representation with opposite additive charges; a neutral particle may be its own antiparticle.

nodes.label: Boson
nodes.summary: A particle with integer spin and bosonic exchange statistics under the relativistic spin–statistics assumptions; the class includes gauge bosons and scalar bosons such as the Higgs.

nodes.label: Charged lepton
nodes.summary: A color-neutral spin-$1/2$ lepton with electric charge $-e$: electron, muon, or tau.

nodes.label: Charged-current weak interaction
nodes.summary: The weak interaction mediated perturbatively by $W^\pm$ fields, changing electric charge and fermion flavor within left-handed doublets.

nodes.label: Elementary particle
nodes.summary: A particle treated as having no resolved internal constituents in the Standard Model.

sections.title: Qualification
sections.body: “Elementary” is relative to current experimental resolution and theory; quarks and leptons are elementary in the Standard Model, while hadrons are composite.

nodes.label: Fermion
nodes.summary: A particle with half-integer spin obeying Fermi–Dirac statistics; Standard Model matter fields are fermionic.

nodes.label: Fermion generation
nodes.summary: A repeated family of Standard Model chiral matter representations. Three generations are observed; “generation” is a grouping of quark and lepton species, not itself a particle subtype.

nodes.label: Flavor
nodes.summary: The species label distinguishing quarks or leptons with the same gauge-role pattern but different masses and mixing.

nodes.label: Gauge boson
nodes.summary: A bosonic quantum associated with a gauge field: photons, gluons, and the $W$ and $Z$ bosons in the Standard Model.

nodes.label: Helicity
nodes.summary: The projection of spin along momentum; Lorentz invariant for massless particles but frame-dependent for massive particles.

nodes.label: Lepton
nodes.summary: A spin-one-half fermion that does not carry color charge; charged leptons and neutrinos occur in three generations.

nodes.label: Neutral-current weak interaction
nodes.summary: The weak interaction mediated perturbatively by the $Z$ field, coupling to flavor-diagonal neutral currents at tree level.

nodes.label: Neutrino mass
nodes.summary: Nonzero neutrino mass is established through oscillation measurements of mass-squared differences; the absolute mass scale and Dirac-versus-Majorana nature remain unresolved.

nodes.label: Neutrino mixing
nodes.summary: The mismatch between neutrino flavor and mass eigenstates encoded by the PMNS matrix.

nodes.label: Particle or field polarization
nodes.summary: The orientation or helicity state of a vector field, gauge boson, or wave relative to its propagation and reference frame.

nodes.label: Quark
nodes.summary: A color-charged spin-one-half fermion occurring in six flavors and confined into hadrons by QCD.

nodes.label: Quark flavor mixing
nodes.summary: Weak charged-current transitions between quark mass eigenstates with amplitudes set by the CKM matrix.

nodes.label: Antiquark
nodes.summary: The antiparticle of a quark, transforming in the conjugate color representation and carrying opposite additive quantum numbers.

nodes.label: Bottom quark
nodes.summary: A third-generation color-triplet quark with electric charge $-e/3$.

nodes.label: Charm quark
nodes.summary: A second-generation color-triplet quark with electric charge $+2e/3$.

nodes.label: Color confinement
nodes.summary: The absence of isolated color-charged asymptotic states and formation of color-singlet hadrons at ordinary energies.

nodes.label: Down quark
nodes.summary: A first-generation color-triplet quark with electric charge $-e/3$.

nodes.label: Electron
nodes.summary: The lightest charged lepton, with negative elementary electric charge and spin one-half.

nodes.label: First fermion generation
nodes.summary: The $u,d,e,\nu_e$ generation. Confined up- and down-quark fields underlie ordinary nucleons, while the electron is the stable charged lepton of ordinary atoms.

nodes.label: Gluon
nodes.summary: The massless spin-1 quantum of the QCD gauge field. The eight gluon field components transform in the adjoint representation of $SU(3)_C$ and carry color charge.
nodes.status: Experimentally established through hadronic and jet phenomena; not observed as an isolated asymptotic particle because of confinement

nodes.label: Higgs boson
nodes.summary: The spin-zero quantum excitation of the Higgs field, discovered in 2012.

nodes.label: Muon
nodes.summary: The second-generation charged lepton, unstable to weak decay.

nodes.label: Neutrino
nodes.summary: An electrically neutral lepton occurring in three flavors; observed flavor oscillations imply nonzero neutrino masses beyond the minimal massless-neutrino Standard Model.

nodes.label: Neutrino oscillation
nodes.summary: The distance- and energy-dependent change of neutrino flavor caused by coherent propagation of distinct mass eigenstates.

nodes.label: Photon
nodes.summary: The massless spin-one gauge boson of unbroken electromagnetic $U(1)$. Photon excitations form electromagnetic radiation states, and photon propagators organize electromagnetic interactions in perturbative QED.

nodes.label: Second fermion generation
nodes.summary: The $c,s,\mu,\nu_\mu$ generation, whose charged members are unstable.

nodes.label: Strange quark
nodes.summary: A second-generation color-triplet quark with electric charge $-e/3$.

nodes.label: Tau lepton
nodes.summary: The third-generation charged lepton, unstable to weak decay.

nodes.label: Third fermion generation
nodes.summary: The $t,b,\tau,\nu_\tau$ generation, whose charged members are unstable.

nodes.label: Top quark
nodes.summary: A third-generation color-triplet quark with electric charge $+2e/3$.

nodes.label: Up quark
nodes.summary: A first-generation color-triplet quark with electric charge $+2e/3$.

nodes.label: W boson
nodes.summary: A massive charged spin-one electroweak gauge boson whose field generates charged-current weak amplitudes.

nodes.label: Z boson
nodes.summary: A massive neutral spin-one electroweak gauge boson whose field generates neutral-current weak amplitudes.

nodes.label: Electron antineutrino
nodes.summary: The antiparticle flavor state produced with an electron in beta-minus decay and other charged-current processes.

nodes.label: Electron neutrino
nodes.summary: The neutrino flavor state produced with an electron in charged-current weak interactions.

nodes.label: Hadronization
nodes.summary: The conversion of energetic colored quarks and gluons into color-singlet hadrons.

nodes.label: Muon neutrino
nodes.summary: The neutrino flavor state produced with a muon in charged-current weak interactions.

nodes.label: Positron
nodes.summary: The electron antiparticle, with the same mass and spin and opposite electric charge.

nodes.label: Tau neutrino
nodes.summary: The neutrino flavor state produced with a tau in charged-current weak interactions.

nodes.label: Color-singlet state
nodes.summary: A state transforming trivially under global color, required for isolated observable hadrons.

nodes.label: Composite particle
nodes.summary: A particle-like bound or resonant state with resolvable internal degrees of freedom.

nodes.label: Constituent-quark model
nodes.summary: A hadron model using massive effective constituent quarks, encoding part of the surrounding QCD dressing rather than bare Lagrangian quarks.

nodes.label: Sea-quark degrees of freedom
nodes.summary: Quark–antiquark excitations in a hadron beyond the net valence content.

nodes.label: Valence-quark content
nodes.summary: The net quark flavor content fixing a hadron’s additive quantum numbers, distinct from its full quark–gluon state.

nodes.label: Hadron
nodes.summary: A color-singlet composite state of QCD, including baryons, mesons, and more general hadronic configurations; its mass and structure arise substantially from strongly interacting quark and gluon fields.

nodes.label: Baryon
nodes.summary: A hadron with baryon number $B=+1$ (or $B=-1$ for an antibaryon). Conventional baryons have net valence content of three quarks, while exotic baryons may contain additional quark–antiquark or gluonic components.

nodes.label: Meson
nodes.summary: A baryon-number-zero hadron with mesonic net valence quantum numbers, conventionally a quark–antiquark pair; exotic mesons may contain additional quark, antiquark, or gluonic components.

nodes.label: Residual strong interaction
nodes.summary: The color-singlet interaction between hadrons arising from QCD, analogous in role—but not form—to a residual interaction between neutral composites.

nodes.label: Nuclear effective field theory
nodes.summary: A low-energy expansion for nuclear interactions and currents using nucleons, pions or pionless degrees of freedom according to the scale.

nodes.label: Nucleon
nodes.summary: A proton or neutron, treated as a baryonic QCD bound state and as an effective degree of freedom in nuclei.

nodes.label: Pion
nodes.summary: The lightest meson isotriplet, central to low-energy QCD and the long-range part of the nuclear force.

nodes.label: Neutron
nodes.summary: A neutral baryon with valence content $udd$ plus gluon and sea-quark degrees of freedom; free neutrons are unstable to beta decay.

nodes.label: Nuclear force
nodes.summary: The effective interaction among nucleons, including two-nucleon and three-nucleon terms. Its long-range part is governed by pion exchange, while shorter-range operators are organized and fitted within nuclear effective field theory.

nodes.label: Nucleon–nucleon interaction
nodes.summary: The two-nucleon interaction extracted from scattering and constrained by QCD symmetries, forming a leading part of nuclear Hamiltonians.

nodes.label: Proton
