nodes.summary: The lightest baryon with electric charge $+e$, a QCD bound state with valence content $uud$ plus gluon and sea-quark degrees of freedom.

nodes.label: Antineutron
nodes.summary: The neutron antiparticle: electrically neutral, with baryon number $-1$, conjugate internal quantum numbers, and a magnetic moment opposite in sign to the neutron under standard conventions.

nodes.label: Antiproton
nodes.summary: The antiparticle of the proton, with opposite additive charges.

nodes.label: One-pion exchange
nodes.summary: The longest-range term in low-energy nucleon–nucleon interactions generated by pion dynamics; in perturbative diagrams it is represented by a pion propagator between nucleon vertices.

nodes.label: Three-nucleon force
nodes.summary: An irreducible effective interaction among three nucleons, required in nuclear EFT and precision nuclear structure beyond pairwise forces.

nodes.label: Nuclear Coulomb interaction
nodes.summary: The electrostatic repulsion among protons and electromagnetic corrections within a nucleus, competing with nuclear attraction and breaking isospin symmetry.

nodes.label: Nuclear potential
nodes.summary: A nonunique potential representation of nuclear interactions, dependent on resolution, regulator, and unitary conventions while preserving observables.

nodes.label: Nuclear many-body system
nodes.summary: A bound or resonant system of interacting protons and neutrons with internal excitations and collective modes.

nodes.label: Atomic nucleus
nodes.summary: The compact positively charged core of an atom, ordinarily composed of protons and neutrons bound by residual strong interactions.

nodes.label: Alpha particle
nodes.summary: A tightly bound helium-4 nucleus containing two protons and two neutrons.

nodes.label: Deuteron
nodes.summary: The bound proton–neutron nucleus of deuterium and the only bound two-nucleon system.

nodes.label: Mass number $A$
nodes.summary: The integer $A=Z+N$ counting nucleons in a nucleus.

nodes.label: Neutron number $N$
nodes.summary: The number of neutrons in a nucleus.

nodes.label: Nuclear spin
nodes.summary: The total angular momentum quantum number of a nuclear state, combining nucleon orbital and intrinsic spins.

nodes.label: Nuclear state
nodes.summary: A quantum state of a nucleus labeled by energy, angular momentum, parity, isospin-related quantities, and other quantum numbers.

nodes.label: Proton number $Z$
nodes.summary: The number of protons in a nucleus, determining the chemical element.

nodes.label: Liquid-drop model
nodes.summary: A coarse-grained nuclear model capturing volume, surface, Coulomb, asymmetry, and pairing contributions to masses and collective behavior.

nodes.label: Nuclear binding energy
nodes.summary: The energy required to separate a nucleus into free nucleons, equal to its mass defect times $c^2$.

nodes.label: Nuclear energy level
nodes.summary: A discrete or resonant nuclear excitation energy above the ground state.

nodes.label: Nuclear mean-field theory
nodes.summary: An approximation replacing much of the many-nucleon interaction by self-consistent one-body fields, often extended by pairing and correlations.

nodes.label: Nuclear shell model
nodes.summary: A model of nucleons moving in an effective mean field with residual interactions, organizing nuclear levels into shell-model configurations.

nodes.label: Nuclide
nodes.summary: A species of atom characterized by the numbers of protons and neutrons in its nucleus and, when needed, by the nuclear energy state.

nodes.label: Isotone
nodes.summary: Nuclides with the same neutron number $N$ but different proton number $Z$.

nodes.label: Isotope
nodes.summary: A member of a set of nuclides having the same atomic number but different mass numbers; equivalently, the same proton number but different neutron numbers.

nodes.label: Nuclear isobar
nodes.summary: Nuclides with the same mass number $A$ but different proton number $Z$.

nodes.label: Nuclear isomer
nodes.summary: A relatively long-lived excited state of a nuclide, distinguished from its ground state and shorter-lived excitations.

nodes.label: Nuclear mass defect
nodes.summary: The difference between the total rest mass of separated constituent nucleons and the measured nuclear mass.

nodes.label: Radioactive decay
nodes.summary: A transition of an unstable nuclear or particle state to lower-energy products with a characteristic probability per unit time.

nodes.label: Alpha decay
nodes.summary: Quantum tunneling emission of an alpha particle from a parent nucleus.

nodes.label: Beta decay
nodes.summary: A weak-interaction process changing nuclear charge through nucleon flavor conversion, including beta-minus, beta-plus, and related capture processes.

nodes.label: Gamma decay
nodes.summary: An excited nuclear state emits one or more photons or transfers energy internally to atomic electrons.

nodes.label: Beta-minus decay
nodes.summary: A neutron-rich system converts a neutron to a proton while emitting an electron and electron antineutrino.

nodes.label: Beta-plus decay
nodes.summary: A proton-rich system converts a proton to a neutron while emitting a positron and electron neutrino, when energetically allowed.

nodes.label: Electron capture
nodes.summary: A nucleus captures an atomic electron and converts a proton to a neutron while emitting an electron neutrino.

nodes.label: Nonrelativistic QED
nodes.summary: An effective field theory for nonrelativistic charged particles coupled to photons, organized in powers of velocity, $1/m$, and the fine-structure constant.

nodes.label: Atomic Hamiltonian
nodes.summary: The Hamiltonian describing nuclear and electronic kinetic energy plus electromagnetic interactions, with relativistic, finite-size, recoil, and QED refinements as required.

nodes.label: Electromagnetic atomic binding
nodes.summary: The binding of electrons to a positively charged nucleus through the electromagnetic interaction, modified by quantum statistics, relativity, nuclear structure, and QED.

nodes.label: Electron–electron Coulomb interaction
nodes.summary: The repulsive pair interaction among atomic electrons, responsible for much of many-electron structure and correlation.

nodes.label: Electron–nucleus Coulomb interaction
nodes.summary: The attractive Coulomb interaction between negatively charged electrons and the positive nuclear charge distribution.

nodes.label: Nonrelativistic Coulomb Hamiltonian
nodes.summary: The Schrödinger many-body Hamiltonian with kinetic energies and instantaneous Coulomb interactions among nuclei and electrons.

nodes.label: Center-of-mass separation
nodes.summary: Separation of overall translational motion from internal atomic motion; exact for isolated nonrelativistic systems with translation-invariant interactions.

nodes.label: Relativistic atomic structure
nodes.summary: Atomic structure based on Dirac electrons and relativistic electromagnetic interactions, increasingly important for high nuclear charge and precision.

nodes.label: Dirac–Coulomb Hamiltonian
nodes.summary: A many-electron Hamiltonian using one-electron Dirac operators and instantaneous Coulomb interactions, usually in the no-pair approximation.

nodes.label: Infinite-nuclear-mass approximation
nodes.summary: An approximation fixing the nucleus at the origin and neglecting recoil, controlled by the electron-to-nucleus mass ratio.

nodes.label: Reduced-mass treatment
nodes.summary: The exact two-body reduction or leading finite-nuclear-mass treatment replacing electron mass by electron–nucleus reduced mass.

nodes.label: Atomic QED corrections
nodes.summary: Radiative and vacuum effects from QED added to bound-state energies and transition amplitudes, including self-energy and vacuum polarization.

nodes.label: Breit interaction
nodes.summary: The leading frequency-independent transverse-photon correction to the instantaneous Coulomb interaction between electrons.

nodes.label: Chemical element
nodes.summary: The class of atoms and ions with the same proton number $Z$.

nodes.label: Nuclear recoil correction
nodes.summary: Corrections caused by nuclear motion, including reduced-mass and mass-polarization terms.

nodes.label: Atom
nodes.summary: An electrically neutral system consisting of a nucleus and bound electrons, identified chemically by the proton number of its nucleus.

nodes.label: Bound-electron self-energy
nodes.summary: The radiative correction to an electron propagator or bound-electron energy arising from virtual electron–photon interactions, after regularization and renormalization.

nodes.label: One-electron atomic system
nodes.summary: An atom or ion with a single bound electron, permitting an exact two-body Coulomb solution in the nonrelativistic point-nucleus model before recoil, finite-size, relativistic, and QED corrections.

nodes.label: Vacuum polarization
nodes.summary: A radiative correction in which charged-field loops modify the photon propagator and therefore the effective electromagnetic response, producing effects such as the Uehling potential.

nodes.label: Darwin term
nodes.summary: A contact-like correction in the low-energy expansion of the Dirac equation, affecting primarily states with nonzero density at the nucleus.

nodes.label: Electronic screening
nodes.summary: Reduction and reshaping of the effective nuclear attraction experienced by an electron due to the other electrons’ charge distribution and correlations.

nodes.label: Exchange interaction
nodes.summary: Energy and state-structure effects arising from antisymmetry of identical-fermion states; it is not an additional fundamental force.

nodes.label: Hydrogen atom
nodes.summary: The neutral one-proton, one-electron atom; its spectrum is the benchmark for quantum mechanics, relativity, nuclear effects, and QED.

nodes.label: Hydrogen-like ion
nodes.summary: An ion with one bound electron and nuclear charge $Z$, such as $He^+$.

nodes.label: Many-electron atom
nodes.summary: An atom with two or more electrons, requiring antisymmetrization and treatment of electron–electron interaction and correlation.

nodes.label: Orbital angular-momentum quantum number $l$
nodes.summary: The nonnegative integer labeling an orbital angular-momentum representation, with $l=0,\ldots,n-1$ for hydrogenic bound states.

nodes.label: Principal quantum number $n$
nodes.summary: The positive-integer radial/shell label for hydrogenic bound states and a principal shell label in central-field atomic descriptions.

nodes.label: Relativistic kinetic-energy correction
nodes.summary: The leading correction to nonrelativistic kinetic energy from expanding the relativistic energy–momentum relation.

nodes.label: Spin–orbit coupling
nodes.summary: Coupling between an electron’s spin and orbital motion in the electric field, contributing to fine structure.

nodes.label: Atomic orbital
nodes.summary: A one-electron wavefunction or basis function used in exact one-electron atoms and approximate many-electron descriptions; it is not a classical electron trajectory.

sections.title: Qualification
sections.body: Orbitals are not classical electron trajectories and are representation-dependent ingredients of atomic and molecular models.

nodes.label: Atomic state
nodes.summary: A stationary, metastable, resonance, or continuum state of the full atom, labeled by total angular momentum, parity, configuration, and other quantum numbers.

nodes.label: Central-field approximation
nodes.summary: An approximation replacing the nonspherical instantaneous many-electron interaction by an effective spherically symmetric one-electron potential.

nodes.label: Configuration-state function
nodes.summary: A symmetry-adapted linear combination of Slater determinants with specified angular momentum, spin, parity, or other quantum numbers.

nodes.label: Electron shell
nodes.summary: A group of one-electron states sharing a principal-shell label, especially a common principal quantum number in hydrogenic or central-field descriptions; it is a classification of states, not a literal spherical material layer.

nodes.label: Finite nuclear-size effect
nodes.summary: The shift of atomic levels caused by the extended nuclear charge distribution rather than an ideal point charge.

nodes.label: Independent-particle model
nodes.summary: An approximation representing a many-electron state using independently occupied one-electron orbitals in an effective field, with antisymmetry imposed for fermions.

nodes.label: Magnetic quantum number $m$
nodes.summary: The projection label of angular momentum along a chosen axis, ranging from $-j$ to $j$ in unit steps for angular momentum $j$.

nodes.label: Rutherford nuclear atom model
nodes.summary: A small positive nucleus with orbiting electrons; it established nuclear concentration of charge but lacks quantum stability and spectra.

nodes.label: Spin-projection quantum number $m_s$
nodes.summary: The projection of electron spin along a chosen axis, $m_s=\pm1/2$.

nodes.label: Atomic energy level
nodes.summary: A discrete energy eigenvalue or spectroscopically resolved level of an atom or atomic ion, including degeneracy and fine or hyperfine structure as appropriate.

nodes.label: Bohr model
nodes.summary: A semiclassical one-electron model with quantized circular orbits, reproducing the gross hydrogen spectrum but not general quantum structure.

nodes.label: Density-functional theory
nodes.conceptType: Ground-state many-body formulation and approximation family
nodes.summary: An exact ground-state density formulation in the Hohenberg–Kohn sense, implemented in practice through Kohn–Sham orbitals and approximate exchange–correlation functionals.

nodes.label: Electron configuration
nodes.summary: An occupation pattern over atomic orbitals or subshells used to organize many-electron basis states; the exact state can be a superposition of configurations.

nodes.label: Electron correlation
nodes.summary: Electronic motion beyond a chosen independent-particle or Hartree–Fock description, including dynamical and near-degeneracy correlation.

nodes.label: Electron subshell
nodes.summary: A grouping of one-electron states by principal and orbital angular-momentum quantum numbers, refined by spin–orbit coupling.

nodes.label: Hartree method
nodes.summary: A variational product-state mean-field method in which each electron moves in the average electrostatic field of the others; it omits exact exchange antisymmetry.

nodes.label: Hartree–Fock method
nodes.summary: A variational single-Slater-determinant method including exchange exactly within that determinant but omitting correlation beyond it.

nodes.label: jj coupling
nodes.summary: A coupling approximation in which each electron’s $l_i$ and $s_i$ first form $j_i$, after which the $j_i$ combine to total $J$.

nodes.label: LS coupling
nodes.summary: A coupling approximation in which individual orbital angular momenta combine to total $L$, individual spins to total $S$, and then $L$ and $S$ combine to total $J$.

nodes.label: Rydberg formula
nodes.summary: The leading hydrogenic relation between transition wavenumbers and principal quantum numbers, corrected in precision work for reduced mass, relativity, QED, and nuclear structure.

nodes.label: Total angular-momentum quantum number $J$
nodes.summary: The quantum number labeling total electronic angular momentum after coupling orbital and spin contributions.

nodes.label: Atomic fine structure
nodes.summary: Splittings from relativistic kinematics, spin–orbit coupling, and related relativistic electromagnetic terms, scaling roughly as powers of $Z\alpha$.

nodes.label: Atomic selection rule
nodes.summary: A condition causing a transition matrix element to vanish or be suppressed under an approximation and specified interaction multipole.

nodes.label: Atomic term symbol
nodes.summary: A compact label such as $^{2S+1}L_J$ for angular-momentum coupling, parity, and related atomic-state quantum numbers.

nodes.label: Configuration interaction
nodes.summary: A variational expansion of an atomic state in multiple configuration-state functions, recovering correlation within the chosen basis and excitation space.

nodes.label: Coupled-cluster method
nodes.summary: An exponential correlated-wavefunction method with systematic truncations such as singles and doubles, widely used for high-accuracy electronic structure.

nodes.label: Atomic hyperfine structure
nodes.summary: Splittings from interactions of electronic fields and angular momentum with nuclear magnetic dipole and electric quadrupole moments.

nodes.label: Atomic ionization
nodes.summary: Removal of one or more bound electrons by photons, collisions, fields, or other interactions.

nodes.label: Atomic spectrum
nodes.summary: Discrete and continuum electromagnetic absorption or emission frequencies determined by atomic energy differences and transition amplitudes.

nodes.label: Atomic transition
nodes.summary: A change between atomic states induced or accompanied by photon absorption, emission, collisions, or other interactions.

nodes.label: Lamb shift
nodes.summary: The QED-dominated splitting of levels that are degenerate in the Dirac–Coulomb approximation, notably hydrogen $2S_{1/2}$ and $2P_{1/2}$.

nodes.label: Atomic absorption
nodes.summary: A transition in which the atom gains energy from an electromagnetic quantum or classical field.

nodes.label: Atomic isotope shift
nodes.summary: The change of atomic transition frequency between isotopes due chiefly to nuclear-mass recoil and nuclear charge-radius differences.

nodes.label: Electric-dipole transition
nodes.summary: A transition governed at leading order by the electric dipole operator, with corresponding angular-momentum and parity selection rules.

nodes.label: Ion
nodes.summary: An atom or molecular entity carrying a net electric charge because its total number of electrons differs from its total nuclear charge.

nodes.label: Spontaneous emission
nodes.summary: Decay of an excited atomic state by coupling to vacuum electromagnetic modes, with photon emission when allowed.

nodes.label: Stark effect
nodes.summary: Splitting and shifting of atomic levels in an applied electric field.

nodes.label: Stimulated emission
nodes.summary: Emission induced by an incident electromagnetic field into an already occupied mode or matching frequency.

nodes.label: Zeeman effect
nodes.summary: Splitting and shifting of atomic levels in an applied magnetic field.

nodes.label: Anion
nodes.summary: A negatively charged atom or molecule with more electrons than total nuclear charge.

nodes.label: Cation
nodes.summary: A positively charged atom or molecule with fewer electrons than total nuclear charge.

nodes.label: Molecule
nodes.summary: An electrically neutral entity consisting of more than one atom; its bound structure and spectra arise from quantum states of electrons and nuclei.

nodes.label: Causal structure
nodes.summary: The chronological and causal reachability relations determined by a spacetime metric. Causal reachability is a partial order only under suitable causality conditions, such as the absence of closed causal curves.

nodes.label: CPT theorem
nodes.summary: A broad class of local Lorentz-invariant quantum field theories with standard unitarity and spectral assumptions is invariant under the combined action of charge conjugation, parity, and time reversal.

nodes.label: Electroweak gauge-boson self-interaction
nodes.summary: Triple and quartic gauge-boson interactions generated by the non-Abelian $SU(2)_L$ field strength; after electroweak mixing they include vertices such as $WW\gamma$, $WWZ$, and quartic counterparts.

nodes.label: Energy
nodes.summary: A conserved generator associated with time-translation symmetry in closed time-independent systems; its concrete representation and localization depend on the theory.

nodes.label: Force
nodes.summary: In Newtonian mechanics, the rate of change of momentum; in more general formulations interactions need not be represented by a fundamental force vector.

nodes.label: Four-velocity
nodes.summary: The tangent vector $u^\mu=dx^\mu/d\tau$ to a timelike worldline, normalized by the spacetime metric according to convention.

nodes.label: Gauge-anomaly cancellation
nodes.summary: Cancellation of all local gauge anomalies among chiral fermion representations, required for a consistent quantum gauge theory; the Standard Model representation assignments satisfy these constraints.

nodes.label: Higgs–gauge interaction
nodes.summary: The coupling of the Higgs doublet to electroweak gauge fields through its covariant derivative; after symmetry breaking it produces $W$ and $Z$ mass terms and Higgs couplings to those bosons.

nodes.label: Light cone
nodes.summary: At an event, the null directions of the Lorentzian metric separating timelike from spacelike directions and determining possible light propagation.

nodes.label: Linear momentum
nodes.summary: The conserved generator associated with spatial translations in translation-invariant systems; in Newtonian particle mechanics it is $\mathbf p=m\mathbf v$.

nodes.label: Newton’s laws of motion
nodes.summary: The inertial, dynamical, and action–reaction laws of Newtonian particle mechanics, valid in inertial frames within its nonrelativistic classical regime.

sections.title: Scope
sections.body: These laws are not fundamental across all regimes: relativistic, quantum, field-theoretic, dissipative, and constrained systems require more general formulations.

nodes.label: Ordinary differential equation
nodes.summary: An equation relating an unknown function of one independent variable to its derivatives.
nodes.notes: An ODE may be linear or nonlinear; existence and uniqueness require additional hypotheses.

nodes.label: Physical event
nodes.summary: An idealized occurrence localized at a point of spacetime.

nodes.label: Quantum anomaly
nodes.summary: Failure of a classical symmetry to survive quantization or regularization; global anomalies can encode real physics, while uncancelled gauge anomalies make a gauge theory inconsistent.

nodes.label: Quantum decoherence
nodes.summary: Suppression of interference in a subsystem’s reduced state through entanglement with uncontrolled environmental degrees of freedom; decoherence does not by itself select a unique measurement outcome.

nodes.label: Quantum entanglement
nodes.summary: A composite quantum state is entangled when it is not separable into a mixture of product states across the chosen subsystem partition.

nodes.label: Quantum superposition
nodes.summary: A linear combination of state vectors representing another possible pure state within the same superselection sector; relative phases can produce interference.

nodes.label: Smooth curve
nodes.summary: A smooth map from an interval or one-dimensional manifold into a smooth manifold.

nodes.label: Spin–statistics theorem
nodes.summary: Under the locality, relativistic covariance, positive-energy, and Hilbert-space assumptions of standard relativistic QFT, integer-spin fields have bosonic statistics and half-integer-spin fields have fermionic statistics.

nodes.label: Tangent vector
nodes.summary: An element of the tangent space at a point of a smooth manifold, equivalently a velocity of a curve or a derivation at that point.
data: derivation at $p$ or equivalence class of curves through $p$
axioms: linearity and Leibniz rule in the derivation model
nodes.notes: The curve and derivation constructions are canonically equivalent for finite-dimensional smooth manifolds.

nodes.label: Worldline
nodes.summary: A timelike or null curve representing the spacetime history of an idealized particle or light signal; extended bodies require worldtubes or field descriptions.

nodes.label: Continuity equation
nodes.summary: A local conservation equation of the form $\partial_t\rho+\nabla\cdot\mathbf j=0$; in flat relativistic spacetime it is $\partial_\mu j^\mu=0$, while on curved spacetime the corresponding form is $\nabla_\mu j^\mu=0$.

nodes.label: Mass–energy equivalence
nodes.summary: The invariant mass of an isolated system equals its total rest-frame energy divided by $c^2$; binding, kinetic, field, and internal energies therefore contribute to composite mass.

nodes.label: Binding energy
nodes.summary: The energy required to separate a bound system into specified free constituents; equivalently, the bound state lies below that breakup threshold and has a corresponding mass deficit in its rest frame.

nodes.label: Gauge-covariant derivative
nodes.summary: A derivative $D_\mu=\partial_\mu+A_\mu$ in mathematical convention, or with coupling and representation factors in physics convention, that differentiates charged fields while transforming covariantly under local gauge transformations.

nodes.label: Gauge field strength
nodes.summary: The curvature $F=dA+A\wedge A$ of a gauge connection; its Abelian specialization is the electromagnetic field-strength tensor, while non-Abelian theories contain gauge self-interactions.

nodes.label: Goldstone theorem
nodes.summary: Under its relativistic-QFT assumptions, spontaneous breaking of a continuous global symmetry implies gapless Nambu–Goldstone excitations, one per broken generator subject to the theorem’s qualifications.

nodes.label: Nambu–Goldstone mode
nodes.summary: A gapless mode associated with spontaneous breaking of a continuous global symmetry; explicit breaking generally gives a pseudo-Nambu–Goldstone mode a nonzero mass.

nodes.label: Longitudinal massive-gauge-boson mode
nodes.summary: The third physical polarization of a massive vector boson. In a Higgs phase, degrees of freedom represented as would-be Goldstone modes in a gauge-fixed description reorganize into longitudinal massive-gauge-boson polarizations.

nodes.label: Low-energy effective field theory below the electroweak scale (LEFT)
nodes.summary: The effective field theory below the electroweak scale after integrating out the $W$, $Z$, Higgs, and top quark. It contains QCD and QED for light fields plus higher-dimension weak and possible beyond-Standard-Model operators.

nodes.label: Approximate chiral symmetry of QCD
nodes.summary: For light-quark masses small compared with the strong scale, the QCD Lagrangian has an approximate $SU(N_f)_L\times SU(N_f)_R$ flavor symmetry, apart from anomalous and mass effects.

nodes.label: Spontaneous chiral-symmetry breaking in QCD
nodes.summary: The low-energy QCD vacuum does not preserve the approximate light-quark chiral symmetry, producing a quark condensate and light pseudo-Nambu–Goldstone mesons.

nodes.label: Quark condensate
nodes.summary: The vacuum expectation value $\langle\bar q q\rangle$, an order parameter for spontaneous chiral-symmetry breaking in the chiral limit; its numerical value depends on renormalization scheme and scale.

nodes.label: Pseudo-Nambu–Goldstone mode
nodes.summary: A would-be Goldstone mode that acquires a nonzero mass because the corresponding symmetry is explicitly as well as spontaneously broken; the light pions are the principal QCD example.

nodes.label: Yang–Mills mass gap
nodes.conceptType: Expected nonperturbative property / open mathematical problem
nodes.summary: Pure four-dimensional confining quantum Yang–Mills theory is expected to have a positive energy gap above its vacuum. Constructing the continuum theory rigorously and proving the gap remains an open Clay Millennium problem. This must not be conflated with exact chiral-limit QCD, whose spontaneously broken chiral symmetry gives massless Nambu–Goldstone modes.

sections.title: Distinction from QCD
sections.body: Physical QCD with nonzero light-quark masses has a gapped hadron spectrum. In the exact massless-light-quark limit, however, spontaneous chiral-symmetry breaking produces massless pions, so the full theory does not have a positive spectral gap. The Clay problem concerns pure Yang–Mills theory.

sections.title: Mathematical status
sections.body: A satisfactory solution must construct a nontrivial four-dimensional quantum Yang–Mills theory with appropriate axiomatic properties and prove a strictly positive mass gap.

nodes.label: Isospin
nodes.summary: An approximate $SU(2)$ flavor symmetry treating up and down quarks, and correspondingly proton and neutron, as multiplet components when electromagnetic effects and the up–down mass difference are neglected.

nodes.label: Electromagnetic wave
nodes.summary: A propagating solution of Maxwell’s equations in which electric and magnetic fields vary together and carry energy and momentum.

nodes.label: Electromagnetic radiation
nodes.summary: Energy and momentum carried by propagating electromagnetic fields. Classical radiation is described by Maxwell fields; quantum radiation is described by photon-field states that need not have a definite photon number.

nodes.label: Ground state
nodes.summary: A state of minimum energy for a specified Hamiltonian or sector; degeneracy is possible, and some systems have no normalizable ground state.

nodes.label: Excited state
nodes.summary: A state with energy above the ground state of the specified Hamiltonian; it may be stationary, metastable, resonant, or unstable.

nodes.label: Parity
nodes.summary: The eigenvalue under spatial inversion when parity is a symmetry. Atomic and nuclear states are commonly labeled by parity, and transition operators impose parity selection rules.

nodes.label: Ionization energy
nodes.summary: The minimum energy required to remove an electron from an atom or ion in its ground state, for a specified charge state and final channel.

nodes.label: Operator commutator
nodes.summary: For operators $A$ and $B$ with a common meaningful domain, the commutator is $[A,B]=AB-BA$; domain issues are essential for unbounded operators.
axioms: defined only where both compositions make sense
nodes.notes: For unbounded operators, domain questions are essential.

nodes.label: Operator anticommutator
nodes.summary: For operators $A$ and $B$ with defined products, the anticommutator is $\{A,B\}=AB+BA$.
axioms: defined only where both compositions make sense
induces: Clifford and fermionic canonical anticommutation relations
nodes.notes: For unbounded operators, domain questions are essential.

nodes.label: Direct sum of vector spaces
nodes.summary: The direct sum $\bigoplus_i V_i$ consists of tuples with finite support in the algebraic case; Hilbert direct sums complete square-summable families under the natural inner product.
axioms: only finitely many nonzero components in the algebraic direct sum
nodes.notes: The Hilbert direct sum is a different completed construction using square-summable families.

nodes.label: Quantum expectation value
nodes.summary: For a state $\rho$ and observable $A$, the expectation value is $\langle A\rangle_\rho=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)$ when defined; for a pure vector state it reduces to $\langle\psi|A|\psi\rangle$.

nodes.label: Antineutrino
nodes.summary: A neutral-lepton state produced in the charge-conjugate charged-current channel to a neutrino. Whether neutrino and antineutrino are fundamentally distinct Dirac particles or Majorana manifestations of one field remains experimentally unresolved.

nodes.label: Neutrino flavor state
nodes.summary: An electron-, muon-, or tau-flavor state defined by the charged-current interaction. Flavor states are coherent superpositions of neutrino mass eigenstates.

nodes.label: Neutrino mass eigenstate
nodes.summary:
One of the propagation eigenstates conventionally labeled $
u_1,
u_2,
u_3$, with definite mass in vacuum. Their coherent phases and PMNS amplitudes generate flavor oscillation.

nodes.label: Muon antineutrino
nodes.summary: The antineutrino flavor state associated with the muon charged-current channel.

nodes.label: Tau antineutrino
nodes.summary: The antineutrino flavor state associated with the tau charged-current channel.

nodes.label: Galileo’s inclined-plane experiments
nodes.summary: Galileo used inclined planes to slow free fall enough to measure approximately uniform acceleration and to replace Aristotelian motion with quantitative kinematics.

sections.title: Historical role
sections.body: The experiments helped establish mathematical laws of accelerated motion that became inputs to Newtonian mechanics; they did not by themselves contain Newton’s later dynamical laws.

nodes.label: Cavendish torsion-balance experiment
nodes.summary: Cavendish’s 1798 torsion-balance measurements detected gravitational attraction between laboratory masses and determined the mean density of Earth.

sections.title: Result
sections.body: The experiment supplied a terrestrial quantitative test of universal Newtonian gravitation; the modern value of $G$ is inferred when the result is expressed in later notation.

nodes.label: Young’s double-slit experiment
nodes.summary: Young’s early nineteenth-century interference experiment showed that light intensities form fringes when coherent paths overlap, providing strong evidence for a wave description of light.

sections.title: Scope
sections.body: This historical optical experiment is distinct from later single-particle double-slit experiments in quantum mechanics.

nodes.label: Ørsted’s compass experiment
nodes.summary: Ørsted observed in 1820 that an electric current deflects a nearby compass needle, establishing an empirical link between electricity and magnetism.

nodes.label: Faraday’s induction experiments
nodes.summary: Faraday’s 1831 experiments showed that changing magnetic flux induces an electromotive effect and introduced field-based patterns that Maxwell later mathematized.

nodes.label: Fizeau moving-water experiment
nodes.summary: Fizeau measured the speed of light in moving water in 1851, obtaining partial ether-drag behavior later explained by relativistic velocity addition.

nodes.label: Mercury perihelion anomaly
nodes.summary: Nineteenth-century orbital analyses found a residual advance of Mercury’s perihelion not accounted for by known Newtonian perturbations.

nodes.label: Michelson–Morley experiment
nodes.summary: The 1887 interferometer experiment found no ether-wind fringe shift of the expected magnitude, sharply constraining stationary luminiferous-ether models.

nodes.label: Hertz electromagnetic-wave experiments
nodes.summary: Hertz generated and detected radio-frequency electromagnetic waves in the late 1880s, confirming central wave predictions of Maxwellian electrodynamics.

nodes.label: Eötvös torsion-balance experiments
nodes.summary: Eötvös and collaborators compared the accelerations of bodies of different composition, tightly testing equality of inertial and gravitational mass.

nodes.label: 1919 eclipse light-deflection observations
nodes.summary: Eclipse expeditions in 1919 measured the apparent displacement of stars near the Sun and were interpreted as supporting Einstein’s predicted gravitational deflection of light.

sections.title: Qualification
sections.body: The 1919 data were historically influential but less precise than later radio and optical measurements of light deflection.

nodes.label: Kennedy–Thorndike experiment
nodes.summary: The 1932 unequal-arm interferometer test constrained changes in light speed associated with Earth’s changing velocity and, together with Michelson–Morley, tested Lorentz transformations.

nodes.label: Ives–Stilwell experiment
nodes.summary: Ives and Stilwell measured the transverse Doppler effect using moving ions, providing an early quantitative test of relativistic time dilation.

nodes.label: Pound–Rebka experiment
nodes.summary: The 1959–1960 Mössbauer experiment measured the gravitational frequency shift of gamma rays over a vertical height in Earth’s field.

nodes.label: Shapiro time-delay measurement
nodes.summary: Radar ranging to planets measured the extra propagation time of signals passing near the Sun, testing the relativistic gravitational time delay.

nodes.label: Hulse–Taylor binary-pulsar observations
nodes.summary: Long-term timing of PSR B1913+16 revealed orbital decay agreeing with general-relativistic energy loss by gravitational radiation.

nodes.label: GW150914 gravitational-wave detection
nodes.summary: LIGO observed a transient waveform from a binary-black-hole merger in 2015, the first direct detection of gravitational waves and a strong-field test of general relativity.

nodes.label: Balmer hydrogen-spectrum observations
nodes.summary: The visible hydrogen lines summarized by Balmer’s 1885 formula exhibited a regular discrete spectrum that classical atomic models could not explain.

sections.title: Historical role
sections.body: Hydrogen spectroscopy motivated empirical spectral formulas and later the Bohr model; modern quantum mechanics explains the levels and transition amplitudes.

nodes.label: Perrin Brownian-motion experiments
nodes.summary: Jean Perrin’s quantitative studies of Brownian particles tested Einstein’s statistical theory, estimated Avogadro’s number by several methods, and supplied strong evidence for molecular and atomic reality.

nodes.label: Anomalous Zeeman-effect observations
nodes.summary: Spectral-line splittings more complex than the normal Zeeman triplet resisted orbital explanations and became an important clue toward electron spin and modern angular-momentum theory.

nodes.label: Blackbody spectrum and ultraviolet catastrophe
nodes.summary: Measured blackbody spectra remained finite at high frequency, while classical equipartition produced the divergent Rayleigh–Jeans prediction known as the ultraviolet catastrophe.

nodes.label: Photoelectric-effect experiments
nodes.summary: Photoelectron energies depend on light frequency rather than intensity alone and show a threshold frequency, behavior explained by quantized light energy.

nodes.label: Thomson cathode-ray experiments
nodes.summary: J. J. Thomson’s deflection measurements showed that cathode rays consist of negatively charged particles with a common charge-to-mass ratio, establishing the electron as a constituent of matter.

nodes.label: Millikan oil-drop experiment
nodes.summary: Millikan and collaborators measured charges on suspended droplets and found them in integer multiples of an elementary charge, enabling a precision value of $e$.

nodes.label: Geiger–Marsden gold-foil experiment
nodes.summary: Large-angle alpha-particle scattering from thin foils contradicted diffuse-charge atomic models and led Rutherford to a compact, positively charged nucleus.

nodes.label: Moseley X-ray spectroscopy
nodes.summary: Moseley found that characteristic X-ray frequencies track an integer nuclear charge, establishing atomic number as a physical ordering principle.

nodes.label: Aston mass-spectrograph measurements
nodes.summary: Aston separated isotopes by mass-to-charge ratio and established isotope masses and packing-fraction regularities central to nuclide and binding-energy systematics.

nodes.label: Franck–Hertz experiment
nodes.summary: Electrons lose energy to mercury atoms in discrete increments, providing direct evidence for quantized atomic excitation energies.

sections.title: Historical qualification
sections.body: Franck and Hertz initially interpreted the observed threshold as ionization; its later interpretation as discrete excitation energy supplied the canonical quantum-level test.

nodes.label: Stern–Gerlach experiment
nodes.summary: A beam of silver atoms split into discrete components in an inhomogeneous magnetic field, demonstrating space quantization and later becoming a canonical manifestation of spin-$1/2$.

nodes.label: Compton scattering experiment
nodes.summary: X-ray scattering exhibited a wavelength shift determined by scattering angle, quantitatively supporting photon energy and momentum.

nodes.label: Davisson–Germer electron-diffraction experiment
nodes.summary: Electrons scattered from a nickel crystal produced diffraction peaks with the de Broglie wavelength, directly demonstrating matter-wave behavior.

nodes.label: Single-particle double-slit experiments
nodes.summary: Electron, neutron, atom, and molecule experiments build interference patterns from individually detected particles, displaying superposition amplitudes and probabilistic detection.

nodes.label: Einstein–Podolsky–Rosen argument
nodes.summary: The 1935 EPR argument used entangled correlations to challenge the completeness of quantum mechanics under locality and separability assumptions.

nodes.label: Bell-test experiments
nodes.summary: Bell tests measure correlations between separated entangled systems and violate Bell inequalities, excluding broad classes of local hidden-variable models under the tested assumptions.

nodes.label: Aharonov–Bohm interference experiments
nodes.summary: Electron-interference phases respond to enclosed magnetic flux even when the electrons traverse regions with negligible magnetic field, testing the gauge-potential structure of quantum mechanics.

nodes.label: Lamb–Retherford experiment
nodes.summary: Microwave spectroscopy showed that hydrogen’s $2S_{1/2}$ and $2P_{1/2}$ levels are not degenerate, revealing the Lamb shift and driving renormalized QED calculations.

nodes.label: Electron anomalous-magnetic-moment measurements
nodes.summary: Measurements of the electron magnetic-moment anomaly, compared with high-order calculations, provide one of the most precise quantitative tests of QED.

nodes.label: Casimir-force measurements
nodes.summary: Measurements of forces between closely spaced conductors agree with QED calculations of boundary-dependent electromagnetic fluctuations and material response.

sections.title: Qualification
sections.body: The Casimir effect tests QED predictions for interacting boundaries; it is not by itself a unique measurement of an absolute vacuum energy.

nodes.label: Cavity-QED decoherence experiments
nodes.summary: Controlled cavity experiments tracked the loss of coherence in superpositions coupled to an environment, directly testing quantitative decoherence models.

nodes.label: Hong–Ou–Mandel experiment
nodes.summary: Two indistinguishable photons entering a balanced beam splitter from different inputs bunch into the same output, producing the Hong–Ou–Mandel dip.

nodes.label: Fullerene matter-wave interference
nodes.summary: Interference of $C_{60}$ molecules extended matter-wave superposition to large composite particles and enabled quantitative study of environmental decoherence.

nodes.label: Proton-radius puzzle
nodes.summary: Muonic-hydrogen spectroscopy initially inferred a proton charge radius significantly smaller than the value from ordinary hydrogen and electron scattering, motivating renewed recoil, finite-size, and radiative analyses.

nodes.label: Continuous beta-spectrum problem
nodes.summary: Measured beta-decay electron spectra were continuous, creating an apparent energy-and-momentum conservation problem before the neutrino hypothesis and Fermi’s theory.

nodes.label: Positron discovery in cloud-chamber tracks
nodes.summary: Anderson identified positively curved electron-like cloud-chamber tracks in cosmic rays, establishing the positron predicted by relativistic electron theory.

nodes.label: Chadwick neutron experiment
nodes.summary: Chadwick showed that penetrating radiation from alpha-bombarded beryllium consisted of neutral particles with mass near the proton mass, establishing the neutron.

nodes.label: Muon discovery in cosmic rays
nodes.summary: Cloud-chamber cosmic-ray tracks revealed a charged particle heavier than the electron and lighter than the proton, later identified as the muon.

nodes.label: Pion discovery in nuclear emulsions
nodes.summary: Nuclear-emulsion observations identified the pion and its decay to the muon, establishing the light meson associated with the long-range nuclear interaction.

nodes.label: Cowan–Reines reactor-neutrino experiment
nodes.summary: Inverse-beta events near a nuclear reactor provided the first direct detection of the electron antineutrino.

nodes.label: Wu parity experiment
nodes.summary: Angular correlations in polarized cobalt-60 beta decay showed that the weak interaction violates spatial parity.

nodes.label: Goldhaber neutrino-helicity experiment
nodes.summary: Goldhaber, Grodzins, and Sunyar inferred the neutrino’s negative helicity from recoil-free nuclear capture and gamma-ray polarization correlations.

nodes.label: Brookhaven muon-neutrino experiment
nodes.summary: A high-energy neutrino beam produced muons but not electrons at the expected rate, establishing the muon neutrino as distinct from the electron neutrino.

nodes.label: Kaon CP-violation experiment
nodes.summary: Cronin and Fitch’s group observed the nominally CP-forbidden decay of the long-lived neutral kaon into two pions, establishing CP violation.

nodes.label: Solar-neutrino deficit
nodes.summary: Radiochemical solar-neutrino experiments detected substantially fewer electron neutrinos than predicted by solar models, creating the solar-neutrino problem.

nodes.label: SLAC deep-inelastic scattering experiments
nodes.summary: High-energy electron scattering from nucleons revealed approximately pointlike charged constituents and scaling behavior, establishing partonic nucleon structure and driving quark acceptance.

nodes.label: Gargamelle neutral-current discovery
nodes.summary: The Gargamelle bubble chamber observed weak neutrino interactions without charged leptons, establishing neutral-current weak interactions predicted by electroweak theory.

nodes.label: $J/\psi$ discovery and the November Revolution
nodes.summary: Independent discoveries of a narrow $J/\psi$ resonance in 1974 established charmonium and transformed acceptance of the quark model and Standard Model.

nodes.label: Tau-lepton discovery
nodes.summary: Electron–positron collision events with missing energy revealed the tau, establishing a third charged-lepton species.

nodes.label: Upsilon and bottom-quark discovery
nodes.summary: A narrow dimuon resonance near $9.5\,\mathrm{GeV}$ revealed bottomonium and established the bottom-quark flavor.

nodes.label: PETRA three-jet gluon evidence
nodes.summary: Three-jet electron–positron events at PETRA displayed hard gluon radiation and supplied direct evidence for the gluon and QCD’s vector gauge dynamics.

nodes.label: UA1 and UA2 discovery of the $W$ and $Z$ bosons
nodes.summary: Proton–antiproton collisions at CERN produced events with the masses and decay signatures predicted for the charged $W$ and neutral $Z$ weak bosons.

nodes.label: LEP precision electroweak measurements
nodes.summary: LEP measurements of the $Z$ resonance, electroweak observables, and fermion production subjected the Standard Model to high-precision consistency tests.

nodes.label: Top-quark discovery at the Tevatron
nodes.summary: The CDF and DØ collaborations observed top–antitop production in 1995, completing the third-generation quark doublet predicted by the Standard Model.

nodes.label: Super-Kamiokande atmospheric-neutrino result
nodes.summary: Super-Kamiokande observed a zenith-angle-dependent deficit of muon neutrinos, providing compelling evidence for atmospheric neutrino oscillations.

nodes.label: SNO solar-neutrino flavor-change measurement
nodes.summary: SNO separately measured electron-neutrino and all-flavor solar-neutrino fluxes, showing that the missing electron neutrinos changed flavor rather than disappearing.

nodes.label: ATLAS and CMS Higgs-boson discovery
nodes.summary: ATLAS and CMS observed a new approximately $125\,\mathrm{GeV}$ scalar resonance in 2012 whose measured properties support identification with the Standard Model Higgs boson.

nodes.label: Nuclear magic-number systematics
nodes.summary: Enhanced stability and recurring spectroscopic patterns at particular proton and neutron numbers motivated the nuclear shell model and its spin–orbit structure.

nodes.label: Rutherford proton-transmutation experiment
nodes.summary: Alpha bombardment of nitrogen produced hydrogen nuclei, establishing the proton as a nuclear constituent and demonstrating artificial transmutation.

edges.label: form D(A)
edges.detail: Form complexes in A, pass to the homotopy category K(A), and localize at quasi-isomorphisms. The result is a new category, not an equivalent presentation of A.

edges.label: take all short exact sequences
edges.detail: Every abelian category has a canonical Quillen exact structure consisting of all short exact sequences.

edges.label: + AB5 and generator
edges.detail: Require exact filtered colimits, small coproducts, and a generator.

edges.label: forget additive inverses
edges.detail: Retain the commutative associative operation and identity.

edges.label: additive carrier M
edges.detail: Supply the additive abelian group.

edges.label: additive carrier V
edges.detail: Supply the additive abelian group.

edges.label: stationary-action rule
edges.detail: Stationarity of the action supplies the variational dynamical principle.

edges.label: require exact kernel/cokernel behavior
edges.detail: Require kernels and cokernels and normality of monomorphisms and epimorphisms.

edges.label: + conflations
edges.detail: Choose a class of kernel–cokernel pairs satisfying exact-category axioms.

edges.label: + shift and distinguished triangles
edges.detail: Add triangulated structure satisfying TR1–TR4.

edges.label: self-adjointness
edges.detail: Self-adjointness requires equality with the adjoint including the operator domain.

edges.label: affine spacetime structure
edges.detail: Minkowski spacetime is an affine space modeled on a Lorentzian vector space, not canonically a vector space with preferred origin.

edges.label: + associativity
edges.detail: Require $(ab)c=a(bc)$.

edges.label: add a quadratic form
edges.detail: A vector space with quadratic form $Q$ determines the Clifford algebra characterized by the universal relation $v^2=Q(v)1$.

edges.label: operation signature
edges.detail: Supply the operation symbols and their arities.

edges.label: emitted alpha particle
edges.detail: Alpha decay produces a helium-4 nucleus (alpha particle) and a daughter nuclide, with the cluster escaping through quantum tunneling.

edges.label: $jj$ coupling regime
edges.detail: $jj$ coupling is useful when individual spin–orbit couplings dominate residual interelectronic angular coupling.

edges.label: LS coupling regime
edges.detail: LS coupling is useful when electrostatic interactions dominate individual spin–orbit couplings in a many-electron atom.

edges.label: orbital contribution
edges.detail: Orbital angular momentum is the contribution from spatial wavefunction transformations.

edges.label: intrinsic contribution
edges.detail: Spin is intrinsic quantum angular momentum associated with symmetry representations.

edges.label: antisymmetric many-particle space
edges.detail: Fermionic states occupy antisymmetric Fock space.

edges.label: implies Noetherian
edges.detail: Every commutative Artinian ring is Noetherian.

edges.label: associative multiplication
edges.detail: Supply an associative algebra over the same normed field K, on the same carrier, addition, and scalar action as the Banach space.

edges.label: + involution
edges.detail: Over a scalar field with involution, add a semilinear involutive anti-automorphism.

edges.label: require a unit
edges.detail: Select associative algebras whose multiplication has a two-sided identity; it is unique.

edges.label: stationary energy states
edges.detail: Atoms possess discrete bound-state energy levels and continua, measured through spectroscopic transitions.

edges.label: atomic quantum states
edges.detail: The atom has a spectrum of bound, resonant, and continuum states.

edges.label: ionization or electron attachment
edges.detail: Removing electrons from, or attaching electrons to, an atom produces an atomic ion.

edges.label: electron removal
edges.detail: Ionization removes a bound electron when sufficient energy or field strength is supplied.

edges.label: many-electron atom
edges.detail: Most neutral atoms have several interacting electrons.

edges.label: atomic nuclei and electrons reorganized in molecular state
edges.detail: Molecules are not classical sums of pre-existing intact atoms; their nuclei and electrons form a joint quantum bound state conventionally described by atomic composition.

edges.label: specified nuclear composition
edges.detail: A nuclide is a species of atom characterized by proton number, neutron number, and, when relevant, nuclear energy state.

edges.label: single bound electron
edges.detail: One-electron atomic systems are physical systems that include neutral hydrogen and hydrogenlike positive ions with one bound electron.

edges.label: historical nuclear model
edges.detail: The Rutherford model captures the concentration of positive charge in a nucleus but fails as a stable classical atom.

edges.label: transition frequencies
edges.detail: Differences between levels contribute spectral line frequencies, subject to transition matrix elements and broadening.

edges.label: atomic bound-state dynamics
edges.detail: An atomic Hamiltonian describes the internal dynamics and energy spectrum of an atom within its stated effective and approximation regime.

edges.label: neglect nuclear recoil
edges.detail: Fixing the nucleus is controlled by small electron-to-nuclear mass ratios, but precision work restores recoil and mass-polarization terms.

edges.label: leading nonrelativistic Coulomb model
edges.detail: The Coulomb Hamiltonian follows when transverse-photon, relativistic, radiative, recoil, and finite-size effects are smaller than the required accuracy.

edges.label: finite-mass correction
edges.detail: Nuclear recoil and mass-polarization terms are finite-nuclear-mass components of precision atomic Hamiltonians.

edges.label: relativistic atomic description
edges.detail: Relativistic atomic structure replaces or augments the nonrelativistic Hamiltonian with Dirac-based and QED-matched descriptions when $Z\alpha$ or required precision makes relativistic effects important.

edges.label: nuclear constituent
edges.detail: An atom contains one nucleus carrying almost all its mass and all positive charge.

edges.label: extended charge distribution
edges.detail: The finite nuclear charge radius perturbs electronic wavefunctions and energy levels.

edges.label: mass and charge-radius dependence
edges.detail: Nuclear mass and charge distribution shift atomic transition frequencies across isotopes.

edges.label: neutron count
edges.detail: Neutron number counts nuclear neutrons.

edges.label: separation energy total
edges.detail: Nuclear binding energy measures the mass-energy difference from separated nucleons.

edges.label: nuclear quantum states
edges.detail: Each nucleus has ground, excited, resonant, and continuum states.

edges.label: proton count
edges.detail: Proton number counts nuclear protons.

edges.label: unstable nuclear transition
edges.detail: Unstable nuclei transform through radioactive decay channels permitted by interactions and energetics.

edges.label: occupation basis
edges.detail: Electron configurations record occupations of a chosen orbital or subshell basis; they are state descriptions, not material assemblies of orbitals.

edges.label: grouped by principal shell
edges.detail: In hydrogenic and central-field classifications, one-electron orbitals sharing the principal quantum number are grouped into a shell; a shell is a state classification, not a material composite.

edges.label: self-energy correction
edges.detail: Bound-electron self-energy is a principal atomic QED correction.

edges.label: radiative level splitting
edges.detail: Self-energy and vacuum polarization dominate the Lamb shift, with recoil and nuclear-size contributions also relevant.

edges.label: vacuum-polarization correction
edges.detail: Vacuum polarization modifies the nuclear Coulomb potential.

edges.label: energy level
edges.detail: Energy levels are energies assigned to stationary or metastable atomic states.

edges.label: angular-momentum label
edges.detail: Term symbols label symmetry and angular-momentum properties of atomic states.

edges.label: state change
edges.detail: Atomic transitions connect initial and final atomic states.

edges.label: upward radiative transition
edges.detail: Absorption raises the atomic energy by taking energy from a field.

edges.label: electric-dipole channel
edges.detail: Electric-dipole transitions are the leading radiative multipole channel when allowed.

edges.label: vacuum-induced emission
edges.detail: Spontaneous emission lowers an excited state through coupling to the quantized field.

edges.label: field-stimulated emission
edges.detail: Stimulated emission is induced by an incident field.

edges.label: complete normed algebra
edges.detail: Supply the complete normed complex algebra structure on the same carrier and multiplication used by the star-algebra input.

edges.label: complete norm
edges.detail: Supply a Banach-space norm over the same normed field K and on the same carrier, addition, and scalar action as the algebra.

edges.label: weak-derivative norm
edges.detail: Sobolev spaces complete functions under norms including weak derivatives.

edges.label: neutron baryon
edges.detail: The neutron is an electrically neutral baryon.

edges.label: nucleon baryons
edges.detail: The nucleon doublet consists of proton and neutron baryons.

edges.label: proton baryon
edges.detail: The proton is the lightest positively charged baryon.

edges.label: beta-minus channel
edges.detail: Beta-minus decay emits an electron and antineutrino.

edges.label: beta-plus channel
edges.detail: Beta-plus decay emits a positron and neutrino.

edges.label: electron-capture channel
edges.detail: Electron capture is the crossed weak process competing with beta-plus decay.

edges.label: electron product
edges.detail: Beta-minus decay produces an electron.

edges.label: electron-antineutrino product
edges.detail: Beta-minus decay produces an electron antineutrino.

edges.label: proton product
edges.detail: At the nucleon level, beta-minus decay converts a neutron into a proton.

edges.label: electron-neutrino product
edges.detail: Beta-plus decay produces an electron neutrino.

edges.label: positron product
edges.detail: Beta-plus decay produces a positron and an electron neutrino while converting a proton to a neutron within a nucleus.

edges.label: require an antipode
edges.detail: Select bialgebras for which a convolution inverse of the identity exists; the antipode is then unique.

edges.label: add horizontal and vertical differentials
edges.detail: Add differentials of bidegrees (1,0) and (0,1) (or the homological sign variant), require each square to vanish, and require anticommutation.

edges.label: + reflexive, symmetric, transitive
edges.detail: First specialize to an endorelation $X=Y$; restrict to equivalence relations.

edges.label: + total and single-valued
edges.detail: Specialize to a relation $R\subseteq X\times Y$ that is total and single-valued in X; this is exactly a function $X\to Y$.

edges.label: add propositional valuation
edges.detail: Specialize to an endorelation on worlds, treat it as accessibility, and assign atomic propositions to worlds.

edges.label: + reflexive, transitive
edges.detail: First specialize to an endorelation $X=Y$; restrict to reflexive and transitive relations.

edges.label: + well-foundedness
edges.detail: First specialize to an endorelation $X=Y$; require every nonempty subset to have a minimal element.

edges.label: require completeness
edges.detail: Require arbitrary joins and meets.

edges.label: add modal operator
edges.detail: Add a normal unary operator interpreting necessity.

edges.label: forget the topology
edges.detail: Retain only the Borel σ-algebra as a measurable-space structure.

edges.label: outcome probabilities
edges.detail: The Born rule maps states and measurement operators to probabilities.

edges.label: spin-one gauge boson
edges.detail: Photons, gluons, and $W$ and $Z$ particles are gauge bosons.

edges.label: scalar boson
edges.detail: The Higgs boson is a spin-zero boson, not a gauge boson.

edges.label: electric charge
edges.detail: This particle carries the indicated electromagnetic charge.

edges.label: + complements exist
edges.detail: Require every element to have a complement; distributivity makes it unique.

edges.label: + relative pseudocomplements exist
edges.detail: Require every meet map $a\wedge -$ to have a right adjoint $a\to -$.

edges.label: forget meet and join operations
edges.detail: Retain the partial order with its least and greatest elements.

edges.label: supply bounds
edges.detail: Use the bounded-lattice structure.

edges.label: idempotence
edges.detail: A projection satisfies $P^2=P$; orthogonal projections also satisfy $P=P^*$.

edges.label: summable singular values
edges.detail: Trace-class operators form an operator ideal with a finite trace norm.

edges.label: unitarity
edges.detail: A unitary operator preserves the inner product and is surjective.

edges.label: impose symmetry
edges.detail: Require double braiding to be the identity.

edges.label: covariant differentiation
edges.detail: Gauge covariant derivatives are connections on associated vector bundles.

edges.label: observable algebra
edges.detail: Operator-algebraic quantum theory organizes bounded observables in C*-algebras.

edges.label: first variation
edges.detail: The functional derivative represents the first variation when such a representation exists.

edges.label: variational stationarity
edges.detail: The stationary-action principle is formulated using the calculus of variations.

edges.label: noncommuting-observable bound
edges.detail: Canonical noncommutation implies position–momentum uncertainty relations.

edges.label: canonical construction
edges.detail: Canonical quantization is one route to QFT formulations.

edges.label: add exponentials
edges.detail: Add internal $\operatorname{hom}$ objects right-adjoint to product.

edges.label: supply exponentials
edges.detail: Use the cartesian-closed structure.

edges.label: add finite products
edges.detail: Choose a terminal object and binary products satisfying their universal properties.

edges.label: + dagger involution
edges.detail: Add an involutive identity-on-objects contravariant endofunctor.

edges.label: require finite limits
edges.detail: Require every finite diagram to have a limit.

edges.label: require invertible arrows
edges.detail: Require every morphism to have a two-sided inverse.

edges.label: ambient category
edges.detail: Supply the category in which the diagram takes values.

edges.label: ambient category
edges.detail: Supply the category in which the diagram takes values.

edges.label: + weak equivalences, fibrations, cofibrations
edges.detail: Add three morphism classes satisfying Quillen model-category axioms.

edges.label: add tensor and unit
edges.detail: Add a tensor bifunctor, unit object, associator, and unitors satisfying coherence.

edges.label: add abelian hom-groups
edges.detail: Give each hom-set an abelian-group structure and make composition bilinear.

edges.label: + set-sized objects and arrows
edges.detail: Require the collections of objects and morphisms to be sets.

edges.label: at most one arrow
