edges.label: law within theory
edges.detail: A physical theory contains or entails laws within its stated domain.

edges.label: model realization
edges.detail: A physical model selects a system, degrees of freedom, parameters, boundary or initial data, and often idealizations within or motivated by a theory; not every model is a controlled approximation.

edges.label: domain of scales
edges.detail: The validity and useful variables of a physical theory depend on physical scales.

edges.label: quantum framework
edges.detail: Quantum mechanics specializes physical theory to systems requiring quantum states, amplitudes, and probabilistic measurement rules.

edges.label: relativistic spacetime framework
edges.detail: Special relativity specializes physical theory to nongravitational laws compatible with Lorentz symmetry.

edges.label: exchanged pion field
edges.detail: Pion exchange produces the longest-range component of the nucleon–nucleon interaction.

edges.label: flavor–mass mixing
edges.detail: The PMNS matrix relates flavor and mass bases.

edges.label: Poincaré group action
edges.detail: Poincaré symmetry is mathematically represented by the Poincaré group.

edges.label: flat-spacetime symmetry
edges.detail: Relativistic QFT in Minkowski spacetime carries a unitary Poincaré action.

edges.label: mass Casimir
edges.detail: For a stable one-particle sector, mass is fixed by the Poincaré energy–momentum Casimir; unstable resonances are not exact asymptotic one-particle representations.

edges.label: basepoint
edges.detail: Supply the Pointed set structure as one jointly required input.

edges.label: + multiplication up to unit homotopy
edges.detail: Add continuous multiplication with homotopy unit laws.

edges.label: Hamiltonian evolution bracket
edges.detail: Hamiltonian time evolution is generated by the Poisson bracket with the Hamiltonian.

edges.label: Poisson-bracket geometry
edges.detail: Poisson manifolds supply the bracket structure generating Hamiltonian evolution and include symplectic phase spaces as the nondegenerate case.

edges.label: positive state operator
edges.detail: Density operators are positive operators normalized by their trace.

edges.label: positive-operator-valued measure
edges.detail: A POVM adds a normalized, weakly countably additive assignment of a positive operator to each measurable outcome set.

edges.label: generalized measurement outcomes
edges.detail: POVMs assign outcome probabilities through the Born rule.

edges.label: add finite biproducts
edges.detail: Add a zero object and finite biproducts.

edges.label: require common upper bounds
edges.detail: Require the carrier to be nonempty and every pair to have a common upper bound.

edges.label: add persistent valuation
edges.detail: Add a valuation monotone along the information preorder.

edges.label: + antisymmetry
edges.detail: Require $x\le y$ and $y\le x$ to imply $x=y$.

edges.label: view as a thin category
edges.detail: Use elements as objects and a unique morphism $x\to y$ exactly when $x\le y$; thin categories conversely determine preorders on their objects.

edges.label: presheaf data
edges.detail: Supply the contravariant functor to which the sheaf condition will be applied.

edges.label: global gauge geometry
edges.detail: Connections on principal bundles provide the global geometric formulation of gauge potentials and curvature.

edges.label: principal connection
edges.detail: A principal connection is additional equivariant horizontal-distribution or connection-form data.

edges.label: spin lift
edges.detail: A spin structure lifts the oriented orthonormal frame bundle to a spin bundle.

edges.label: connection curvature
edges.detail: A connection canonically determines its curvature two-form.

edges.label: connection one-form
edges.detail: Gauge potentials are local representatives of principal connections.

edges.label: require local discrete valuation form
edges.detail: Require the PID to be a nonfield local ring with a unique nonzero prime ideal (its maximal ideal).

edges.label: principal shell label
edges.detail: In central-field language, the principal quantum number primarily labels electron shells.

edges.label: probability measure
edges.detail: Supply the Probability space structure as one jointly required input.

edges.label: probability domain
edges.detail: Supply the probability measure and its underlying measurable space.

edges.label: + standard Borel form
edges.detail: Require a standard Borel realization modulo null sets.

edges.label: state rays
edges.detail: Pure states are represented by rays in a complex Hilbert space, equivalently points of projective Hilbert space.

edges.label: two proton constituents
edges.detail: An alpha particle contains two protons.

edges.label: proton constituent
edges.detail: Protons are constituent nucleons of nuclei.

edges.label: proton constituent
edges.detail: The deuteron contains one proton.

edges.label: element identity
edges.detail: Chemical elements are defined by proton number.

edges.label: $A=Z+N$ contribution
edges.detail: Mass number equals proton plus neutron number.

edges.label: metric-compatible torsion-free connection
edges.detail: Every pseudo-Riemannian metric determines a unique Levi–Civita connection.

edges.label: fix Lorentzian signature
edges.detail: Require one time-like direction in the metric signature.

edges.label: + positive definiteness
edges.detail: Require the nondegenerate metric tensor to be positive definite at every point.

edges.label: + point separation
edges.detail: Require $d(x,y)=0$ only when $x=y$.

edges.label: ultraviolet running
edges.detail: The renormalization-group flow of QCD produces asymptotic freedom at high momentum transfer.

edges.label: low-energy pion expansion
edges.detail: Chiral perturbation theory is the low-energy EFT of QCD’s approximate chiral symmetry and its breaking.

edges.label: nonperturbative confined phase
edges.detail: Confinement is a nonperturbative property of low-energy QCD, supported by experiment and lattice calculations, though no general continuum proof exists for physical QCD.

edges.label: dressed-quark hadron model
edges.detail: The constituent-quark model is a phenomenological low-energy model of selected hadron properties, not a controlled universal reduction of QCD.

edges.label: gluon fields
edges.detail: QCD describes self-interacting gluon gauge fields.

edges.label: gluon field
edges.detail: The $SU(3)_C$ gluon connection is a QCD field component.

edges.label: gauge self-interaction
edges.detail: Three- and four-gluon vertices are QCD interaction components.

edges.label: colored-to-hadronic conversion
edges.detail: Hadronization is a nonperturbative QCD process modeled phenomenologically in event generators.

edges.label: regulated nonperturbative formulation
edges.detail: Lattice QCD is a gauge-invariant regulator and nonperturbative computational formulation. Finite lattice spacing, finite volume, and unphysical parameter choices introduce controlled errors that are extrapolated away.

edges.label: strongly coupled regime
edges.detail: Low-energy QCD is the confined, nonperturbative regime of the theory.

edges.label: low-energy nucleon/pion degrees of freedom
edges.detail: Nuclear EFT matches QCD symmetries and low-energy constants using nucleons and pions or pionless degrees of freedom.

edges.label: quark fields
edges.detail: QCD describes color-charged quark fields.

edges.label: quark matter fields
edges.detail: Color-triplet quark fields are QCD matter components.

edges.label: quark–gluon coupling
edges.detail: The covariant-derivative quark–gluon coupling is a QCD interaction component.

edges.label: color-singlet residual interaction
edges.detail: Interactions between color-singlet hadrons emerge from low-energy QCD. At nuclear scales they are represented systematically by hadronic and nuclear effective field theories.

edges.label: strong sector
edges.detail: QCD supplies the $SU(3)_C$ strong-interaction sector of the Standard Model.

edges.label: color interaction
edges.detail: QCD is the fundamental theory of the strong interaction.

edges.label: bound-state low-energy Hamiltonian
edges.detail: Atomic Hamiltonians are low-energy bound-state descriptions matched to QED, with nuclear structure and weak/gravitational effects added when relevant.

edges.label: bound-state perturbative corrections
edges.detail: Atomic QED computes radiative corrections in expansions adapted to bound states, with nonperturbative-in-$Z\alpha$ methods for high $Z$.

edges.label: one-transverse-photon correction
edges.detail: The Breit operator is a leading low-frequency, one-transverse-photon relativistic correction to instantaneous Coulomb interaction, not the full QED interaction.

edges.label: classical coherent-field limit
edges.detail: Maxwell electrodynamics is recovered for suitable coherent states, weak quantum fluctuations, and classical sources; radiative quantum corrections are neglected.

edges.label: static nonrelativistic one-photon sector
edges.detail: The Coulomb potential is the leading low-energy static interaction obtained from QED between charged sources.

edges.label: no-pair relativistic bound-state Hamiltonian
edges.detail: The Dirac–Coulomb Hamiltonian is an effective bound-state reduction of QED and is not the full field theory.

edges.label: quantum electromagnetism
edges.detail: QED describes electromagnetic interactions of charged quantum fields and photons.

edges.label: charged lepton field
edges.detail: QED describes electron and positron fields interacting with the electromagnetic field.

edges.label: low-velocity charged-particle EFT
edges.detail: NRQED integrates out relativistic modes and expands in $v/c$, momentum over mass, and $\alpha$.

edges.label: photon field
edges.detail: The photon is the gauge quantum of QED.

edges.label: electromagnetic-current vertex
edges.detail: The photon coupling to the conserved electric current of charged fermion fields is the basic QED interaction term.

edges.label: photon gauge field
edges.detail: The photon field is the gauge-field component of QED.

edges.label: gauge connection field
edges.detail: Gauge fields implement local gauge structure.

edges.label: scalar quantum field
edges.detail: The Higgs field is a scalar quantum field.

edges.label: matter field
edges.detail: Matter fields carry nontrivial internal representations.

edges.label: scalar field
edges.detail: A scalar field transforms in the trivial finite-dimensional representation of the Lorentz group under Lorentz transformations.

edges.label: spinor field
edges.detail: Spinor fields transform under spin representations.

edges.label: vector field
edges.detail: Vector fields transform in Lorentz-vector representations.

edges.label: interpolated one-particle state
edges.detail: A suitably smeared field acting on the vacuum can have overlap with one-particle states; the relation is theory- and stability-dependent.

edges.label: distributional definition
edges.detail: In rigorous local formulations, a quantum field is represented as an operator-valued distribution that must be smeared with test functions rather than as a pointwise operator.

edges.label: conjugate particle sectors
edges.detail: Relativistic QFT naturally includes antiparticle sectors for charged fields.

edges.label: correlation functions
edges.detail: Correlation functions encode QFT observables and dynamics.

edges.label: scale-organized QFT
edges.detail: Effective field theory is a scale-organized use of QFT with a specified cutoff and degrees of freedom.

edges.label: quadratic theory
edges.detail: Free QFTs have quadratic actions and no interactions.

edges.label: gauge-invariant QFT
edges.detail: The Standard Model interactions are described by relativistic quantum gauge field theories.

edges.label: interacting theory
edges.detail: Interacting QFTs include nonquadratic couplings.

edges.label: multiparticle sectors
edges.detail: QFT supports multiparticle states and variable particle number.

edges.label: low-energy fixed-particle sector
edges.detail: Nonrelativistic quantum mechanics emerges as a low-energy effective description of suitable QFT sectors when pair creation and relativistic corrections are suppressed.

edges.label: one-particle sector
edges.detail: Stable particles correspond to one-particle asymptotic sectors or representations when they exist.

edges.label: coupling / loop expansion
edges.detail: Perturbative QFT is a loop or coupling expansion around a solvable theory. It is often asymptotic rather than convergent and is quantitatively useful only in appropriate coupling and kinematic regimes.

edges.label: local field operator
edges.detail: Local field operators are formal ingredients of common QFT formulations.

edges.label: regulated expressions
edges.detail: Perturbative and lattice formulations introduce regulators to define intermediate quantities.

edges.label: asymptotic scattering operator
edges.detail: QFT defines an S-matrix when asymptotic particle states and suitable long-time limits exist.

edges.label: vacuum selection
edges.detail: QFT can have vacua that do not preserve all symmetries of the action.

edges.label: vacuum state
edges.detail: A QFT may have one or more vacuum states relative to its dynamics and spacetime.

edges.label: semiclassical correspondence model
edges.detail: The Bohr model is a semiclassical approximation superseded by wave mechanics.

edges.label: bound spectrum
edges.detail: Quantum Hamiltonians may have normalizable bound states.

edges.label: semiclassical and decohered regimes
edges.detail: Classical behavior emerges in suitable large-action, narrow-wavepacket, coarse-grained, and environmentally decohered regimes; no single universal $\hbar\to0$ limit covers all quantum systems.

edges.label: many-body systems
edges.detail: Many-body quantum mechanics specializes quantum theory to interacting multi-degree systems.

edges.label: molecular quantum states
edges.detail: Molecular electronic, vibrational, and rotational states are quantum mechanical; practical calculations use controlled approximations such as Born–Oppenheimer separation.

edges.label: nonrelativistic regime
edges.detail: Nonrelativistic quantum mechanics specializes quantum theory to low velocities and fixed particle number.

edges.label: quantum principles
edges.detail: QFT incorporates quantum states, observables, amplitudes, and probabilistic prediction while allowing fields and variable particle number.

edges.label: quadratic model
edges.detail: The harmonic oscillator is the universal quadratic quantum model near stable equilibria and for free field modes.

edges.label: operator observable
edges.detail: Quantum mechanics represents observables by operators or generalized measurements.

edges.label: small perturbation expansion
edges.detail: Perturbation theory expands around a solvable Hamiltonian in a controlled small parameter when convergence or asymptotic accuracy permits.

edges.label: quantum state
edges.detail: Quantum mechanics represents the state of a system by a state vector, ray, or density operator.

edges.label: quantum dynamics and predictions
edges.detail: Quantum mechanics governs quantum systems in its domain.

edges.label: continuum state
edges.detail: Quantum Hamiltonians may have continuum scattering states.

edges.label: trial-state restriction
edges.detail: The variational method restricts the state search to a parameterized family and optimizes the energy.

edges.label: projection quantum number
edges.detail: The magnetic number labels a chosen-axis projection.

edges.label: orbital angular-momentum number
edges.detail: The orbital number is one angular-momentum quantum number.

edges.label: principal quantum number
edges.detail: The principal number is one atomic quantum number.

edges.label: spin projection
edges.detail: Electron spin projection is an atomic quantum number.

edges.label: total angular momentum
edges.detail: Total $J$ labels a coupled angular-momentum representation.

edges.label: asymptotic scattering states
edges.detail: Scattering theory analyzes continuum in/out states.

edges.label: mixed state
edges.detail: Mixed states are non-extremal quantum states.

edges.label: pure state
edges.detail: Pure states are extremal quantum states.

edges.label: coordinate representation
edges.detail: A wavefunction is a representation of a quantum state in a chosen basis, commonly position.

edges.label: bottom quark
edges.detail: Bottom quark is one of six quark flavors.

edges.label: charm quark
edges.detail: Charm quark is one of six quark flavors.

edges.label: color quantum number
edges.detail: This field or particle carries nontrivial color structure.

edges.label: down quark
edges.detail: Down quark is one of six quark flavors.

edges.label: sea-quark content
edges.detail: Hadron states and parton distributions include quark–antiquark sea degrees of freedom beyond their net valence content.

edges.label: strange quark
edges.detail: Strange quark is one of six quark flavors.

edges.label: top quark
edges.detail: Top quark is one of six quark flavors.

edges.label: up quark
edges.detail: Up quark is one of six quark flavors.

edges.label: net valence content
edges.detail: A hadron’s valence content records its net quark-flavor quantum numbers, not the complete quark–gluon state.

edges.label: quark-field degrees of freedom
edges.detail: Hadron states contain quark and antiquark field degrees of freedom, including valence and sea components.

edges.label: quark quanta
edges.detail: Quark particles are excitations/asymptotic partonic states of quark fields, though isolated quarks are not asymptotic states in the confined regime.

edges.label: require an identity
edges.detail: Select quasigroups with a two-sided identity; it is then unique.

edges.label: + idempotence
edges.detail: Require $x\triangleright x=x$.

edges.label: alpha decay channel
edges.detail: Alpha decay is a radioactive decay channel.

edges.label: beta decay channel
edges.detail: Beta decay is a radioactive decay channel.

edges.label: gamma transition channel
edges.detail: Gamma decay is an electromagnetic de-excitation channel.

edges.label: family members
edges.detail: Supply measurable random variables on one common probability space.

edges.label: finite-mass Rydberg correction
edges.detail: Replacing the electron mass by the reduced mass gives the leading finite-nuclear-mass correction to hydrogenic gross structure.

edges.label: + irreducibility and nonemptiness
edges.detail: Require the reduced scheme to be nonempty and irreducible.

edges.label: remove regulator dependence
edges.detail: Renormalization relates regulated parameters to finite observables and controlled regulator removal or matching.

edges.label: relativistic splitting
edges.detail: Fine structure arises from the relativistic atomic Hamiltonian and its low-energy expansion.

edges.label: spin-$1/2$ wave equation
edges.detail: The Dirac equation is the relativistic spinor wave equation.

edges.label: spin-zero wave equation
edges.detail: The Klein–Gordon equation is the relativistic scalar wave equation.

edges.label: scale dependence
edges.detail: Renormalization-group equations describe how renormalized couplings and operators change with scale.

edges.label: beta-function flow
edges.detail: Running couplings solve renormalization-group flow equations.

edges.label: nucleon interaction
edges.detail: The nuclear force is the residual strong interaction in the nucleon sector.

edges.label: divergence-free curvature combination
edges.detail: Combining Ricci and scalar curvature gives the Einstein tensor.

edges.label: metric trace
edges.detail: Tracing Ricci curvature with the inverse metric gives scalar curvature.

edges.label: spacetime curvature
edges.detail: General relativity formulates gravitation using the curvature of a Lorentzian metric.

edges.label: tensor contraction
edges.detail: Contracting the Riemann tensor gives the Ricci tensor.

edges.label: positive metric
edges.detail: Supply the Riemannian manifold structure as one jointly required input.

edges.label: generalized eigenstates
edges.detail: Rigged Hilbert spaces accommodate distributional generalized eigenvectors used for continuum spectra.

edges.label: right-handed charged-lepton components
edges.detail: The lepton field content includes right-handed charged-lepton weak singlets.

edges.label: right-handed down-type components
edges.detail: The quark field content includes right-handed down-type weak singlets.

edges.label: right-handed up-type components
edges.detail: The quark field content includes right-handed up-type weak singlets.

edges.label: + ab=ba
edges.detail: Require multiplication to commute.

edges.label: + nonzero inverses
edges.detail: Require each nonzero element to be multiplicatively invertible.

edges.label: scalar ring R
edges.detail: Supply the scalar ring.

edges.label: supply ring
edges.detail: Use the ring operations on the common carrier.

edges.label: ring structure
edges.detail: Supply ring operations.

edges.label: is a Dedekind domain
edges.detail: The ring of integers of a number field is a Dedekind domain.

edges.label: + local stalks
edges.detail: Require every stalk of the structure sheaf to be a local ring.

edges.label: quantized-orbit supplement
edges.detail: The Bohr model adds ad hoc quantization to the Rutherford atom and works mainly for hydrogenic gross spectra.

edges.label: matrix elements
edges.detail: Scattering amplitudes are matrix elements of the S-matrix after removing normalization and conservation factors.

edges.label: bosonic scalar field
edges.detail: Physical Lorentz-scalar particles are bosonic under the spin–statistics assumptions; auxiliary ghost scalars are not physical asymptotic particle fields.

edges.label: Higgs potential
edges.detail: The Higgs potential includes a quartic self-interaction.

edges.label: + globally affine
edges.detail: Require the scheme to be isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ for some commutative ring R.

edges.label: geometric object
edges.detail: Supply the Scheme structure as one jointly required input.

edges.label: + local Noetherianity and quasi-compactness
edges.detail: Require Noetherian affine neighborhoods and quasi-compactness.

edges.label: + reduced local rings
edges.detail: Require no nonzero nilpotents in local rings.

edges.label: require local Noetherian regularity
edges.detail: Require X to be locally Noetherian and every local ring $O_{X,x}$ to be a regular local ring; quasi-compactness is not required.

edges.label: + base and structure morphism
edges.detail: Choose a base scheme S and a morphism $X\to S$.

edges.label: + closed diagonal
edges.detail: For the absolute node, require $\Delta_{X/\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb{Z})}\colon X\to X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb{Z})}X$ to be a closed immersion; over a base S use $\Delta_{X/S}$.

edges.label: + projectivity
edges.detail: Require $X\to S$ to factor as a closed immersion into $P^{n}_S$ followed by the projection to S, for some n.

edges.label: differential evolution equation
edges.detail: The Schrödinger equation is the differential form of Hamiltonian unitary evolution.

edges.label: continuous dual
edges.detail: Tempered distributions are continuous linear functionals on Schwartz space.

edges.label: test functions
edges.detail: Quantum fields are smeared against smooth test functions, often Schwartz functions in Minkowski-space treatments.

edges.label: screened effective potential
edges.detail: Central-field models encode much of electron screening in an effective radial potential.

edges.label: sea-quark contribution
edges.detail: The neutron contains sea-quark and antiquark degrees of freedom.

edges.label: sea-quark contribution
edges.detail: The proton contains sea-quark and antiquark degrees of freedom.

edges.label: implies first-countable
edges.detail: Restricting a countable global base to neighborhoods of a point gives a countable local base.

edges.label: countable base
edges.detail: Supply second countability.

edges.label: charm quark
edges.detail: This particle belongs to the second fermion generation.

edges.label: muon
edges.detail: This particle belongs to the second fermion generation.

edges.label: muon neutrino
edges.detail: This particle belongs to the second fermion generation.

edges.label: strange quark
edges.detail: This particle belongs to the second fermion generation.

edges.label: mode-lowering operator
edges.detail: Annihilation operators are components of the second-quantized occupation-number formalism.

edges.label: mode-raising operator
edges.detail: Creation operators are components of the second-quantized occupation-number formalism.

edges.label: E1 selection rules
edges.detail: Angular momentum and parity constrain electric-dipole matrix elements.

edges.label: nonnegative quadratic form
edges.detail: A positive operator is self-adjoint with nonnegative expectation values.

edges.label: self-adjoint observable
edges.detail: Sharp quantum observables are represented by self-adjoint operators or their spectral measures.

edges.label: spectral resolution
edges.detail: The spectral theorem associates a projection-valued measure to a self-adjoint operator.

edges.label: spectral resolution
edges.detail: The spectral theorem gives a projection-valued measure and functional calculus.

edges.label: semigroup law
edges.detail: Supply the Semigroup structure as one jointly required input.

edges.label: require an identity
edges.detail: Select semigroups in which a two-sided identity exists; it is then unique.

edges.label: + definiteness
edges.detail: Require $p(x)=0$ only for $x=0$.

edges.label: + additive inverses
edges.detail: Require the additive commutative monoid to be an abelian group.

edges.label: + target set Y and R⊆X×Y
edges.detail: Choose a target set Y and a subset $R\subseteq X\times Y$. Endorelations are the specialization $Y=X$.

edges.label: + countability
edges.detail: Restrict to finite or countably infinite sets.

edges.label: add vertices, arrows, source, target
edges.detail: Use sets of vertices and arrows with source and target maps.

edges.label: + finite cardinality
edges.detail: Restrict to sets with finitely many elements.

edges.label: choose symbols and arities
edges.detail: Choose sets of function, relation, and constant symbols with arity assignments.

edges.label: + family of subsets
edges.detail: Choose a family of hyperedges, each a subset of vertices.

edges.label: object set
edges.detail: Supply the collection of objects (set-sized in this atlas presentation).

edges.label: supply carrier
edges.detail: Use a nonempty carrier set.

edges.label: acted-on carrier
edges.detail: Supply the Set structure as one jointly required input.

edges.label: carrier set
edges.detail: Supply the common carrier on which all operations are interpreted.

edges.label: + binary operation
edges.detail: Choose a closed operation $M\times M\to M$.

edges.label: + independence system
edges.detail: Add independent subsets satisfying hereditary and exchange axioms.

edges.label: + σ-algebra
edges.detail: Choose measurable subsets.

edges.label: + choose x₀
edges.detail: Choose one distinguished element of the set.

edges.label: + pseudometric d
edges.detail: Choose a distance-like function.

edges.label: + zero and successor
edges.detail: Choose a distinguished element 0 and a unary map $S:N\to N$.

edges.label: + topology τ
edges.detail: Choose open subsets satisfying the topology axioms.

edges.label: + transitivity
edges.detail: Require every element of an element of X to lie in X.

edges.label: + edges
edges.detail: Add a collection of edges with endpoints in the vertex set.

edges.label: + uniformity
edges.detail: Choose entourages satisfying the uniformity axioms.

edges.label: + representable diagonal and existence of étale cover
edges.detail: Specialize to an fppf sheaf F on Sch/S, require representable diagonal, and require that some scheme U admit a surjective étale morphism $h_U\to F$.

edges.label: + group structures
edges.detail: Equip every section set with compatible group structure.

edges.label: + ring structures
edges.detail: Equip every section set with compatible ring structure.

edges.label: structure sheaf
edges.detail: Supply the Sheaf of rings structure as one jointly required input.

edges.label: specialize the target to Set
edges.detail: A simplicial object in Set is precisely a simplicial set; this changes the ambient target category rather than imposing an internal axiom.

edges.label: form the sheaf topos
edges.detail: Form Sh(C,J), the category of sheaves of sets on the site. This is a canonical construction from a site, not an equivalence between the site and the resulting topos.

edges.label: covering structure
edges.detail: Supply the covers on the presheaf’s domain category.

edges.label: symmetry-adapted determinant combination
edges.detail: Configuration-state functions are symmetry-adapted combinations of Slater determinants.

edges.label: antisymmetric fermion ansatz
edges.detail: A Slater determinant is the basic single-configuration antisymmetric state for identical fermions.

edges.label: forget identities and composition to a quiver
edges.detail: Retain objects as vertices, morphisms as arrows, and the source/target maps. Parallel arrows and loops remain.

edges.label: choose a Set-valued contravariant functor
edges.detail: Choose a functor $C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathbf{Set}$ on the small category C.

edges.label: + Grothendieck covering structure
edges.detail: Choose covering sieves or covering families on the small category satisfying the Grothendieck-topology axioms.

edges.label: + contact distribution
edges.detail: Add a maximally nonintegrable hyperplane field.

edges.label: smooth alternating covariant tensor field
edges.detail: Differential forms are smooth sections of exterior powers of the cotangent bundle.

edges.label: + integrable distribution
edges.detail: Add an integrable tangent distribution or foliation atlas.

edges.label: supply smooth manifold
edges.detail: Use the smooth-manifold structure on the common carrier.

edges.label: smooth object/arrow spaces
edges.detail: Supply the Smooth manifold structure as one jointly required input.

edges.label: smooth base
edges.detail: Supply the Smooth manifold structure as one jointly required input.

edges.label: add affine connection
edges.detail: Add a covariant derivative on vector fields.

edges.label: + orientation
edges.detail: Choose a consistent orientation.

edges.label: add Poisson bracket
edges.detail: Add a Lie bracket on smooth functions that is a derivation in each argument.

edges.label: add nondegenerate metric tensor
edges.detail: Add a smoothly varying nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form.

edges.label: + compatible analytic atlas
edges.detail: Choose a real-analytic atlas compatible with the underlying smooth structure.

edges.label: smooth event manifold
edges.detail: Relativistic spacetime is modeled as a smooth manifold so that fields, curves, and differential equations are defined locally.

edges.label: add closed nondegenerate 2-form
edges.detail: Add a differential 2-form that is closed and nondegenerate.

edges.label: tangent bundle
edges.detail: Each smooth manifold canonically determines its tangent bundle.

edges.label: covariant derivative
edges.detail: A connection is additional differentiation data on a smooth vector bundle.

edges.label: weak-solution spaces
edges.detail: Sobolev spaces formulate finite-energy fields and weak solutions of field equations.

edges.label: dynamical spacetime geometry
edges.detail: General relativity treats spacetime geometry as a dynamical component coupled to matter and non-gravitational fields.

edges.label: flat spacetime
edges.detail: Minkowski spacetime is the flat, nongravitating special case of relativistic spacetime.

edges.label: curvature dynamics
edges.detail: Einstein’s equation relates curvature of the metric to stress–energy.

edges.label: dynamical Lorentzian metric
edges.detail: General relativity treats the spacetime metric as a dynamical gravitational field.

edges.label: four-vector kinematics
edges.detail: Relativistic events, velocities, currents, and momenta are organized as Lorentz tensors including four-vectors.

edges.label: Lorentz invariance
edges.detail: Lorentz symmetry is the defining spacetime symmetry of special relativity.

edges.label: flat relativistic spacetime
edges.detail: Minkowski spacetime is the standard flat spacetime geometry of special relativity.

edges.label: $c\to\infty$ / low-velocity limit
edges.detail: Newtonian particle kinematics and dynamics are recovered from relativistic particle mechanics when characteristic velocities are small compared with $c$ and relativistic energy corrections are negligible.

edges.label: relativistic causal and symmetry structure
edges.detail: Relativistic QFT in Minkowski spacetime incorporates Lorentz/Poincaré symmetry and causal locality; QFT as a general framework can also be formulated on curved or nonrelativistic backgrounds.

edges.label: relativistic particle dynamics
edges.detail: Relativistic particle mechanics specializes classical dynamics to Minkowski spacetime.

edges.label: $SU(2)_L$ and $SU(3)_C$ factors
edges.detail: Special unitary groups supply the weak-isospin and color gauge factors.

edges.label: non-Abelian gauge groups
edges.detail: Important Yang–Mills theories use $SU(n)$ gauge groups.

edges.label: projective measurement
edges.detail: Projection-valued measures represent ideal sharp measurements.

edges.label: spectral measure of observable
edges.detail: The spectral theorem supplies the projection-valued measure and functional calculus of a self-adjoint observable.

edges.label: angular orbital basis
edges.detail: Hydrogenic and central-field orbitals separate into radial functions and spherical harmonics.

edges.label: spin projection on momentum
edges.detail: Helicity is the projection of spin along momentum.

edges.label: spin-$1/2$
edges.detail: Spin one-half is a particular irreducible angular-momentum representation.

edges.label: spin representation
edges.detail: A spinor representation is a linear action of the spin group.

edges.label: global spinor geometry
edges.detail: A spin structure is required to define spinor bundles globally on a curved spacetime.

edges.label: fermionic spinor field
edges.detail: Physical half-integer-spin spinor fields obey fermionic statistics under the spin–statistics assumptions; commuting spinor auxiliaries are not ordinary physical particle fields.

edges.label: spinor representation
edges.detail: Spin-$1/2$ states transform in spinor representations.

edges.label: Lorentz spinor transformation
edges.detail: Spinor fields transform in spin representations of the Lorentz spin group.

edges.label: particle content
edges.detail: The Standard Model specifies fields and interactions for the known elementary particles.

edges.label: higher-dimension operator extension
edges.detail: SMEFT extends the Standard Model Lagrangian by higher-dimension operators built from Standard Model fields and symmetries. It is an EFT of unspecified heavy new physics, not an effective reduction of the Standard Model itself.

edges.label: left lepton doublet
edges.detail: One Standard Model chiral representation type is the left-handed lepton doublet.

edges.label: left quark doublet
edges.detail: One Standard Model chiral representation type is the left-handed quark doublet.

edges.label: right charged-lepton singlet
edges.detail: One Standard Model chiral representation type is the right-handed charged-lepton singlet.

edges.label: right down-type singlet
edges.detail: One Standard Model chiral representation type is the right-handed down-type quark singlet.

edges.label: right up-type singlet
edges.detail: One Standard Model chiral representation type is the right-handed up-type quark singlet.

edges.label: chiral fermion kinetic and gauge terms
edges.detail: The Standard Model Lagrangian contains three generations of chiral fermion multiplets.

edges.label: gauge symmetry
edges.detail: The Standard Model is built around the color and electroweak gauge group.

edges.label: gauge invariance
edges.detail: The Lagrangian is invariant under the local Standard Model gauge group before gauge fixing.

edges.label: dynamical formulation
edges.detail: The Standard Model Lagrangian is the usual local action formulation encoding the theory’s field content, symmetries, masses, and interactions.

edges.label: involution
edges.detail: Supply the conjugate-linear involutive anti-automorphism on the same complex algebra carrier used by the Banach-algebra input.

edges.label: Euler–Lagrange equations
edges.detail: Variation of the action yields equations of motion under appropriate boundary conditions.

edges.label: Euler–Lagrange equation
edges.detail: Stationarity of the action under admissible variations yields the Euler–Lagrange equations.

edges.label: + Markov property
edges.detail: Require discrete time (typically index set $\mathbb{N}$) and the Markov conditional-independence property.

edges.label: self-adjoint generator
edges.detail: Stone’s theorem relates continuous unitary time evolution to a self-adjoint Hamiltonian.

edges.label: electric charge
edges.detail: This particle carries the indicated electromagnetic charge.

edges.label: matter source
edges.detail: The stress–energy tensor appears on the matter side of Einstein’s equation.

edges.label: + Peano axioms
edges.detail: Require successor injectivity, zero not to be a successor, and the adopted second-order induction axiom.

edges.label: symmetric many-particle space
edges.detail: Bosonic states occupy symmetric Fock space.

edges.label: choose duals and duality maps
edges.detail: Equip every object with a chosen dual, evaluation, and coevaluation satisfying the snake identities.

edges.label: phase-space geometry
edges.detail: Hamiltonian mechanics is naturally formulated on symplectic manifolds, whose symplectic form defines Hamiltonian vector fields and Poisson brackets.

edges.label: symplectic phase space
edges.detail: Hamiltonian phase spaces are symplectic manifolds or appropriate generalizations.

edges.label: invert the symplectic form
edges.detail: The inverse bivector of a symplectic form defines a Poisson bracket.

edges.label: + T₁
edges.detail: Require singletons to be closed.

edges.label: + disjoint neighborhoods
edges.detail: Require distinct points to have disjoint neighborhoods.

edges.label: + normal separation
edges.detail: Separate disjoint closed sets by neighborhoods.

edges.label: + regular separation
edges.detail: Separate points from closed sets by neighborhoods.

edges.label: dual bundle
edges.detail: The cotangent bundle is the fiberwise dual of the tangent bundle.

edges.label: tensor bundles
edges.detail: Tensor powers and duals of tangent bundles form tensor bundles.

edges.label: electric charge
edges.detail: This particle carries the indicated electromagnetic charge.

edges.label: smooth section
edges.detail: A tensor field is a smooth section of a tensor bundle.

edges.label: metric and curvature tensors
edges.detail: General relativity uses tensor fields on a smooth manifold.

edges.label: rank-two tensor field
edges.detail: Stress–energy is represented by a symmetric tensor field.

edges.label: composite-system state space
edges.detail: Composite distinguishable quantum systems use tensor-product Hilbert spaces, with symmetry restrictions for identical particles.

edges.label: trace one subsystem
edges.detail: The partial trace maps operators on a tensor product to reduced operators.

edges.label: composite-system state space
edges.detail: The state space of distinguishable composite quantum systems is modeled by a tensor product, with constraints for identical particles.

edges.label: bottom quark
edges.detail: This particle belongs to the third fermion generation.

edges.label: tau lepton
edges.detail: This particle belongs to the third fermion generation.

edges.label: tau neutrino
edges.detail: This particle belongs to the third fermion generation.

edges.label: top quark
edges.detail: This particle belongs to the third fermion generation.

edges.label: many-nucleon binding contribution
edges.detail: Three-nucleon forces contribute to nuclear binding, spectra, and saturation.

edges.label: electric charge
edges.detail: This particle carries the indicated electromagnetic charge.

edges.label: topological scalars
edges.detail: Supply the topology on the scalar field.

edges.label: locally compact Hausdorff, nondiscrete
edges.detail: Require the topology to be locally compact, Hausdorff, and nondiscrete.

edges.label: Haar existence theorem
edges.detail: Every locally compact Hausdorff topological group admits a nonzero left Haar measure, unique up to multiplication by a positive scalar.

edges.label: structure group
edges.detail: Supply the topological group that acts continuously on the total space.

edges.label: add holomorphic atlas
edges.detail: Choose complex charts with holomorphic transition maps.

edges.label: add smooth atlas
edges.detail: Choose a maximal atlas whose transition functions are smooth.

edges.label: forget strict associativity/unit
edges.detail: A topological monoid determines an H-space after retaining only the multiplication and basepoint.

edges.label: forget the identity
edges.detail: Retain the continuous associative multiplication and forget the distinguished unit.

edges.label: generate the Borel σ-algebra
edges.detail: Take the smallest σ-algebra containing every open set. This measurable structure is canonical for the topology.

edges.label: + compactness
edges.detail: Require every open cover to have a finite subcover.

edges.label: + compact-generation
edges.detail: Require closedness/topology to be detected by compact Hausdorff probes.

edges.label: + connectedness
edges.detail: Require no separation into two nonempty disjoint open subsets.

edges.label: require a contraction
edges.detail: Require the identity map to be homotopic to a constant map. A particular contraction is not part of the structure.

edges.label: + cell decomposition
edges.detail: Choose cells and attaching maps satisfying the CW axioms.

edges.label: + countable local bases
edges.detail: Require a countable neighborhood basis at every point.

edges.label: total and base topologies
edges.detail: Instantiate topological-space structure on the spaces occurring in the map.

edges.label: total and base topologies
edges.detail: Instantiate topological-space structure on the spaces occurring in the map.

edges.label: underlying space
