edges.label: topology on V
edges.detail: Supply the topology on the vector carrier.

edges.label: + local compactness
edges.detail: Require compact neighborhoods under the selected convention.

edges.label: + connected local bases
edges.detail: Require connected neighborhoods to form local bases.

edges.label: + Euclidean neighborhoods
edges.detail: Require local homeomorphisms to open subsets of Euclidean space.

edges.label: + smooth half-space manifold structure
edges.detail: Require Hausdorffness and second countability, and add an atlas of charts to open subsets of the closed half-space with smooth transition maps.

edges.label: + paths between points
edges.detail: Require every two points to be joined by a path.

edges.label: + separable complete metrizability
edges.detail: Require the topology to be separable and induced by at least one complete metric.

edges.label: + countable base
edges.detail: Require a countable basis for the topology.

edges.label: + T₀
edges.detail: Distinct points must be topologically distinguishable.

edges.label: + distinguished subspace
edges.detail: Choose a subspace $A\subseteq X$.

edges.label: + singleton components
edges.detail: Require every connected component to be a singleton.

edges.label: + clopen basis
edges.detail: Require a basis consisting of clopen sets.

edges.label: + local convexity
edges.detail: Restrict the scalar field to $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and require a neighborhood base at 0 consisting of convex sets.

edges.label: supply total order
edges.detail: Use the total order on the common carrier.

edges.label: supply total order
edges.detail: Use the total order on the common carrier.

edges.label: supply total order
edges.detail: Use the total order on the common carrier.

edges.label: require least elements
edges.detail: Require every nonempty subset to have a least element.

edges.label: trace-one state operator
edges.detail: Normal density operators are positive trace-class operators of unit trace.

edges.label: + membership well-orders the set
edges.detail: Require the inherited membership relation $\in$ to be a well-order of the transitive set.

edges.label: + bipartiteness
edges.detail: Require the existence of a vertex bipartition with every edge crossing between the two parts.

edges.label: + acyclicity
edges.detail: Require no undirected cycles.

edges.label: + planar embeddability
edges.detail: Require the graph to admit an embedding in the plane with edges meeting only at common endpoints.

edges.label: + no loops or parallels
edges.detail: Restrict the broad incidence graph to loopless graphs with at most one edge occurrence per unordered vertex pair.

edges.label: + weights
edges.detail: Add a weight function on edges or vertices.

edges.label: induce topology
edges.detail: Every uniformity canonically determines a topology by its entourages.

edges.label: require principal ideals
edges.detail: Require every ideal to have one generator.

edges.label: + commutativity
edges.detail: Require multiplication to commute.

edges.label: unital algebra structure
edges.detail: Supply multiplication and unit on the common carrier.

edges.label: unitary dynamics
edges.detail: Closed-system time evolution is represented by unitary operators.

edges.label: symmetry representation
edges.detail: One-particle state spaces carry unitary representations of spacetime and internal symmetry groups.

edges.label: electric charge
edges.detail: This particle carries the indicated electromagnetic charge.

edges.label: $udd$ net valence content
edges.detail: The neutron has net valence flavor $udd$, embedded in a full quark–gluon state.

edges.label: $uud$ net valence content
edges.detail: The proton has net valence flavor $uud$, embedded in a full quark–gluon state.

edges.label: canonically local
edges.detail: Every valuation ring is a local domain.

edges.label: require valuation completeness
edges.detail: Require completeness for the valuation-induced uniformity; for absolute values or rank-one valuations this is the familiar metric completeness condition.

edges.label: linear bundle
edges.detail: Supply the Vector bundle structure as one jointly required input.

edges.label: forget the chosen origin
edges.detail: Forgetting the distinguished zero of a vector space while retaining its translation action yields an affine space; abstractly, an affine space is a torsor for a vector space.

edges.label: + bilinear multiplication
edges.detail: Choose a bilinear map $A\times A\to A$; do not yet require associativity or a unit.

edges.label: + comultiplication and counit
edges.detail: Add coassociative comultiplication and a counit.

edges.label: complex scalars
edges.detail: A complex vector space is a vector space over $\mathbb C$.

edges.label: linear dual
edges.detail: The algebraic dual is canonically constructed as the vector space of linear functionals.

edges.label: exterior algebra
edges.detail: The exterior algebra is the quotient of the tensor algebra by the two-sided ideal generated by all $v\otimes v$.

edges.label: same algebra; Grassmann terminology
edges.detail: “Grassmann algebra” is standard terminology for the exterior algebra, especially in fermionic and path-integral applications.

edges.label: + inner product
edges.detail: For a real or complex vector space, choose a positive-definite symmetric bilinear form (real) or Hermitian sesquilinear form (complex).

edges.label: linear carrier
edges.detail: Supply the Vector space structure as one jointly required input.

edges.label: linear carrier
edges.detail: Supply a k-vector space V over the same field k as the Lie-algebra input.

edges.label: vector structure
edges.detail: Supply the vector-space operations.

edges.label: add Lie bracket
edges.detail: Add an alternating bilinear bracket satisfying Jacobi.

edges.label: choose a linear endomorphism
edges.detail: A linear operator is additional data: a chosen linear map from a vector space to itself, or more generally between specified vector spaces.

edges.label: + real-valued absolute value and seminorm
edges.detail: Equip the scalar field with a real-valued absolute value $|\cdot |$ and choose $p:V\to \mathbb{R}\ge 0$ with $p(x+y)\le p(x)+p(y)$ and $p(\lambda x)=|\lambda |p(x)$.

edges.label: symplectic form
edges.detail: A symplectic vector space adds a nondegenerate alternating bilinear form.

edges.label: tensor product
edges.detail: The tensor product is characterized by its universal property for bilinear maps.

edges.label: electric charge
edges.detail: This particle carries the indicated electromagnetic charge.

edges.label: $W^\pm$ interaction field
edges.detail: The charged weak fields generate charged-current amplitudes in perturbative electroweak theory.

edges.label: $W^\pm$ quantum
edges.detail: The charged $W$ bosons are excitations of the charged weak fields.

edges.label: charged-current weak interaction
edges.detail: The charged $W$ fields generate charged-current weak processes.

edges.label: hypercharge coupling
edges.detail: Weak hypercharge couples to the $U(1)_Y$ gauge field.

edges.label: flavor-changing weak process
edges.detail: Beta decay is generated by charged-current weak interaction at quark level and represented by effective nucleon/nuclear currents.

edges.label: charged-current channel
edges.detail: Charged-current processes are one weak-interaction channel.

edges.label: neutral-current channel
edges.detail: Neutral-current processes are one weak-interaction channel.

edges.label: flavor-changing charged current
edges.detail: The charged-current weak interaction changes quark flavor according to CKM amplitudes.

edges.label: weak-isospin coupling
edges.detail: $SU(2)_L$ weak isospin couples to the weak gauge fields.

edges.label: mixing parameter
edges.detail: The weak mixing angle parametrizes the neutral gauge-field rotation.

edges.label: take ordinal order type
edges.detail: Every well-ordered set is uniquely order-isomorphic to one ordinal. This changes to a canonical representative rather than enriching the original carrier.

edges.label: Yukawa matrices
edges.detail: Yukawa couplings connect Higgs and fermion fields.

edges.label: $Z$ interaction field
edges.detail: The $Z$ field generates neutral-current amplitudes in perturbative electroweak theory.

edges.label: neutral-current weak interaction
edges.detail: The $Z$ field generates neutral-current weak processes.

edges.label: $Z$ quantum
edges.detail: The $Z$ boson is the excitation of the massive neutral $Z$ field.

edges.label: cancel gauge anomalies
edges.detail: A chiral gauge theory must cancel gauge anomalies to preserve gauge consistency and unitarity.

edges.label: quantum consistency condition
edges.detail: Gauge-anomaly cancellation is a non-negotiable consistency condition on Standard Model chiral field content.

edges.label: baryon number one
edges.detail: Ordinary three-quark baryons have baryon number $1$; antibaryons have $-1$.

edges.label: representations cancel anomalies
edges.detail: The hypercharges and color/weak representations of a complete Standard Model generation make the local gauge and mixed anomalies cancel.

edges.label: linear combinations
edges.detail: The linear structure of complex state spaces supplies the formal superposition operation.

edges.label: interaction coefficients
edges.detail: Coupling constants multiply or normalize interaction operators and set perturbative expansion parameters in an interacting QFT.

edges.label: renormalized scale dependence
edges.detail: A renormalized coupling generally depends on the chosen energy scale according to its beta function.

edges.label: classical-like robust states
edges.detail: Decoherence helps explain stable classical-like records and suppressed interference, but does not alone derive all classical dynamics or solve the measurement problem.

edges.label: time component
edges.detail: Energy is the time component, up to units, of relativistic four-momentum.

edges.label: environment-induced reduced-state decoherence
edges.detail: System–environment entanglement transfers phase coherence into nonlocal correlations, suppressing interference in the reduced subsystem state.

edges.label: spacetime event
edges.detail: Spacetime is modeled as the manifold of physical events; the edge expresses point-set composition, not a material assembly.

edges.label: ordered event history
edges.detail: A worldline is a curve of events parameterized by proper time or an affine parameter.

edges.label: electroweak gauge vertices
edges.detail: Electroweak theory contains gauge-boson self-interactions fixed by the non-Abelian gauge structure.

edges.label: gauge kinetic interaction terms
edges.detail: Triple and quartic electroweak gauge vertices arise from Standard Model gauge kinetic terms.

edges.label: net force
edges.detail: The second law relates net force to momentum change, reducing to $\mathbf F=m\mathbf a$ at constant mass.

edges.label: color gauge kinetic terms
edges.detail: The Standard Model Lagrangian contains the $SU(3)_C$ gluon field strength and quark color coupling.

edges.label: covariant-derivative coupling
edges.detail: The Higgs kinetic term couples the doublet to $SU(2)_L$ and $U(1)_Y$ gauge fields.

edges.label: gauge-boson mass terms
edges.detail: In the Higgs vacuum, the covariant-derivative term yields masses for $W^\pm$ and $Z$ while leaving the photon massless.

edges.label: Higgs covariant-derivative terms
edges.detail: Higgs–gauge interactions are explicit terms in the Standard Model Lagrangian.

edges.label: $W$ mass generation
edges.detail: The Brout–Englert–Higgs mechanism generates the $W$-boson mass through the Higgs vacuum and gauge coupling.

edges.label: $Z$ mass generation
edges.detail: The Brout–Englert–Higgs mechanism generates the $Z$-boson mass while the orthogonal photon combination remains massless.

edges.label: hypercharge gauge kinetic term
edges.detail: The Standard Model Lagrangian contains the $U(1)_Y$ hypercharge gauge field and its couplings.

edges.label: lepton flavor
edges.detail: Charged leptons and neutrinos are organized by electron, muon, and tau flavor labels.

edges.label: leptonic quantum number
edges.detail: Leptons carry lepton-number assignments in the Standard Model description, subject to neutrino mixing and possible beyond-model violation.

edges.label: leptonic particle states
edges.detail: After electroweak symmetry breaking and mass diagonalization, lepton fields interpolate charged-lepton and neutrino particle states; unstable particles appear as resonances rather than exact asymptotic states.

edges.label: local causal cones
edges.detail: The continuous arrangement of light cones determines local causal relations and, under suitable conditions, global causal structure.

edges.label: nonseparable many-body states
edges.detail: Interacting and identical-particle many-body states generally exhibit correlations that can include entanglement relative to a chosen subsystem structure.

edges.label: null cone
edges.detail: A Lorentzian metric determines the null cone at every spacetime point.

edges.label: momentum-change rate
edges.detail: In Newtonian mechanics force is $d\mathbf p/dt$; this definition does not make force fundamental in every formulation.

edges.label: spatial components
edges.detail: Linear momentum supplies the spatial components of relativistic four-momentum.

edges.label: momentum dynamics
edges.detail: Newton’s second law is most generally written as a momentum-balance equation.

edges.label: Newtonian equations of motion
edges.detail: Newton’s laws supply the standard particle-law formulation of Newtonian mechanics.

edges.label: equation in one independent variable
edges.detail: An ODE is formed by imposing an equation involving an unknown function of one independent variable and its ordinary derivatives.

edges.label: trajectory equations
edges.detail: Newtonian initial-value problems are ordinarily formulated as systems of ordinary differential equations.

edges.label: reduced density operator
edges.detail: Tracing over environmental degrees of freedom gives the reduced state in which decoherence is quantified.

edges.label: quantum symmetry obstruction
edges.detail: Quantization and regularization can obstruct classical symmetries, producing anomalies.

edges.label: CPT invariance under standard assumptions
edges.detail: Local Lorentz-invariant QFT with the usual spectral and unitarity assumptions obeys CPT symmetry.

edges.label: relativistic spin–statistics connection
edges.detail: The spin–statistics connection follows under the stated structural assumptions, not from spin labels alone.

edges.label: baryon quantum number
edges.detail: Baryon number is an additive internal quantum number, perturbatively conserved in the Standard Model but violated by electroweak anomalies in $B+L$.

edges.label: flavor label
edges.detail: Flavor distinguishes repeated quark and lepton species with otherwise analogous gauge roles.

edges.label: lepton quantum number
edges.detail: Lepton numbers label leptonic states; flavor lepton numbers are violated by neutrino mixing and total lepton number is not established as exact.

edges.label: energy quantity
edges.detail: Energy is a physical quantity whose exact definition is theory-dependent.

edges.label: linear momentum
edges.detail: Linear momentum is a physical quantity associated with spatial translations.

edges.label: quark baryon number
edges.detail: Quarks carry baryon number $1/3$ and antiquarks carry $-1/3$.

edges.label: quark flavor
edges.detail: The six quark species are distinguished by flavor.

edges.label: smooth parameterized map
edges.detail: A smooth curve is a smooth map from a one-dimensional parameter domain into a smooth manifold.

edges.label: smooth spacetime curve
edges.detail: Ideal particle histories are represented by smooth causal curves in spacetime.

edges.label: integer-spin bosonic statistics
edges.detail: The theorem connects integer spin with bosonic exchange statistics under its assumptions.

edges.label: half-integer-spin fermionic statistics
edges.detail: The theorem connects half-integer spin with fermionic exchange statistics under its assumptions.

edges.label: Minkowski causal structure
edges.detail: Special relativity fixes causal ordering through Minkowski light cones.

edges.label: supports coherent superposition
edges.detail: Pure state vectors support coherent linear superposition, while mixtures represent statistical rather than coherent combinations.

edges.label: curve velocity
edges.detail: The derivative of a smooth curve at a parameter value defines a tangent vector.

edges.label: timelike tangent vector
edges.detail: Four-velocity is a normalized timelike tangent vector to a worldline.

edges.label: nonseparable tensor-product states
edges.detail: Entanglement is defined relative to a tensor-product or algebraic subsystem decomposition.

edges.label: non-Abelian gauge self-coupling
edges.detail: The $SU(2)_L$ field strength contains cubic and quartic gauge-field terms.

edges.label: weak gauge kinetic terms
edges.detail: The Standard Model Lagrangian contains the three $SU(2)_L$ gauge fields and their non-Abelian field strength.

edges.label: tangent four-velocity
edges.detail: Differentiating a timelike worldline with respect to proper time gives four-velocity.

edges.label: elapsed proper time
edges.detail: Proper time is the metric length parameter along a timelike worldline.

edges.label: charged-fermion mass parameters
edges.detail: After electroweak symmetry breaking, Yukawa matrices times the Higgs vacuum expectation value determine charged-fermion mass matrices. Minimal Standard Model neutrinos remain massless.

edges.label: symmetry-breaking scalar multiplet
edges.detail: The Higgs doublet and its vacuum configuration supply the scalar degrees of freedom used by the electroweak Higgs mechanism.

edges.label: electromagnetic low-energy sector
edges.detail: QED is the unbroken electromagnetic gauge sector obtained from the Standard Model after electroweak symmetry breaking and field mixing.

edges.label: integrate out electroweak-scale fields
edges.detail: Below the electroweak scale, integrating out $W$, $Z$, Higgs, and top degrees of freedom yields LEFT with QCD, QED, and local higher-dimension operators.

edges.label: match below electroweak scale
edges.detail: SMEFT matches onto LEFT after electroweak symmetry breaking and integration of heavy Standard Model fields; LEFT Wilson coefficients retain the effects of SMEFT operators.

edges.label: QED gauge sector
edges.detail: QED for the light charged fields is a renormalizable gauge-sector component of LEFT.

edges.label: QCD gauge sector
edges.detail: QCD for the light quarks and gluons is a renormalizable gauge-sector component of LEFT.

edges.label: charged-current operator sector
edges.detail: Fermi four-fermion interactions are leading weak-operator components within the broader low-energy effective field theory.

edges.label: local conservation form
edges.detail: A local conservation law is expressed by a continuity equation for a density and current.

edges.label: vanishing divergence
edges.detail: On the equations of motion and with the stated symmetry assumptions, a Noether current obeys a local continuity equation.

edges.label: charge conservation
edges.detail: Electric charge conservation requires $\partial_\mu j^\mu=0$, consistently with Maxwell’s equations.

edges.label: connection derivative
edges.detail: Gauge-covariant differentiation is the physical use of a connection on an associated vector bundle.

edges.label: connection ingredient
edges.detail: A gauge connection together with a representation of the gauge group defines the covariant derivative acting on the associated matter field.

edges.label: connection curvature
edges.detail: The gauge field strength is the curvature of the gauge connection.

edges.label: curvature two-form
edges.detail: Gauge field strengths are Lie-algebra-valued curvature two-forms.

edges.label: minimal gauge coupling
edges.detail: Replacing ordinary derivatives by gauge-covariant derivatives generates matter–gauge interaction terms fixed by the representation and coupling.

edges.label: covariant kinetic terms
edges.detail: Standard Model fermion and Higgs kinetic terms use the gauge-covariant derivative and thereby encode gauge interactions.

edges.label: Yang–Mills kinetic term
edges.detail: The Yang–Mills action is constructed from the non-Abelian field strength, whose commutator term produces gauge self-interactions.

edges.label: gauge kinetic terms
edges.detail: The Standard Model Lagrangian contains field-strength kinetic terms for $SU(3)_C$, $SU(2)_L$, and $U(1)_Y$.

edges.label: continuous global symmetry theorem
edges.detail: For spontaneous breaking of a continuous global symmetry under the theorem’s assumptions, Goldstone’s theorem requires gapless modes.

edges.label: gapless mode
edges.detail: Each independent broken global generator gives a Nambu–Goldstone mode subject to relativistic-QFT qualifications.

edges.label: would-be Goldstone degrees
edges.detail: In a gauge-fixed Higgs phase, would-be Goldstone degrees of freedom combine with gauge fields rather than appearing as physical massless particles.

edges.label: reorganized polarization degree
edges.detail: The degrees of freedom represented as would-be Goldstone modes are reorganized into longitudinal polarizations of massive gauge bosons; this is not literal particle consumption.

edges.label: massive-vector polarization
edges.detail: $W^\pm$ bosons have two transverse and one longitudinal physical polarization.

edges.label: massive-vector polarization
edges.detail: The massive $Z$ boson has two transverse and one longitudinal physical polarization.

edges.label: light-quark chiral symmetry
edges.detail: QCD has an approximate light-flavor chiral symmetry when light-quark masses are neglected, with the axial singlet modified by the anomaly.

edges.label: spontaneously broken vacuum
edges.detail: The low-energy QCD vacuum spontaneously breaks the approximate non-singlet chiral symmetry to its vector subgroup.

edges.label: vacuum order parameter
edges.detail: The quark condensate is a conventional order parameter for chiral-symmetry breaking in idealized light-quark limits.

edges.label: light pseudo-Goldstone modes
edges.detail: Spontaneous breaking gives Goldstone modes, while nonzero light-quark masses make the observed light mesons pseudo-Nambu–Goldstone modes.

edges.label: pion multiplet
edges.detail: The pions are the lightest pseudo-Nambu–Goldstone mesons of approximate QCD chiral symmetry.

edges.label: pion low-energy degree
edges.detail: Mesonic chiral perturbation theory describes pions as its principal low-energy degrees of freedom; baryonic variants also include nucleons.

edges.label: symmetry and power counting
edges.detail: Chiral perturbation theory is organized by the approximate chiral symmetry, its spontaneous breaking pattern, momenta, and light-quark masses.

edges.label: approximate internal symmetry
edges.detail: Isospin is an approximate internal $SU(2)$ flavor symmetry.

edges.label: isospin doublet
edges.detail: Proton and neutron form an approximate isospin doublet when electromagnetic effects and the up–down mass difference are neglected.

edges.label: isospin triplet
edges.detail: The charged and neutral pions form an approximate isospin triplet.

edges.label: approximate charge independence
edges.detail: Approximate isospin symmetry organizes nuclear forces and spectra, with breaking from electromagnetism and quark-mass differences.

edges.label: wave solutions
edges.detail: In source-free regions, Maxwell’s equations imply wave equations for the propagating transverse electromagnetic degrees of freedom.

edges.label: propagating field configuration
edges.detail: An electromagnetic wave is a propagating field configuration, not a distinct material constituent.

edges.label: classical radiation field
edges.detail: Classical electromagnetic radiation is represented by outgoing or propagating Maxwell-wave solutions.

edges.label: quantized radiation field
edges.detail: Quantum electromagnetic radiation is represented by states of the photon field, including number states, wave packets, thermal states, and coherent states.

edges.label: photon excitation content
edges.detail: Definite-number radiation states contain photon excitations; classical coherent radiation generally has no definite photon number.

edges.label: emitted photon
edges.detail: An ordinary allowed one-photon radiative atomic decay produces a photon together with atomic recoil and finite linewidth; higher-order channels can emit two or more photons.

edges.label: additional photon in driven mode
edges.detail: Stimulated emission increases the occupation of the coupled radiation mode; an exact photon-number statement depends on the field state.

edges.label: absorbed radiation quantum
edges.detail: In a single-photon absorption channel, the material system removes one photon while gaining its energy and momentum, subject to selection rules; multiphoton absorption is a distinct higher-order process.

edges.label: rest-frame energy and invariant mass
edges.detail: Special relativity identifies invariant mass with total rest-frame energy divided by $c^2$.

edges.label: binding changes composite mass
edges.detail: Negative binding energy relative to separated constituents reduces the invariant mass of the bound system by the corresponding energy divided by $c^2$.

edges.label: nuclear separation energy
edges.detail: Nuclear binding energy is the binding energy relative to specified separated nucleons or nuclear fragments.

edges.label: atomic breakup threshold
edges.detail: An atom’s electronic binding energy is defined relative to a specified ionization or dissociation threshold.

edges.label: electron separation energy
edges.detail: Ionization energy is an electron-separation binding energy for a specified atom or ion.

edges.label: first ionization threshold
edges.detail: A neutral atom has a first ionization energy defined by the minimum ground-state electron-removal channel.

edges.label: threshold energy
edges.detail: The ionization energy sets the lowest energetic threshold for the specified ionization process.

edges.label: minimum-energy state
edges.detail: A ground state is a quantum state of minimum energy in a specified Hamiltonian sector.

edges.label: above-ground state
edges.detail: An excited state is a quantum state above the ground-state energy of the specified system.

edges.label: atomic ground state
edges.detail: Each stable atomic species and charge state has a lowest-energy state within the chosen Hamiltonian and sector.

edges.label: atomic excited states
edges.detail: Atoms possess excited bound, metastable, resonant, and continuum states above the ground state.

edges.label: radiative de-excitation
edges.detail: An excited atomic state with an allowed radiative channel may decay by spontaneous emission; metastability and nonradiative channels depend on selection rules and environment.

edges.label: discrete symmetry label
edges.detail: Parity is a discrete quantum number when spatial inversion commutes with the relevant Hamiltonian.

edges.label: atomic-state parity
edges.detail: Atomic configurations and levels are labeled by even or odd parity when inversion symmetry applies.

edges.label: nuclear-state parity
edges.detail: Nuclear states are conventionally labeled by total spin and parity.

edges.label: parity selection rule
edges.detail: The parity of initial, final, and transition-operator states constrains allowed multipole transitions.

edges.label: electron repulsion term
edges.detail: Pairwise electron–electron Coulomb repulsion is an explicit term of the leading many-electron Hamiltonian.

edges.label: electron–nucleus attraction term
edges.detail: Electron–nucleus Coulomb attraction, using a point or finite charge distribution as appropriate, is the principal binding term of the leading atomic Hamiltonian.

edges.label: Hamiltonian spectral values
edges.detail: Bound atomic energy levels are discrete spectral values of the atomic Hamiltonian, while ionization and scattering channels contribute continuous spectrum.

edges.label: expected nonperturbative gap
edges.detail: Pure confining four-dimensional quantum Yang–Mills theory is expected to have a positive spectral gap above the vacuum; rigorous continuum construction and proof remain open.

edges.label: noncommutative product difference
edges.detail: Whenever both products are defined on a suitable common domain, operator composition defines the commutator $AB-BA$.

edges.label: symmetrized product
edges.detail: Whenever both products are defined, operator composition defines the anticommutator $AB+BA$.

edges.label: indexed direct sum
edges.detail: An indexed family of vector spaces has a direct sum characterized by finitely supported components and the coproduct universal property.

edges.label: graded direct-sum structure
edges.detail: Fock space is a Hilbert direct sum of zero-, one-, and many-particle tensor-power sectors.

edges.label: canonical operator bracket
edges.detail: Canonical commutation relations are equations for operator commutators, such as $[Q_i,P_j]=i\hbar\delta_{ij}$.

edges.label: canonical anticommutation algebra
edges.detail: Fermionic creation, annihilation, and field operators satisfy canonical anticommutation rather than commutation relations.

edges.label: state functional
edges.detail: A quantum state assigns expectation values to observables; in operator formulations this assignment is a positive normalized functional.

edges.label: observable argument
edges.detail: An expectation value is evaluated for a specified observable in a specified state.

edges.label: trace formula
edges.detail: For a density operator $\rho$, the expectation of $A$ is $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho A)$ whenever the product and trace are defined.

edges.label: pure-state quadratic form
edges.detail: Pure-state expectations use the Hilbert-space inner product $\langle\psi,A\psi\rangle$.

edges.label: weak-interaction flavor basis
edges.detail: Electron-, muon-, and tau-neutrino states are flavor-basis states of the neutrino sector.

edges.label: propagation mass basis
edges.detail:
The observed light neutrino sector contains three propagating mass eigenstates, conventionally labeled $
u_1,
u_2,
u_3$.

edges.label: electron flavor
edges.detail: The electron neutrino is the flavor state coupled to the electron charged-current channel.

edges.label: muon flavor
edges.detail: The muon neutrino is the flavor state coupled to the muon charged-current channel.

edges.label: tau flavor
edges.detail: The tau neutrino is the flavor state coupled to the tau charged-current channel.

edges.label: charge-conjugate weak-interaction channel
edges.detail: Antineutrino denotes the charge-conjugate weak-interaction state or channel; whether it is a distinct particle from the neutrino depends on the unresolved Dirac-versus-Majorana question.

edges.label: electron antineutrino flavor
edges.detail: The electron antineutrino is associated with the charge-conjugate electron charged-current channel.

edges.label: muon antineutrino flavor
edges.detail: The muon antineutrino is associated with the charge-conjugate muon charged-current channel.

edges.label: tau antineutrino flavor
edges.detail: The tau antineutrino is associated with the charge-conjugate tau charged-current channel.

edges.label: weak-interaction basis
edges.detail: Neutrino mixing relates the charged-current flavor basis to the propagation mass basis.

edges.label: propagation basis
edges.detail: Neutrino mixing relates mass eigenstates to flavor states through the PMNS matrix.

edges.label: relative propagation phases
edges.detail: Different mass eigenstates acquire different propagation phases; their coherent interference changes flavor-detection probabilities.

edges.label: up/down quark-field degrees of freedom
edges.detail: The proton is a QCD bound state whose quark-field content has net valence flavor $uud$ together with sea-quark and antiquark excitations.

edges.label: up/down quark-field degrees of freedom
edges.detail: The neutron is a QCD bound state whose quark-field content has net valence flavor $udd$ together with sea-quark and antiquark excitations.

edges.label: spectrum of a self-adjoint operator
edges.detail: A possibly unbounded self-adjoint operator is closed and densely defined, so its resolvent and spectrum are well-defined; its spectrum is real.

edges.label: elementary quark species
edges.detail: In the Standard Model, quarks are elementary spin-$1/2$ particle species.

edges.label: elementary lepton species
edges.detail: In the Standard Model, charged leptons and neutrinos are elementary spin-$1/2$ particle species.

edges.label: elementary gauge bosons
edges.detail: The Standard Model gauge bosons are elementary field quanta.

edges.label: elementary Higgs boson
edges.detail: The Standard Model Higgs boson is the elementary scalar excitation of the Higgs field.

edges.label: electron antiparticle
edges.detail: The positron is the electron antiparticle.

edges.label: proton antiparticle
edges.detail: The antiproton is the proton antiparticle and has baryon number $-1$.

edges.label: neutron antiparticle
edges.detail: The antineutron is the neutron antiparticle and has baryon number $-1$.

edges.label: quark antiparticle class
edges.detail: Each quark flavor has a corresponding antiquark in the conjugate color representation.

edges.label: quantitative accelerated motion
edges.detail: Galileo’s measured laws of falling and inertial motion formed part of the empirical and mathematical background from which Newtonian mechanics was constructed.

edges.label: optical interference
edges.detail: Young’s fringes helped establish wave optics, later incorporated into the electromagnetic-wave theory of light.

edges.label: electric current affects magnetism
edges.detail: Ørsted’s result showed that electricity and magnetism were dynamically connected and launched the experimental program culminating in classical electromagnetism.

edges.label: field lines and induction
edges.detail: Faraday’s induction and field-line experiments supplied the physical concepts that Maxwell recast into field equations.

edges.label: induction law
edges.detail: Maxwell’s equations incorporated and generalized Faraday’s empirical induction law.

edges.label: moving-medium light speed
edges.detail: Fizeau’s result became an important constraint on ether theories and was naturally recovered by relativistic velocity addition; it was one historical input among several, not a unique origin of special relativity.

edges.label: unexplained perihelion advance
edges.detail: Einstein used the residual Mercury precession as a decisive target while developing general relativity and reproduced it in 1915.

edges.label: ether-drift null result
edges.detail: The null result undermined simple stationary-ether models and became part of the experimental setting in which Lorentz invariance and special relativity were accepted; direct influence on Einstein’s 1905 reasoning remains historically uncertain.

edges.label: regular hydrogen line series
edges.detail: Balmer’s empirical pattern was generalized by Rydberg’s spectral formula.

edges.label: discrete hydrogen spectrum
edges.detail: The need to explain Balmer and Rydberg lines was a central target of Bohr’s quantized atomic model.

edges.label: failure of classical equipartition
edges.detail: Planck’s quantized energy elements solved the blackbody problem and initiated the quantum developments that culminated in quantum mechanics.

edges.label: frequency-dependent photoemission
edges.detail: The photoelectric effect was a central anomaly motivating quantum descriptions of radiation and matter.

edges.label: light quanta
edges.detail: Einstein’s light-quantum explanation accounted for the threshold and energy relation and helped establish the photon concept.

edges.label: large-angle alpha scattering
edges.detail: The unexpected backscattering required a compact concentration of positive charge and led to the nuclear atom.

edges.label: nuclear atom model
edges.detail: Rutherford’s atomic model was formulated specifically to explain the Geiger–Marsden angular distribution.

edges.label: two-valued beam splitting
edges.detail: The later reinterpretation of the silver-atom splitting made the experiment a central empirical motivation and illustration for intrinsic spin.

edges.label: unexplained magnetic multiplets
edges.detail: The anomalous Zeeman patterns were a major empirical clue that orbital angular momentum alone was insufficient and helped motivate the introduction of electron spin.

edges.label: nonclassical separated correlations
edges.detail: The EPR argument isolated the conceptual stakes of entangled correlations and made them a central foundational problem.

edges.label: experimental discrimination of local hidden-variable models
edges.detail: EPR’s locality and completeness challenge motivated Bell’s theorem and the subsequent experimental test programs.

edges.label: precision bound-state discrepancy
edges.detail: The discrepancy forced renewed scrutiny of bound-state QED, recoil, spectroscopy, and systematic effects.

edges.label: proton charge-radius sensitivity
edges.detail: The puzzle highlighted how nuclear charge distributions shift atomic levels, especially in muonic hydrogen.

edges.label: missing energy and momentum
edges.detail: Pauli proposed the neutrino to preserve conservation laws in continuous beta decay.

edges.label: quantitative beta-decay dynamics
edges.detail: Fermi’s interaction theory incorporated the neutrino and supplied a dynamical account of beta spectra.

edges.label: CP violation in weak decays
edges.detail: The observed CP violation demanded a weak-interaction mechanism; the three-generation CKM framework supplied one within the Standard Model.

edges.label: flavor-changing weak phases
edges.detail: Kaon CP violation motivated the search for a complex quark-mixing structure.

edges.label: missing electron-neutrino flux
edges.detail: The persistent deficit motivated oscillation and flavor-conversion explanations later tested by Super-Kamiokande and SNO.

edges.label: pointlike nucleon constituents
edges.detail: Scaling and hard scattering made quark-like partons empirically unavoidable and transformed quarks from a classification device into physical constituents.

edges.label: recurring enhanced stability
edges.detail: Magic-number patterns motivated an independent-particle shell structure with strong spin–orbit splitting.

edges.label: laboratory gravitation
edges.detail: The measured attraction between laboratory masses quantitatively supported universal Newtonian gravitation and permitted later extraction of $G$.

edges.label: generated and detected electromagnetic waves
edges.detail: Hertz observed reflection, interference, polarization, and finite-speed propagation consistent with Maxwellian electromagnetic waves.

edges.label: radio-wave realization
edges.detail: The experiments established electromagnetic radiation as a physical field phenomenon.

edges.label: composition-independent free fall
edges.detail: The torsion balances found no differential acceleration at their sensitivity, strongly supporting the weak equivalence principle.

edges.label: solar light deflection
edges.detail: The measured deflection was interpreted as supporting the relativistic prediction; later experiments provide much higher precision.

edges.label: boost invariance with unequal paths
edges.detail: The null result constrained velocity-dependent light propagation and supported Lorentz-Einstein transformations.

edges.label: relativistic time dilation
edges.detail: The measured Doppler shift included the transverse second-order term predicted by special relativity.

edges.label: gravitational frequency shift
edges.detail: The measured gamma-ray shift agreed with the weak-field gravitational-redshift prediction.

edges.label: local gravitational redshift
edges.detail: The result is consistent with the equivalence-principle connection between acceleration and gravitational frequency shifts.

edges.label: gravitational signal delay
edges.detail: Radar ranging measured the additional delay predicted for propagation through curved spacetime near the Sun.

edges.label: radiative orbital decay
edges.detail: The observed orbital-period decrease agrees with general-relativistic gravitational-wave energy loss.

edges.label: strong-field binary-merger waveform
edges.detail: The signal’s inspiral, merger, and ringdown were consistent with numerical general-relativistic predictions.

edges.label: universal corpuscle with fixed charge-to-mass ratio
edges.detail: Deflection of cathode rays established a universal negatively charged subatomic particle.

edges.label: charge quantization and elementary charge
edges.detail: Droplet charges clustered at integer multiples of a common unit.

edges.label: electron charge magnitude
edges.detail: Combined with charge-to-mass measurements, the oil-drop result fixed the electron’s charge and mass scale.

edges.label: X-ray frequency tracks nuclear charge
edges.detail: Moseley’s law established atomic number as nuclear charge rather than atomic-weight order.

edges.label: element identity by atomic number
edges.detail: Characteristic X-ray spectra tied chemical identity to integer atomic number.

edges.label: same element, distinct masses
edges.detail: Mass spectrograph peaks directly separated isotopes of the same chemical element.

edges.label: mass-resolved nuclear species
edges.detail: The measurements supplied mass-to-charge identification of nuclear species.

edges.label: noninteger masses and packing fraction
edges.detail: Precision isotope masses revealed systematic departures from integer mass multiples associated with nuclear binding.

edges.label: discrete excitation thresholds
edges.detail: Repeated inelastic thresholds directly supported discrete atomic excitation energies.

edges.label: quantized atomic excitations
edges.detail: The threshold spacing agreed qualitatively with the quantized-level picture central to the Bohr model.

edges.label: discrete angular-momentum outcomes
edges.detail: Modern quantum mechanics accounts for the two-valued spin measurement of the silver valence electron.

edges.label: photon momentum transfer
edges.detail: The wavelength shift follows energy–momentum conservation for photons scattering from electrons.

edges.label: quantized radiation–matter scattering
edges.detail: The result supported quantum kinematics beyond classical wave scattering.

edges.label: electron diffraction
edges.detail: The diffraction peaks agreed with de Broglie wavelengths and quantum wave mechanics.

edges.label: matter-wave amplitude
edges.detail: Electron diffraction is described by coherent wave amplitudes associated with the electron state.

edges.label: path-amplitude interference
edges.detail: Individual particles produce an interference distribution only when alternatives remain coherent.

edges.label: probabilistic detection distribution
edges.detail: Accumulated detection frequencies follow the squared-amplitude interference pattern.

edges.label: interference of quantum amplitudes
edges.detail: The experiments directly display the predictive role of a coherent state amplitude without implying a classical trajectory through both slits.

edges.label: Bell-inequality-violating correlations
edges.detail: Observed correlations agree with quantum entanglement and exclude tested local hidden-variable bounds.

edges.label: nonclassical correlation predictions
edges.detail: Successive Bell tests, including loophole-reduced and loophole-free implementations, support quantum predictions.

edges.label: flux-dependent quantum phase
edges.detail: The phase shift agrees with quantum minimal coupling and cannot be represented solely by the local magnetic field along the particle paths.

edges.label: gauge-invariant loop phase
edges.detail: The measured phase depends on enclosed flux, represented by a Wilson-loop or line-integral phase of the potential.

edges.label: $2S_{1/2}$–$2P_{1/2}$ splitting
edges.detail: The experiment directly established the level splitting now called the Lamb shift.

edges.label: radiative bound-state correction
edges.detail: Renormalized QED quantitatively accounts for the shift through self-energy, vacuum-polarization, recoil, and related corrections.

edges.label: precision hydrogen radiative shift
edges.detail: The observed splitting is a foundational benchmark for atomic QED corrections.

edges.label: electron magnetic anomaly
edges.detail: The measured anomaly agrees with perturbative QED at extraordinary precision when an independent fine-structure constant is used.

edges.label: precision coupling determination
edges.detail: The anomaly measurement and QED series provide a leading determination and consistency test of $\alpha$.

edges.label: boundary-dependent electromagnetic force
edges.detail: Measured forces agree with QED calculations after geometry, conductivity, temperature, roughness, and electrostatic backgrounds are modeled.

edges.label: measured coherence-loss rate
edges.detail: The observed decay of interference and cat-state coherence followed environment-coupling predictions.

edges.label: two-boson bunching
edges.detail: Indistinguishable photons exhibit the exchange interference expected for bosons.

edges.label: indistinguishability interference
edges.detail: The coincidence dip depends on erasing distinguishing information between the two photons.

edges.label: interference of composite molecules
edges.detail: The molecular beam formed fringes requiring coherent center-of-mass amplitudes.

edges.label: environment-dependent visibility
edges.detail: Controlled thermal and collisional coupling quantitatively suppresses molecular interference.

edges.label: positive-energy antiparticle realization
edges.detail: The positron supplied empirical support for the antiparticle sector implied by relativistic electron theory.

edges.label: positive electron track
edges.detail: Curvature and ionization identified a particle with electron mass and opposite charge.

edges.label: first identified antiparticle
edges.detail: The positron established that particle species can have conjugate antiparticles.

edges.label: neutral nucleon
edges.detail: Recoil kinematics required a neutral particle with mass close to the proton mass.

edges.label: new penetrating charged particle
edges.detail: Cloud-chamber curvature and range established a new lepton species.

edges.label: pion track and decay chain
edges.detail: Emulsion tracks distinguished the pion and its decay to a muon.

edges.label: inverse-beta detection
edges.detail: Delayed coincidence signatures provided direct evidence for reactor antineutrinos.

edges.label: reactor antineutrino detection
edges.detail: The detected inverse-beta process identified the electron-antineutrino flavor associated with beta decay.

edges.label: parity violation in beta decay
edges.detail: The asymmetric electron distribution showed that weak interactions are not invariant under spatial inversion.

edges.label: negative neutrino helicity
edges.detail: The polarization correlation supported left-handed neutrinos in the ultrarelativistic weak interaction.

edges.label: neutrino helicity sign
edges.detail: The experiment determined the emitted neutrino’s helicity to be negative within its assumptions.

edges.label: distinct neutrino flavor
edges.detail: Muon production without corresponding electron production established a neutrino flavor associated with muons.

edges.label: neutrino neutral-current events
edges.detail: Events without outgoing charged leptons established neutral-current weak scattering.

edges.label: predicted neutral weak current
edges.detail: The discovery was a major early confirmation of electroweak gauge theory.

edges.label: partonic scaling and later scaling violations
edges.detail: Deep-inelastic data underpin the QCD description of nucleon structure; exact scaling is modified by QCD evolution.

edges.label: charmonium resonance
edges.detail: The $J/\psi$ spectrum established a charm–anticharm bound state and the charm flavor.

edges.label: third charged lepton
edges.detail: Event topologies and missing energy established the tau as a new charged lepton.

edges.label: third lepton family member
edges.detail: The tau supplied the charged-lepton component of a third fermion generation.

edges.label: bottomonium resonance
edges.detail: The upsilon family established a new heavy quark flavor.

edges.label: hard gluon radiation
edges.detail: Three-jet angular and energy distributions supported a spin-one gluon radiated from quarks.

edges.label: QCD jet topology
edges.detail: The observed three-jet events matched QCD predictions for quark–antiquark–gluon final states.

edges.label: predicted weak gauge bosons
edges.detail: The measured masses and decay signatures confirmed the massive electroweak gauge-boson sector.

edges.label: charged weak boson discovery
edges.detail: Leptonic missing-energy events established charged $W$ production.

edges.label: neutral weak boson discovery
edges.detail: Dilepton resonances established the neutral $Z$ boson.

edges.label: precision radiative-consistency tests
edges.detail: LEP observables agreed with loop-corrected Standard Model predictions and constrained the number of light active neutrinos.

edges.label: $Z$-pole and electroweak observables
edges.detail: Precision measurements confirmed the detailed electroweak coupling structure.

edges.label: third-generation up-type quark
edges.detail: Reconstructed events established a quark with the charge and decay modes expected for the top.

edges.label: predicted third-generation partner
edges.detail: Discovery completed the quark content required by the established third-generation electroweak doublet.

edges.label: atmospheric flavor disappearance
edges.detail: The zenith and energy dependence agreed with oscillation of muon neutrinos.

edges.label: lepton mixing parameters
edges.detail: The data constrain mixing and mass-squared differences represented in the PMNS framework.

edges.label: solar flavor conversion
edges.detail: The total active-neutrino flux agreed with solar predictions while the electron-neutrino component was depleted.

edges.label: solar mixing
edges.detail: The flavor-resolved result supports lepton mixing described by the PMNS matrix.

edges.label: new spin-zero boson near $125\,\mathrm{GeV}$
edges.detail: Observed production and decay channels established a Higgs-like scalar boson.

edges.label: Higgs-field excitation
edges.detail: The boson and its measured couplings strongly support the Brout–Englert–Higgs mechanism, while ongoing measurements test its exact Standard Model form.

edges.label: completion of predicted elementary field content
edges.detail: The discovery supplied the previously missing scalar excitation of the minimal Standard Model.

edges.label: quantitative atomic theory
edges.detail: Agreement among Brownian-motion measurements of molecular scales and Avogadro’s number provided strong evidence that atoms and molecules are physical constituents rather than merely calculational devices.

edges.label: hydrogen nucleus emitted from nitrogen
edges.detail: The transmutation experiment established the hydrogen nucleus as a recurring nuclear constituent identified with the proton.

edges.label: require no elements
edges.detail: Select the unique set having no elements.

edges.label: form all subsets
edges.detail: Send $X$ to $\mathcal P(X)$, the set of all subsets of $X$.

edges.label: strictly larger than its base
edges.detail: Cantor’s diagonal argument proves that $|X|<|\mathcal P(X)|$ for every set $X$.

edges.label: chosen as zero
edges.detail: The von Neumann convention uses the empty set as the set-theoretic representative of the abstract numeral $0$.

edges.label: apply successor
edges.detail: Applying $S(x)=x\cup\{x\}$ to $0$ gives $1=\{0\}$.

edges.label: $S(0)=1$
edges.detail: The successor operation sends $0=\varnothing$ to $1=\{\varnothing\}$.

edges.label: iterate from zero
edges.detail: Finite iteration of von Neumann successor from $0$ produces exactly the finite ordinals.

edges.label: require ordinal form
edges.detail: Select the finite sets that are transitive and well-ordered by membership; these are the finite von Neumann ordinals.

edges.label: finite ordinals
edges.detail: Finite ordinals are the finite members of the ordinal hierarchy.

edges.label: successor ordinals
edges.detail: Successor ordinals are ordinals of the form $\alpha+1$.

edges.label: limit ordinals
edges.detail: Limit ordinals are the nonzero ordinals with no immediate predecessor.

edges.label: collect all finite ordinals
edges.detail: $\omega$ is the set of all finite ordinals.

edges.label: first limit ordinal
edges.detail: $\omega$ is the least nonzero limit ordinal.

edges.label: first infinite ordinal
edges.detail: $\omega$ is the first infinite member of the ordinal hierarchy.

edges.label: standard carrier of $\mathbb N$
edges.detail: Equip $\omega$ with zero, successor, recursively defined arithmetic, and its membership order to obtain the standard natural-number system.

edges.label: standard Peano system
edges.detail: $\mathbb N$ on carrier $\omega$ is the standard second-order Peano system.

edges.label: initial arithmetic semiring
edges.detail: With its usual operations, $\mathbb N$ is a commutative semiring and is initial among semirings in the standard unital convention.

edges.label: form formal differences
edges.detail: Use $\mathbb N\times\mathbb N$ to represent differences before quotienting.

edges.label: identify equal differences
edges.detail: Quotient by $(a,b)\sim(c,d)$ exactly when $a+d=b+c$; induced operations produce $\mathbb Z$.

edges.label: $n\mapsto[(n,0)]$
edges.detail: The map $n\mapsto[(n,0)]$ is an injective semiring homomorphism into the nonnegative integers.

edges.label: forget the distinguished integer realization
edges.detail: Forgetting the canonical origin of its elements leaves the usual ordered-ring structure.

edges.label: forget order
edges.detail: Forgetting the order leaves an integral domain.

edges.label: form nonzero-denominator fractions
edges.detail: Use integer numerator–denominator pairs with nonzero denominator before quotienting.

edges.label: identify equal fractions
edges.detail: Quotient by $(a,b)\sim(c,d)$ exactly when $ad=bc$; induced operations produce the fraction field $\mathbb Q$.

edges.label: $z\mapsto z/1$
edges.detail: The map $z\mapsto[(z,1)]$ embeds $\mathbb Z$ canonically into its field of fractions.

edges.label: forget the distinguished rational realization
edges.detail: Forgetting how elements were constructed leaves the usual ordered-field structure.

edges.label: prime ordered field
edges.detail: The rational numbers form the characteristic-zero prime field, equipped here with their canonical order.

edges.label: form Dedekind cuts
edges.detail: Construct an order-complete field from proper lower cuts of $\mathbb Q$.

edges.label: form Cauchy sequences
edges.detail: Take rational Cauchy sequences in the absolute-value metric.

edges.label: identify null differences
edges.detail: Quotient Cauchy sequences by equality of limiting difference zero to obtain a complete ordered field representing $\mathbb R$.

edges.label: Dedekind realization
edges.detail: The Dedekind-cut field is canonically order-isomorphic to the abstract complete Archimedean ordered field $\mathbb R$.

edges.label: constant cut / constant sequence
edges.detail: Each rational has a canonical image in either completion, giving the standard embedding $\mathbb Q\hookrightarrow\mathbb R$.

edges.label: forget completeness
edges.detail: Forgetting completeness and the distinguished real realization leaves an ordered field.

edges.label: forget completeness and topology
edges.detail: The real numbers are real closed; forgetting their completeness and topology retains that algebraic ordered-field property.

edges.label: forget order completeness
edges.detail: The usual topology and field operations make $\mathbb R$ a topological field.

edges.label: form $\mathbb R^2$ with complex multiplication
edges.detail: Equip ordered pairs of reals with the standard complex field operations.

edges.label: adjoin a root of $x^2+1$
edges.detail: Form $\mathbb R[x]/(x^2+1)$, in which the class of $x$ squares to $-1$.

edges.label: ordered-pair realization
edges.detail: Identify $(a,b)$ with $a+bi$ to obtain the standard complex field.

edges.label: polynomial-quotient realization
edges.detail: Identify the residue class of $x$ with $i$; the quotient is isomorphic to the ordered-pair complex field.

edges.label: $a\mapsto a+0i$
edges.detail: The map $a\mapsto(a,0)$ embeds $\mathbb R$ canonically as the real axis in $\mathbb C$.

edges.label: forget topology and distinguished real subfield
edges.detail: The fundamental theorem of algebra says the complex field is algebraically closed.

edges.label: forget algebraic closure
edges.detail: The Euclidean topology and field operations make $\mathbb C$ a topological field.

edges.label: define transfinite operations
edges.detail: Define addition, multiplication, and exponentiation recursively on ordinal arguments.

edges.label: well-founded recursion
edges.detail: The well-ordering of every ordinal supports unique definitions from earlier stages.

edges.label: countable ordinals
edges.detail: Countable ordinals are the ordinals admitting an injection into $\omega$.

edges.label: collect all countable ordinals
edges.detail: $\omega_1$ is the set of all countable ordinals.

edges.label: first uncountable ordinal
edges.detail: $\omega_1$ is the least uncountable member of the ordinal hierarchy.

edges.label: least fixed point of $\omega^\alpha$
edges.detail: Iterating $\alpha\mapsto\omega^\alpha$ from finite stages and taking the supremum yields $\varepsilon_0$.

edges.label: distinguished countable ordinal
edges.detail: $\varepsilon_0$ is a countable ordinal.

edges.label: collect as a proper class
edges.detail: The ordinals form a proper class rather than a set.

edges.label: finite cardinals
edges.detail: Finite cardinals are the finite initial ordinals.

edges.label: infinite cardinals
edges.detail: Infinite cardinals are the nonfinite initial ordinals.

edges.label: view by cardinality
edges.detail: The same initial ordinal $\omega$ is denoted $\aleph_0$ when regarded as the least infinite cardinal.

edges.label: least infinite cardinal
edges.detail: $\aleph_0$ is the first infinite cardinal.

edges.label: least member
edges.detail: $\aleph_0$ is the least infinite cardinal.

edges.label: cardinality $\aleph_0$
edges.detail: The carrier of $\mathbb N$ is countably infinite and has cardinality $\aleph_0$.

edges.label: countably infinite
edges.detail: $\mathbb Z$ is countably infinite.

edges.label: countably infinite
edges.detail: $\mathbb Q$ is countably infinite.

edges.label: take least larger cardinal
edges.detail: For each cardinal $\kappa$, well-order the cardinals above it and take the least one, denoted $\kappa^+$.

edges.label: limit cardinals
edges.detail: Limit cardinals are infinite cardinals that are not successors.

edges.label: transfinite successor enumeration
edges.detail: Starting from $\aleph_0$, take successor cardinals and suprema at limit stages.

edges.label: successor stages
edges.detail: $\aleph_{\alpha+1}$ is the successor cardinal of $\aleph_\alpha$.

edges.label: limit stages
edges.detail: At limit indices, the aleph hierarchy takes the supremum of earlier alephs.

edges.label: start at $\beth_0$
edges.detail: Set $\beth_0=\aleph_0$ and iterate cardinal exponentiation by $2$.

edges.label: power-set successor stages
edges.detail: In ZFC, the step $\beth_{\alpha+1}=2^{\beth_\alpha}$ records the initial-ordinal cardinality of a power set.

edges.label: strict growth at successors
edges.detail: Cantor’s theorem ensures $\beth_\alpha<\beth_{\alpha+1}$.

edges.label: first power-set step
edges.detail: $\mathfrak c=\beth_1=2^{\aleph_0}$.

edges.label: cardinality $\mathfrak c$
edges.detail: The real line has cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$, denoted $\mathfrak c$.

edges.label: $|\mathcal P(\mathbb N)|=\mathfrak c$
edges.detail: Binary sequences, subsets of $\mathbb N$, and real numbers have the same cardinality.

edges.label: $\mathfrak c=\aleph_1$
edges.detail: CH identifies the continuum cardinal with the first uncountable cardinal.

edges.label: specialize to $\aleph_0$
edges.detail: Taking $\kappa=\aleph_0$ in GCH yields CH.

edges.label: $\beth_\alpha=\aleph_\alpha$
edges.detail: GCH identifies the beth and aleph hierarchies at every ordinal index.

edges.label: ZF theory
edges.detail: ZF is a first-order theory in the language with membership as its only nonlogical relation.

edges.label: + axiom of choice
edges.detail: Adjoin AC to ZF; the resulting theory is ZFC.

edges.label: contains AC
edges.detail: The axiom of choice is one of the axioms of ZFC.

edges.label: equivalent over ZF
edges.detail: Over ZF, AC implies that every set can be well-ordered; conversely, the well-ordering theorem implies AC.

edges.label: cardinal representative for every set
edges.detail: A well-order on a set has a unique ordinal order type; its least equipotent ordinal is the set’s cardinal.

edges.label: all set cardinalities are alephs
edges.detail: Choice ensures every set is well-orderable, so every infinite set has cardinality $\aleph_\alpha$ for some ordinal $\alpha$.

edges.label: + strong cardinal property
edges.detail: Select cardinals satisfying additional closure, compactness, measure, or elementary-embedding properties.

edges.label: inaccessible cardinals
edges.detail: Strongly inaccessible cardinals form an early benchmark in the large-cardinal hierarchy.

edges.label: measurable cardinals
edges.detail: Measurable cardinals are a stronger large-cardinal notion defined by a highly complete nonprincipal measure.

edges.label: supercompact cardinals
edges.detail: Supercompact cardinals satisfy compactness properties at every greater scale.

edges.label: measurable implies inaccessible
edges.detail: In ZFC, every measurable cardinal is strongly inaccessible.

edges.label: supercompact implies measurable
edges.detail: Every supercompact cardinal is measurable.

edges.label: no greatest ordinal
edges.detail: For every ordinal $\alpha$, its successor $\alpha+1$ is a strictly larger ordinal; therefore the ordinal hierarchy has no greatest member.

edges.label: equivalent over ZF
edges.detail: Over ZF, well-order every member of a family and choose its least element; thus the well-ordering theorem implies AC.

edges.label: proves existence and uniqueness
edges.detail: ZF proves that a set with no elements exists and extensionality proves that it is unique.

edges.label: power-set axiom
edges.detail: The power-set axiom of ZF asserts that for every set $X$, the collection $\mathcal P(X)$ is a set.

edges.label: ZFC theory
edges.detail: ZFC is a first-order theory in the language of membership, presented by finitely many axioms together with axiom schemas.

edges.label: well-orderable continuum
edges.detail: Choice well-orders $\mathbb R$, so its equipotence type has a unique initial-ordinal representative $\mathfrak c$.

edges.label: well-order power-set sizes
edges.detail: Choice ensures that every power set appearing in the beth recursion has an initial-ordinal cardinal representative.
